speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Good afternoon, and thanks to all of you for joining us today.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're thrilled to report a return to growth and a new June quarter revenue record of $53.8 billion.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We saw significant improvement in year-over-year iPhone performance compared to last quarter, very strong performances for both Mac and iPad, and absolutely blow out quarter for wearables where we had accelerating our growth of well over 50%, and a new high watermark for services where we set an all-time revenue record of $11.5 billion.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: When you step back and consider wearables and services together, two areas where we have strategically invested in the last several years, they now approach the size of a Fortune 50 company.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Geographically, we are happy with our performance across the board including, a return to growth in Mainland China.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We accomplished these results despite strong headwinds from foreign exchange, which impacted our top line growth rate by 300 basis points compared to a year ago.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: That's equivalent to about $1.5 billion of revenue.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Importantly, in constant currency, our revenue grew in all five of our geographic segments.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: For iPhone, we generated $26 billion in revenue.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: While this is down 12% from last year's June quarter, it is a significant improvement to the 17% year-over-year decline in Q2.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We are encouraged by the results we're seeing from the initiatives that we spoke about in January, including strong customer response to our in-store trade-in and financing programs.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In fact, iPhone in our retail and online stores returned to growth on a year-over-year basis in the month of June.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Our active, installed base of iPhone reached a new all-time high and was up year-over-year in each of our top 20 markets, underscoring the quality of our products and the satisfaction and loyalty of iPhone customers around the world.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Revenue excluding iPhone was up 17% from last year with growth across all categories.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Starting with services, we generated all-time record revenue of $11.5 billion, that's up 13% year-over-year and if we exclude the $236 million favorable one-time item from the June quarter last year, services growth was 15%, or 18% in constant currency, which is consistent with our Q2 performance.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Our strong services performance was broad-based.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We set a new all-time records for AppleCare, Music, cloud services, and our App Store search ad business and we achieved a new third quarter revenue record for the App Store.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: What's more, we had double-digit services revenue growth in all five of our geographic segments.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We surpassed 420 million paid subscriptions to services across our platform, and we remain on track to double our fiscal year 16 Services revenue in 2020.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In May, we launched our all-new Apple TV app in over 100 countries, bringing together all the ways to watch TV in a single app across iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, and select smart TVs.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Monthly viewers in the Apple TV app in the United States are up over 40% year-over-year.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We've seen our success being driven here by several factors.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: First, the fact that we have been able to integrate content from over a 150 leading content providers all in one place.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Second, the same ease of use and unmatched user interface that sits Apple apart in other categories sets us apart in TV as well.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And third, we're benefiting from a broader secular move to over-the-top services.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're engaging with the third trend in five ways.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Our Apple TV hardware, Apple TV channels where customers can choose to pay only for the channels they want, our massive library of over a 100,000 iTunes movies and TV shows, the App Store where users can find their favorite streaming services and later this year, our original programming service, Apple TV Plus.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Apple Pay is now completing nearly 1 billion transactions per month, more than twice the volume of the year-ago.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Apple Pay launched in 17 countries in the June quarter, completing our coverage in the European Union and bringing us to a total of 47 markets currently.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Based on June quarter performance, Apple Pay is now adding more new users than PayPal, and monthly transaction volume is growing four times as fast.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In the United States, in addition to a successful integration into Portland's transit system in May, we're beginning the rollout of New York City Transit, and we'll launch in Chicago later this year.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In China, Apple Pay launched the payment card for DiDi, the world's largest ride hailing provider.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: As I've said before, transit integration is a major driver of a broader digital wallet adoption and we're going to keep up this push to help users leave their wallet at home in more and more instances.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: On a related note, thousands of Apple employees are using Apple Card every day in our beta test, and we plan to begin the rollout of Apple Card in August.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: As I mentioned at the outset, it was another sensational quarter for wearables, with growth accelerating to well over 50%.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We had great results for Apple Watch, which set a new June quarter revenue record and is reaching millions of new users.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Over 75% of customers buying Apple Watch in the June quarter were buying their first Apple Watch.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We continue to see phenomenal demand for AirPods, and when you tally up the last four quarters, our Wearables business is now bigger than 60% of the companies in the Fortune 500.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We had great performance from iPad with revenue of over $5 billion and growth driven by iPad Pro, and by strong customer response to the new iPad mini and iPad Air.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: This was our third consecutive quarter of growth and with revenue up 15% year-to-date, we feel great about where we're headed with iPad.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: With our current lineup of iPad, iPad Mini, iPad Air, and iPad Pro, we've got the perfect device for everyone from young learners to professionals.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We were also very happy with double-digit revenue growth from Mac, fueled by a strong performance of MacBook Air and MacBook Pro.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Looking forward, there is an enormous amount to be excited about for Mac.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: On the heels of our Mac Mini and iMac updates earlier in the fiscal year, we brought significant updates to the bulk of our notebook line up in the last couple of months.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We now have a $999 MacBook Air that is killer for college students, and for our pro users who push the limits of what a Mac can do, we were thrilled unveiled the most powerful Mac ever, the new Mac Pro and the all-new Pro display XDR, which will be available this fall.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: They're designed for maximum performance, expansion, and configurability, and at breakthrough pricing, and they are the most powerful tools Apple has ever put in the hands of Pro customers.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: What's more, the Mac ecosystem as a whole is about to get a big boost.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: At our recent Worldwide Developers Conference, we announced a game-changing tool to help developers easily adapt their iOS and iPad iOS apps for the Mac.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: I'll have a bit more to say on that in a moment.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: I'd like to provide some color on our performance in Greater China, where we saw significant improvement compared to the first half of fiscal 2019 and return to growth in constant currency.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We experienced noticeably better year-over-year comparisons for our iPhone business there than we saw in the last two quarters, and we had sequential improvement in the performance of every category.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The combined effects of government stimulus, consumer response to trade-in programs, financing offers, and other sales initiatives, and growing engagement with the broader Apple ecosystem had a positive effect.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We were especially pleased with a double-digit increase in services driven by strong growth from the App Store in China.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Turning to the future.

sentence: Last week, we announced an agreement with Intel to acquire the majority of it smartphone modem business.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: This is our second-largest acquisition by dollars, and our largest ever in terms of staff.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're looking forward to welcoming all of them to Apple.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We see this is a great opportunity to work with some of the leading talents in this field, to grow our portfolio of wireless technology patents to over 7,000, to expedite our development of our future products, and to further our long-term strategy of owning and controlling the primary technologies behind the products that we make.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We also had our best WWDC ever last month, packed with announcements of great new features coming this fall across our four software platforms, making them more powerful, more personal, and more private.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: For iPhone users, iOS 13 will take on a dramatic new look with dark mode, while delivering major updates to the apps you use every day including photos, camera, and maps.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: iOS 13 offers great new ways to help you manage your privacy and security, including sign-on with Apple, which uses Face ID or Touch ID to quickly sign into apps and websites without sharing your personal information.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And improvements across the entire system will make iPhone even faster and more delightful to use than ever before.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: For the first time, iPad is getting its own version of iOS called iPadOS, a strategic step forward that takes the iPad experience to a whole new level.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The redesigned home screen, powerful new multitasking tools, and deeper integration with Apple Pencil take productivity and creativity further, including using your iPad as an extended an interactive second monitor for your Mac.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: For Apple TV, TvOS 13 will make the big screen experience even more personal.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: With a redesigned home screen and multi-user support, everyone in the family can get a more engaging and tailored experience with their favorite TV shows, movies, sports, and news, along with Apple music photos and videos in iCloud, and an App Store with thousands of great games and apps.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: WatchOS 6 is a major step forward in helping Apple Watch users stay healthy, active, and connected.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Apple Watch now has a dedicated App Store that users can access directly from the device, and new watch faces, Siri enhancements, and music and audio features make Apple Watch more useful than ever.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And of course, we continue to innovate on Apple Watch's promise to be an intelligent guardian for your health.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: WatchOS 6 includes powerful new features like notifications that warned about high-decibel noise to protect your hearing, and cycle tracking to aid in women's healthcare decisions.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In the June quarter, we expanded the availability of the ECG app and irregular rhythm notifications to five additional European countries, and added Canada and Singapore just last week, making them available in 31 countries and regions around the world with more to come later this year.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're very proud of the muscle we've built in bringing regulated products like these to market.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: This is an important competency that creates exciting opportunities for us moving forward.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: As I noted earlier, we believe Mac OS Catalina will be a breakthrough in the Mac ecosystem.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: A new tool included in Mac OS Catalina called Mac Catalyst gives developers a major head start in bringing their iOS apps to the Mac.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Thousands of developers are already using it to bring their apps to the Mac ecosystem, and we expect to see a wave the popular apps arriving for the Mac as early as this fall.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Again as we're taking a step back and digesting the bigger picture here, these updates of the latest steps in a broader strategic effort to make the user experience across iOS, Mac OS, iPad OS, Watch OS and TvOS more effort effortless, and more intuitive.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Apple is alone in offering this kind of value and ecosystem to its customers, and these devices and their platforms are unmatched in their ease of use, their seamlessness, and their privacy and security.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And while providing these things, we've created a dynamic environment where a developer benefits benefit greatly from creating for, and distributing on these platforms.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And our customers of course benefit greatly from access to all this creativity and innovation.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We also unveiled other exciting technologies to make it easier and faster for developers to create powerful new apps.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: SwiftUI provides an intuitive new framework for building sophisticated user interfaces across our software platforms using simple, easy to use, code.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Core ML3 supports the acceleration of more types of advanced real-time machine learning models and Create ML lets developers build machine learning models without writing code.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We have the world's largest augmented-reality-enabled platform, and thousands of AR Kit enabled applications in the App Store.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Building on this strategy, and our momentum in this area, we introduced three new AR-based technologies.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: ARKit 3 uses on-device, real-time machine learning to recognize the human form and integrates people seamlessly into AR experiences.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Reality Kit is a new developer framework built from the ground-up to provide all the tools and technologies required to make AR objects virtually life=like.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And Reality Composer brings AR content creation to tens of millions of developers who had no 3-D experience.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Our developers are already running with these new technologies and we think our customers are going to love some of the apps these creators have in store in the months ahead.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: On so many fronts, there is an enormous amount to look forward to over the next few months, including the launch of new services, like Apple Arcade, Apple TV Plus, and Apple Card.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And without giving too much away, we have several new products that we can't wait to share with you.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Until then, thanks for joining us today and for more details on the June quarter results, I'll turn the call over to Luca.

sentence: Our business and financial performance in the December quarter were exceptional as we set new all-time records for revenue, net income and earnings per share.

sentence: Net income was an all-time record at $22.2 billion, up $2.3 billion or 11% over last year.

sentence: Diluted EPS was also an all-time record at $4.99, up 19%, and operating cash flow was a very strong $30.5 billion, an improvement of $3.8 billion over a year ago.

sentence: iPhone revenue of $56 billion grew 8% year-over-year as we saw a great customer response to the launch of our newest iPhones.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We set all-time revenue records in several countries, including the US, Mexico, the UK, France, Spain, Poland, Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam.

sentence: Our active installed base of iPhones has reached an all-time high and is growing in each of our geographic segments.

sentence: In the US, the latest survey of consumers from 451 Research indicates iPhone customer satisfaction of 98% for iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max combined.

sentence: We set an all-time revenue record of $12.7 billion with double-digit growth in all of our five geographic segments.

sentence: As Tim mentioned, we established new all-time records for Apple Music, cloud services, payment services and our App Store search ad business and December quarter records for the App Store and Apple Care.

sentence: We are well on our way to accomplishing our goal of doubling our fiscal year '16 Services revenue during 2020.

sentence: We've actually already reached that goal on a run rate basis with the results of the December quarter.

sentence: Customer engagement in our ecosystem continues to grow and the number of both transacting and paid accounts on our digital content stores reached a new all-time high with paid accounts growing double-digits in all of our geographic segments.

sentence: And so, there was a very small contribution to revenue from the deferral, and there was also contribution to revenue from the people, the subscribers that are actually paying for the service.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: When you think about what goes into the Apple TV+ revenue at this point, there are two components, the paid subscribers.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: These are customers that pay for the service.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And we recognize revenue over the subscription period.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And then, we've got the, what we call, the Apple TV+ bundle subscribers.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: These are the customers that buy an eligible hardware device and redeem the offer for a three-year of TV+ services.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We defer revenue for this offer based on three items.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: The first one is the value of the service that is being provided, the one year of Apple TV+.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: The second one is the number of customers that are eligible for the offer.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And the third one is our estimate of the expected number of customers that we redeem the offer.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So you need to keep in mind that from our total eligible device sales, you need to make a number of reductions for family sharing, for multiple device purchases and for geographic availability.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Also the take rates can also be impacted by the availability of local content, and we also require a payment method on file.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So this estimate is reviewed quarterly and gets updated based on actual trends of the offer.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so, these inputs provide us with the amount of revenue that we defer for each device sale that then gets recognized over the one year period that the TV+ service is provided.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so, when you take the combination of paid subscribers and bundled subscribers, you get the Apple TV+ revenue, of course because we launched the service very recently.

speaker: Luca Maestri

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: With regard to the cost of the service, of developing the content, we -- essentially, as we incur this cost, we put them on the balance sheet and then we amortize them over a certain period of time depending on the type of content that we produce.

sentence: This is something Apple has been contending with since January, and I think that how we have responded, what we have been inspired to do tells an important story about Apple's great durability as a business and the enduring importance of our products and our customers' lives.

sentence: It also speaks to Apple's unmatched capacity to be creative, to think always in terms of the long term, and to forge ahead when others may feel an instinct to pull back.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Before COVID-19 was on the horizon, we anticipated that Q2 was going to be a prolific and energetic period for Apple.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And when the pandemic did strike, our teams not only succeeded in growing the business in introducing powerful new products and in meeting our customers needs, but they also rose to the occasion in terms of meeting our broader obligations to the communities in which we live and work.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Let's look quickly across the business.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: At the same time that they were leaving no stone unturned to get our latest generation of devices manufactured and into our customers' hands, our worldwide network of supply chain partners, logistics and operations folks in every part of the company were also sourcing more than 30 million masks for frontline medical workers, ensuring they're donated to places of greatest need in every region around the world.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: While our product teams were preparing to launch a new iPad Pro, Magic Keyboard, MacBook Air and the new iPhone SE, all of which have been very well received by reviewers and consumers alike, they were also working with our suppliers to design, test, manufacture and distribute more than 7.5 million face shields, and we continue to ship more than 1 million of these every week to the doctors, nurses and medical personnel on the frontlines.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In a quarter, where our Services teams achieved strong growth, which Luca will dig into in a minute and which speaks to the real durability of our services strategy, these teams were also putting COVID-19 front and center.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: As Apple News reached 125 million monthly active users, we elevated trusted information from reliable sources through a special COVID-19 vertical.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We let customers skipped payments without incurring interests on Apple Card for March and April in light of financial hardship for many families.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We worked with everyone from Oprah to Lady Gaga, to inform, entertain and give back through Apple TV.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And services like FaceTime and Messages set new all-time records for daily volume during this quarter as users relied on their devices to stay connected in a new reality.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In software, at the same time that our teams work with great creativity and excitement as we prepare to deliver our first-ever all-online Worldwide Developers Conference later this quarter, they also worked with the same creativity and speed to put together our COVID-19 symptom checking website and app, in partnership with the CDC.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: As of today, the app has been installed nearly 2 million times and the web tool has received over 3 million unique visits.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And just this month, to accelerate contact tracing, we are launching a joint effort with Google to enable to use of Bluetooth technology to help governments and health agencies spread the -- reduce the spread of the virus with user privacy and security central to the design.

sentence: We paired these programmatic efforts with a broader strategy to give back where it's needed most.

sentence: We've made major corporate donations to response efforts around the world to support global citizen, as well as a new fund for Americans experiencing food and security as a result of the crisis.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: When you tally these things up and consider our ongoing two-to-one match for employee donations, Apple's contributions to the global response are significant, diverse and a great source of pride for the whole team.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're also doing what we can to help our employees, their families, and by extension their communities, stay safe and well by modifying our operations where appropriate.

sentence: This extends of course to our retail employees.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: They're Apple's face to our customers and an instrumental part of our business, and we're compensating them normally despite store closures.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: During a quarter where circumstances evolve by the hour, we have been gratified by the resilience and adaptability of our global supply chain.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: While we felt some temporary supply constraints in February, our operations team, suppliers and manufacturing partners have been safely returning to work and production was back at typical levels toward the end of March.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: At this time of social distance, of shuttered schools and gathering places, of delayed plans and new ways of socializing, we have seen significant evidence that our products have taken a renewed importance for our customers.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Teachers and students around the world are relying on our technology to teach, learn and stay connected with each other.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We are in the process of deploying major orders of iPads to school systems working to keep learning going strong at a distance, including tens of thousands in Ontario, Canada, Glasgow, Scotland, and Puerto Rico, 100,000 into the city of Los Angeles, and 350,000 to New York City, our largest educational iPad deployment ever.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Since early March, we've seen unprecedented demand for our Pro Apps from students, enthusiasts and creative professionals.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: These folks are keeping us all entertained and inspired as we stay at home, and to help them do it, we made Final Cut Pro X and Logic Pro X available for free for 90 days for everyone.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And the reaction has been overwhelming driving software downloads and usage to record levels.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And doctors and medical professionals are making even greater use of Apple Watch and other health features to communicate with patients and to treat them safely from a distance when necessary.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: With new FDA guidance on non-invasive remote patient monitoring for example, the ECG app on Apple Watch is increasingly being used to facilitate remote ECG measurements and recordings for telemedicine usage, reducing patient and healthcare provider contact and exposure.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Many hospitals such as Geisinger Health System, NYU Langone Health and Stanford Health Care are using apps on iPad and iPhone to support communication and video conferences between hospitalized patients and their care teams.

sentence: This enables the care teams to keep a close watch on patients without entering isolation rooms, which helps to minimize exposure and reduces some of the need for personal protective equipment.

sentence: Based on Apple's performance during the first five weeks of the quarter, we were confident we were headed toward a record second quarter at the very high end of our expectations.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: This quarter and throughout the year, our response to this crisis has been to ask, how can we help?

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In terms of COVID-19 response, that has meant sourcing and donating millions of face masks, designing and manufacturing millions of face shields and scaling the production of millions of test kits.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: But we have tried to live our values more broadly.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We've pledged $100 million to our new Racial Equity and Justice Initiative.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We've committed to be fully carbon-neutral by 2030 across our entire supply chain and device usage as massive wildfires, hurricanes and floods bring home the consequences of climate change for all of us.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And we've deepened our enduring educational partnerships, from coding education beginning in elementary school to new efforts with dozens of historically black colleges and universities.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: One of the many areas where COVID-19 continues to have a significant impact is in education.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: As teachers, students and parents alike work hard to keep education relevant, creative and effective, our products have helped them meet the moment.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In a typical year, the back-to-school season is a bustling time for us.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: This year, that was true in the biggest way ever.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We've helped school districts around the world meet this moment in an unprecedented way, including starting nine of our 10 largest school district deployments ever that alone will support over 1 million students and teachers.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We have also supported these deployments and educators and learners everywhere with free tools and training, reaching over 150,000 teachers and millions of parents and students around the world.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Looking forward, we feel great optimism about the road in front of us.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're in the midst of our most prolific product introduction period ever.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In addition to the announcement of HomePod mini, which achieves unmatched sound quality and Siri and smart home capabilities in a small and affordable format, we just marked the beginning of a new era for iPhone with the arrival of our first 5G-enabled devices.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The iPhone 12 and 12 mini boast powerful breakthroughs like an edge-to-edge Super Retina XDR display, unprecedented durability with a new Ceramic Shield developed with our partners at Corning, new MagSafe charging and accessories, the fastest-ever A14 Bionic chip and a new dual camera system driven by computational photography.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The iPhone 12 Pro and 12 Pro Max take all of this to an even higher level, driven by the most powerful photo and video tools ever delivered by a smartphone, including an all-new LiDAR scanner and the ability to shoot in Apple ProRaw and full Dolby video.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And of course, all of these devices bring the 5G experience users have been waiting for, with lightning-fast downloads and uploads, a new standard in video streaming, more responsive gaming and much more.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The early product reviews have been tremendously positive, and our customers have been similarly excited to get their hands on this next era of devices.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're very optimistic about what the next few weeks will bring.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We're also seeing a very positive response to our September announcement.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The all-new Apple Watch Series 6 boasts powerful new health and wellness features, including a blood oxygen sensor, a next-generation altimeter and a wide variety of new colors and bands.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The potential for Apple Watch's powerful health and wellness capabilities continues to grow.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Just yesterday, the government of Singapore and Apple launched LumiHealth, a first-of-its-kind program designed to encourage healthy activity and behaviors using Apple Watch.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Created in collaboration with a team of physicians and public health experts, LumiHealth uses technology and behavioral insights to encourage Singaporeans to keep healthy and complete wellness challenges through their Apple Watch and iPhone.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Singapore is a trailblazer here, and we're proud to be their partner.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Our iPad lineup continues to set the pace for the category, including the new iPad Air now shipping with the A14 Bionic, our most powerful chip ever.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We announced Apple Fitness Plus, which delivers deep personalization and integration across the fitness tools our users love and depend on.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And Apple One, launching tomorrow, is the easiest way for users to enjoy Apple services like Music, TV Plus Arcade, iCloud, News Plus and Fitness Plus on a single plan that is right for them and their family.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Looking across services more broadly, we're really excited about what we see.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: This was a record quarter for the App Store, AppleCare, cloud services, Music and payment services.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The App Store, in particular, continues to play an essential role in helping small businesses, educational institutions and workplaces adapt to COVID-19.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Apple TV Plus continues to impress from fan favorites like Ted Lasso, which has won a worldwide audience with its hopeful tone during challenging times, to critical and award praise, including a Primetime Emmy for Billy Crudup in The Morning Show.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Luca will speak in greater detail about our expectations for the December quarter.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Without giving away too much, I can tell you that this year has a few more exciting things in store.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Before I hand things off, I want to offer one more comment on resilience because I think if I had to describe our performance this quarter in a single word, it's resilient.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Financial performance aside, I don't think this year will be a time that any of us look back on with great fondness or nostalgia.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Those of us who wake up every day hoping for a return to normal can count ourselves fortunate.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Others don't have that luxury.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: There is the great pain of a lost loved one, the uncertainty and fear of a lost job, a deep well of concern for people we care about who we are not able to see.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: A sense of opportunities missed, of plans delayed, of time lost.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Even though we are apart, it's been obvious this year that around the company, teams and colleagues have been leaning on and counting on each other more than in normal times.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: I think that instinct, that resilience has been an essential part of how we have navigated this year.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Work can't solve for all the things we're missing right now, but a shared sense of purpose goes a long way.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: A belief that we can do more together than we can alone, that people of goodwill, driven by creativity and passion and that certain itch of a big idea, can still do things that help other people in our own small way to teach, to learn, to create or just to relax at a time like this.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Even as the things we make require us to operate at the very cutting edge of technology, in materials, products and ideas that didn't exist just a few years ago, this year has forced us to face plainly the things that make us human: disease, resilience and hope.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: You never wish for a year like this one, but I couldn't be prouder of the team, the work we have done and the small role we have played in helping our communities find hope and resilience in this time.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: With that, I'll hand things over to Luca.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Good afternoon, everyone.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We're very pleased to report today a new September quarter revenue record, which caps a remarkable level of performance for our fiscal-year 2020, during which we set new all-time records for revenue, earnings per share and free cash flow in spite of an extremely volatile and challenging macro environment.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We could not be more proud of the way our team has innovated and executed throughout this unprecedented period of uncertainty.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We reported total revenue of $64.7 billion for the September quarter, up 1% from a year ago.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: This is a very impressive level of performance when we consider that this year, we did not launch and ship any new iPhone models during the quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Outside of iPhone, we grew 25% in aggregate and had strong double-digit year-over-year revenue growth in each of our product categories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We set all-time records for Mac and services and a September quarter record for wearables, home and accessories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We also achieved new September quarter records in the vast majorities of countries that we track, including, among others, the U.S., Canada, Brazil, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Turkey, Russia, India, Korea, Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Products revenue was $50.1 billion, with very strong underlying performance across each product category.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Our products outside of iPhone grew a combined 30% despite supply constraints on iPad, Mac and Apple Watch throughout the quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: For iPhone, through mid-September, customer demand grew double digits.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As a result of this level of sales performance and the unmatched loyalty of our customers, our installed base of active devices reached an all-time high in aggregate and in each of our major product categories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Our services set an all-time record of $14.5 billion, growing 16% year over year.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We established new all-time records in many services categories and September quarter records in each geographic segment.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: I'll cover this in more detail later.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Company gross margin was 38.2%.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: This was up 20 basis points sequentially due to cost savings and a higher mix of services, partially offset by a different mix of products.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Products gross margin was 29.8%, growing 10 basis points sequentially, driven by cost savings, partially offset by a different mix.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Services gross margin was 66.9%, decreasing 30 basis points sequentially, mainly due to a different mix.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Let me get into more detail for each of our product categories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: iPhone revenue was $26.4 billion as we did not have availability of new iPhone models during the September quarter this year, which we had mentioned during our call in July.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: While COVID-19 and social distancing measures impacted store operations in a significant manner, demand for iPhone remained very strong.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: In fact, through mid-September, customer demand for our current product lineup grew double digits and was well above our expectations.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Our active installed base of iPhones reached a new all-time high, thanks to the exceptional loyalty of our customer base and strength of our ecosystem.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: In fact, in the U.S., the last survey of consumers from 451 Research indicates iPhone customer satisfaction of 98% for iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max combined.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Turning to services, as I said, we set an all-time revenue record of $14.5 billion.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We grew strong double digits and set all-time records in App Store, cloud services, Music, advertising and payment services.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We also set an all-time record in AppleCare as in-store traffic improved and we were able to support more customers.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Our new services, Apple TV Plus Apple Arcade, Apple News Plus and Apple Card, are also contributing to overall services growth and continue to add users, content and features.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: The key drivers for our services growth all continue to be moving in the right direction.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: First, our installed base continues to grow and is an all-time high across each major product category.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Second, the number of both transacting and paid accounts on our digital content stores reached a new all-time high.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: during the September quarter, with paid accounts increasing double digits in each of our geographic segments.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Third, paid subscriptions grew more than 35 million sequentially, and we now have over 585 million paid subscriptions across the services on our platform, up 135 million from just a year ago.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: With this momentum, we are very confident to reach and exceed our increased target of 600 million paid subscriptions before the end of calendar 2020.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Finally, as Tim mentioned, we continue to improve the breadth and the quality of our current services offerings and are adding new service offerings that we think our customers will love, like Apple One and Apple Fitness Plus.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Wearables, home and accessories established a new September quarter record with revenue of $7.9 billion, up 21% year over year.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We set September quarter records in every geographic segment and for each of the three product categories: wearables, home and accessories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As a result, our wearables business is now the size of a Fortune 130 company.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Importantly, Apple Watch continues to extend its reach, with over 75% of the customers purchasing Apple Watch during the quarter being new to the product.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We're very excited about the future of this category, including the recent launches of our new products: Apple Watch Series 6 and SE, HomePod mini and the MagSafe ecosystem of accessories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Next, I'd like to talk about Mac.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Revenue was, by far, an all-time record at $9 billion, up 29% over last year and $1.6 billion above our previous record in spite of supply constraints during the quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We grew strong double digits in each geographic segment and set all-time revenue records in the Americas and rest of Asia Pacific, as well as September quarter records in Europe and Japan.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We have seen amazing customer response to the new MacBook Air and MacBook Pro and very strong demand during the back-to-school season.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: IPad performance was also very impressive with revenue of $6.8 billion, up 46% and our highest September quarter revenue in eight years despite supply constraints.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Demand exceeded our expectations around the world as we grew very strong double digits in every geographic segment, including an all-time record in Japan and a September quarter record in the Americas.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Both Mac and iPad are incredibly relevant products for our customers in the current working and learning environments, and we are delighted that the most recent surveys of consumers from 451 Research measured customer satisfaction at 93% for Mac and 95% for iPad.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: With this level of customer satisfaction and with around half of the customers purchasing Mac and iPad during the quarter being new to that product, it is no surprise that the active installed base for both products reached a new all-time high.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: In the enterprise market, our products are helping companies grow their business while achieving their sustainability goals.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: One example is Vestas, a leading producer of wind turbines.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Vestas is using Apple products and native iOS apps extensively across their operations to deliver renewable energy efficiently to customers worldwide.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: For instance, they use iPads to help -- optimize on-site construction operations, having crane usage, on average, by one day per project.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Vestas' field technicians are using iPhone for work orders, troubleshooting and remote collaboration, saving them 400,000 service hours annually.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: More recently, they have started piloting the augmented reality capability in iPads to help customers visualize wind turbine installations in the field.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Another example of how organizations are using Apple products to reduce carbon impact is digitizing paper workflows.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: In Switzerland alone, Zurich Insurance has reduced paper consumption by over 10,000 sheets per day by equipping 1,000 customer advisors with iPads.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Air Canada is reducing its carbon footprint by over 2,200 metric tons annually by loading flight plans and manuals onto iPads rather than using paper.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We are thrilled that our products are helping businesses run more efficiently and sustainably.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Let me now turn to our cash position.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We ended the quarter with almost $192 billion in cash plus marketable securities.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We issued $5.5 billion of new term debt and decreased short-term borrowing facilities by $6.2 billion during the quarter, leaving us with total debt of $112 billion.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As a result, net cash was $79 billion at the end of the quarter as we continue on our path to reaching a net cash neutral position over time.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We returned nearly $22 billion to shareholders during the September quarter, including $3.5 billion in dividends and equivalents and $18 billion through open market repurchases of 168.7 million Apple shares.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We also retired an additional 3.1 million shares in the final settlement of our 16th ASR.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Before looking ahead, I want to provide just a few highlights for the amazing fiscal year we just completed.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: In fiscal '20, we grew revenue by 6% to $274.5 billion, a new all-time record.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We showed remarkable resilience throughout the year as we were able to grow both revenue and installed base of active devices in every quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: In spite of the most challenging economic environment we can remember, we set new revenue records in the Americas, in Europe and in the rest of Asia Pacific.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We grew our business outside of iPhone by 16%.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We grew earnings per share 10% to a new all-time record.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And most importantly, we continued to deliver innovative products and services that our customers love.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As we move ahead into the December quarter, I'd like to provide some color on what we are seeing, which includes the types of forward-looking information that Tejas referred to at the beginning of the call.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Given the continued uncertainty around the world in the near term, we will not be issuing revenue guidance for the coming quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: However, we are providing some insights on our expectations for the December quarter for our product categories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: These directional comments assume that COVID-related impacts to our business in November and December are similar to what we've seen in October.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We just started shipping iPhone 12 and 12 Pro, and we're off to a great start.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We are also excited to start preorders on iPhone 12 mini and 12 Pro Max next Friday.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Given the tremendously positive response, we expect iPhone revenue to grow during the December quarter despite shipping iPhone 12 and 12 Pro 4 weeks into the quarter and iPhone 12 mini and 12 Pro Max 7 weeks into the quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect all other products in aggregate to grow double digits, and we also expect services to continue to grow double digits.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: For gross margin, we expect it to be similar to our most recent quarters despite the costs associated with the launch of several new products.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: For opex, we expect to be between $10.7 billion and $10.8 billion.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect OI&E to be around $50 million and the tax rate to be around 16%.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Finally, today, our board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.205 per share of common stock payable on November 12, 2020, to shareholders of record as of November 9, 2020.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: With that, let's open the call to questions.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Thank you, Luca.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: We ask you that you limit yourself to two questions.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Operator, may we have the first question, please?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: Thank you very much.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: Tim, can you talk a bit more about China?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: And in terms of linearity, I think, Luca, you'd mentioned that services in all regions were at an all-time high.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: I'm not sure exactly what your comment was.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: But maybe give us a little idea of whether you're seeing any blowback or benefit from the Huawei situation and just dig a bit more into the trends you're seeing in China.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: And then, I have a follow-up.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Thanks, Shannon.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: If you look at China and look at last quarters -- I'll talk about both last quarter and this quarter a bit.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Last quarter, what we saw was our non-iPhone business was up strong double digit for the full quarter.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And then, if you look at iPhone and you look at it in two parts: one, pre-mid-September, which is pre the point at which the previous year we would have launched iPhones, that that period of time, which was the bulk of the quarter, iPhone was growing from a customer demand point of view.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And of course, the -- not shipping new iPhones for the last two weeks of September makes that number in the aggregate a negative.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: But the net is the underlying business in China last quarter was very strong and perhaps very different than you might think from just a quick look at the stated number.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In terms of this quarter, given the explanation for last quarter and the momentum that we've got, and as importantly, given the initial data points that we see on iPhone 12 and iPhone 12 Pro, although we don't guide to revenue, as Luca said, I would tell you that we are confident that we will grow this quarter in China.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so we are very bullish on what's going on there.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: A little more color on last quarter.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We had a much more significant inventory drawdown on the channel side than other regions.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so that is one reason why the numbers are different than other regions.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And additionally, the new products in the year-ago quarter were a higher percentage of our iPhone sales than they were in other regions.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: So hopefully, that explains what's going on in China.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In terms of the market there, 5G is fairly advanced there.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: They're forecasting 600,000 base stations by the end of the year, and so we're entering the market at a very good time.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And with the reception that we've gotten so far, we're very confident there.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: And then, can you talk a bit about just overall in the world -- the cadence that you see sort of for the 5G adoption launch?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: What you see will be sort of the key drivers?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: Obviously, there's a fair amount of subsidies going on in the U.S. at this point.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Yeah, we're working hard to provide the best experience for our iPhone users.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: To do so, we've been collaborating closely with carriers all around the world to ensure iPhone has great throughput and coverage and battery and call quality.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We've completed 5G testing so far on over 100 carriers, in over 30 regions.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so it's pretty pervasive around the world.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: But grantedly, it will continue to roll out in more places as carriers continue to expand their coverage, and this will happen every week.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so it's just going to get better.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: There are obvious places in the world where it's more ahead than in others, but we feel like we are entering at -- sort of at exactly the right time.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Thanks, Shannon.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Can we have the next question, please?

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Operator That will be from Jeriel Ong with Deutsche Bank.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: Yes, thank you so much.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: I guess, I appreciate the guidance for revenues to grow.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: But I guess, my question, perhaps if I could, is relative to seasonality.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: You guys, over the last five years, your seasonality is typically up about 50% quarter on quarter.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: Do you think that you can beat that even with the later release?

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: And I have a follow-up.

sentence: So as I said, Jeriel, we're not providing a range for the reasons that I explained during my prepared remarks.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So you need to keep in mind a couple of things that are unique about this quarter versus the past.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And then, I mentioned again, the launch timing of the phones is different from the past.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So we're launching the new iPhones four weeks into the quarter for two models, for the 12 and the 12 Pro; and seven weeks into the quarter for the other two, the iPhone mini and the 12 Pro Max.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So that is something to keep in mind as you think about the growth rates.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: With regard to all the other product categories, as I said, we are expecting to grow double digits essentially across the board for the rest of our products and for services.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so we are incredibly optimistic about what we are seeing so far.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Obviously, we started taking preorders five days ago, and so it's a bit early for the phone.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: But we think that there are a lot of tailwinds this year for iPhone, for the entire cycle, some of the comments that Tim has already made, right?

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We've got the best lineup of iPhones that we've ever had.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We've got an installed base of iPhone that is very large, continues to grow.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: It's at an all-time high.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Obviously, 5G is a once-in-a-decade opportunity.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And as you've seen in some markets, certainly here in the United States, carrier offers are very aggressive.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so that is very good for consumers and ultimately very good for us.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So very, very optimistic, given what we've seen so far.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: Thank you so much for that context and giving us some of the levers to think about.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: I'd like to ask a little bit more of a strategic one, a little bit longer term in nature.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: I think the one thing that's interesting about the Apple One bundle is the desire to bundle in the first place.

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: I guess, I'm wondering, and some investors have asked me this as well, is that why wouldn't you also take that rationale perhaps to hardware, perhaps maybe AirPods and iPhone or AirPods, Watch and iPhone?

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: Because if it makes sense to bundle services, wouldn't it also make sense to bundle hardware?

speaker: Jeriel Ong
sentence: And if that's not the case, then are there benefits of services bundling that don't necessarily translate to hardware bundling?

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Yes, we don't have anything to announce today on a hardware bundle.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: But backing up a bit, and we do view that people like to pay for their hardware, or at least some substantial portion of it, monthly.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so that's the reason that we have implemented installments in our stores and online.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And that's the reason you see in some of the channels, too, selling a hardware on a per month kind of basis.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: That begins to look like subscription perhaps to some buyers because they're used to holding the phone for X period of time and then turning it over and using the residual value of that phone in a way that gives them a de facto kind of subsidy on a new phone.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so there is something today in the market that works somewhat similar.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: On the services side, we had customers coming to us and asking for an easier way to buy all of our services, and we wanted to provide that, and we're looking forward to tomorrow to getting Apple One out there.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Thank you for the question.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Thank you, Jeriel.

sentence: Can we have the next question, please?

sentence: Operator It will come from Katy Huberty with Morgan Stanley.

sentence: New technologies, including the chips that support 5G, put upward pressure on cost this year, but you managed to leave ASPs for iPhones relatively unchanged this product cycle.

speaker: Katy Huberty
sentence: How should we think about the margin profile of iPhone 12 relative to past iPhone cycles?

sentence: Hi, Katy, obviously, we don't provide any outlook at the gross margin level for product categories.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: What I said in my prepared remarks, we expect gross margins in total for the company to be pretty much in line with what we've seen during the last quarter, which, obviously, as you said, it's very good, right, because we are offering the new phones at price points that are essentially unchanged, and we're taking on a lot of new technology into the phones.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: I would say the commodity environment is good.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: For the first time in many, many quarters, I don't have to say that foreign exchange is a headwind getting into the quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Let me now turn to our cash position.

sentence: We ended the quarter with over 204 billion in cash plus marketable securities.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We issued $14 billion of new term debt and retired 3.5 billion of term debt, leaving us with total debt of almost 122 billion.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As a result, net cash was 83 billion at the end of the quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: This strong position allows us to continue to invest confidently in our future, while also returning value to our shareholders.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We are innovating and investing at an unprecedented pace, including accelerating our investment in the United States with our new commitment to contribute more than 430 billion and 20,000 jobs to the country over the next five years.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As we continue to execute at an extremely high level, we were also able to return nearly 23 billion to shareholders during the March quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: This included 3.4 billion in dividends and equivalents and 19 billion through open market repurchases of 147 million Apple shares.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We continue to believe there is great value in our stock and maintain our target of reaching a net cash neutral position over time.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Given the confidence we have in our business today and into the future, our board has authorized an additional 90 billion for share repurchases.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We're also raising our dividend by 7% to $0.22 per share, and we continue to plan for annual increases in the dividend going forward.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As we move ahead into the June quarter, I'd like to review our outlook, which includes the types of forward-looking information that Tejas referred to at the beginning of the call.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Given the continued uncertainty around the world in the near term, we are not providing revenue guidance, but we are sharing some directional insights assuming that the COVID-related impacts to our business do not worsen from what we are seeing today for the current quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect our June quarter revenue to grow strong double digits year over year.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: However, we believe that the sequential revenue decline from the March quarter to the June quarter will be greater than in prior years for two reasons.

sentence: First, keep in mind that due to the later launch timing and strong demand, iPhone only achieved supply demand balance during the March quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Second, we believe supply constraints will have a revenue impact of 3 to $4 billion in the June quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect gross margin to be between 41.5 and 42.5%.

speaker: Luca Maestri

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect OI&E to be around 50 million and our tax rate to be around 14.5%.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Finally, reflecting the approved 7% dividend increase I just mentioned, today, our board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.22 per share of common stock payable on May 13, 2021, to shareholders of record as of May 10, 2021.

sentence: We ended the quarter with $169 billion in cash and marketable securities.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We repaid $2.8 billion in maturing debt and decreased commercial paper by $1 billion while issuing $5.5 billion of new debt, leaving us with total debt of $120 billion.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As a result, net cash was $49 billion at the end of the quarter as we continue to make progress toward our goal of becoming net cash neutral over time.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As we move ahead into the December quarter, I'd like to review our outlook, which includes the types of forward-looking information that Tejas referred to at the beginning of the call.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Given the continued uncertainty around the world in the near term, we are not providing revenue guidance but we are sharing some directional insights based on the assumption that the macroeconomic outlook and COVID-related impacts to our business do not worsen from what we are projecting today for the current quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Overall, we believe total company year-over-year revenue performance will decelerate during the December quarter as compared to the September quarter for a number of reasons.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: First, we expect nearly 10 percentage points of negative year-over-year impact from foreign exchange.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Second, on Mac, in addition to increasing FX headwinds, we have a very challenging compare against last year, which had the benefit of the launch and associated channel fill of our newly redesigned MacBook Pro with M1.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Therefore, we expect Mac revenue to decline substantially year over year during the December quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Specifically on services, we expect to grow but to be impacted by the macroeconomic environment increasingly affecting foreign exchange, digital advertising and gaming.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect gross margin to be between 42.5% and 43.5%.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect opex to be between $14.7 billion and $14.9 billion.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We expect OI&E to be around negative $300 million, excluding any potential impact from the mark-to-market of minority investments and our tax rate to be around 16.5%.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Finally, today, our board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.23 per share of common stock, payable on November 10, 2022, to shareholders of record as of November 7, 2022.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: With that, let's open the call to questions.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Thank you, Luca.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: We ask that you limit yourself to two questions.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Operator, may we please have the first question?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: Thank you very much.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: It's great to talk to you on the call again.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: I'm wondering, can you just talk a bit about how you're thinking about this iPhone generation?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: On the positive side, you've raised prices.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: It seems to be mixing up.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: On the negative side, investors are concerned about impacted demand from the higher prices, what Huawei meant to you in prior years versus what could happen now.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: There are just some pressures out there.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: So I'm curious if you can talk to what you're seeing initially in iPhone demand and how you think it will move through.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: With the caveat that I understand, things are pretty uncertain out there.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: And then I have a follow-up.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Shannon, it's Tim.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: iPhone grew 10% in the Q4 timeframe to $42.6 billion.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: Customer demand was strong and better than we anticipated that it would be.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And keep in mind that this is on top of a fiscal year of 2021 that had iPhone revenue grow by 39%, and so it's a tough compare as well.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so we were happy with it.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In terms of the new products, the 14 and the 14 Pro and Pro Max, it's still very early.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: But since the beginning, we've been constrained on the 14 Pro and the 14 Pro Max and we continue to be constrained today.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so we're working very hard to fulfill the demand.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: It's difficult to say what the mix will be until we can satisfy the demand because we're not able to determine the accurate mix until then.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: But we're working very hard to do that.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We were really pleased with the broadness of the iPhone strength last quarter.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: We had three of the top four smartphones in the U.S. and the U.K., the top three in Urban China, the top six in Australia, four out of the top five in Germany and the top two in Japan.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And customer satisfaction for the iPhone remains very, very strong at 98%.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so we feel very good about how we performed in Q4.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And certainly, the start of this generation would suggest that we're going to be constrained for a little while on the 14 Pro and 14 Pro Max.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: But we're working very hard to try to remedy that.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: And then, Luca, can you talk a bit about gross margin puts and takes?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: Just how we should think about, I mean, 10 basis points of currency this coming quarter is, I don't want to say unprecedented, but maybe it is.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: So I know you have hedges, but how do we think about it flowing through?

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: And then what other -- components seem to be very favorable.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: But what else should we throw into the mix as we look forward?

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Well, let me start with gross margin in Q4 and then I'll get to Q1.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: It was a September quarter record for the company.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We did 42.3%, and that is in spite of, as you mentioned, very significant negative FX, for example, for Q4, on a sequential basis, FX was negative 70 basis points and on a year-over-year basis it was negative 170 basis points.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Essentially every currency around the world has weakened against the dollar.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Now, we have guided Q1 to 42.5% to 43.5% in spite of the fact that we have, on a year-over-year basis, 330 basis points of negative exchange.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Sequentially, it's 120 basis points unfavorable.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So obviously, the strong dollar makes it difficult in a number of areas.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Obviously, our pricing in emerging markets makes it difficult, and the translation of that revenue back into dollars is affected.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: But on the positive side, we are seeing commodities behave fairly favorably for us.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so we believe we can offset the negative foreign exchange that we're seeing.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And I think that the guidance that we provided reflects that.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: It takes into account, of course, FX.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: It takes into account some level of inflationary pressures.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: But I think the outcome is, I think, is a good one.

speaker: Shannon Cross
sentence: Thank you very much.

speaker: Tejas Gala
sentence: Thanks, Shannon.

speaker: Tim Cook

speaker: Tim Cook

sentence: And so that's the reason iPad contracted during this quarter.

sentence: OK.That's helpful.

speaker: Erik Woodring
sentence: And that's it for me.

sentence: In general, we have a few more days in the quarter that we're going to -- are going to affect both our revenues and our costs.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Not every week is equal because obviously, we have certain peaks during the course of the quarter.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Think about Black Friday or the Christmas holiday.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: But, in general, we're adding a few days of sale and additional opex as well on the cost front.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So that's what happens to us every approximately six years as we need to align our weekly calendar to the fiscal calendar.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We have certain dedicated tools for the manufacturing facilities.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We had some spend around data centers, and we have spent around our office facilities around the world.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We obviously monitor all of them.

speaker: Luca Maestri

speaker: Tim Cook

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And the reviews for the product have just been off the charts in terms of the noise cancellation features and the sound quality.

speaker: Tim Cook

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: In terms of what played the other way, the headwinds, obviously, FX was a headwind that affected wearables, home, and accessories, just like it affected the rest of our products and services.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And we also had effect from the business in Russia, obviously, or the impact there.

speaker: Tim Cook

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The other thing that I should mention is that about two-thirds of the Apple Watches that we sold were to customers that had not previously owned an Apple Watch.

speaker: Tim Cook

speaker: Kyle McNealy

speaker: Kyle McNealy

speaker: Kyle McNealy

speaker: Tim Cook

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: The M2 MacBook Air, the launch of the new product, satisfying the back orders from the previous quarter and then filling the channel, all of those were key contributors.

sentence: Can we have our next question, please?

sentence: Thank you, and it's great to see that you talked about your suppliers going carbon-neutral, something -- a small statement I really took to heart.

sentence: So could it be that services growth was impacted a little bit more by FX and down the road, we could see growth reaccelerate, or am I just reading too much into the FX impact that could be different from services versus product?

sentence: Obviously, the FX impact on our business depends on the geographic mix of the sales that we do.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so yes, it can be -- services and products can have slightly different effects on foreign exchange.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so, if we look at our services business in constant currency, we would have grown double digits.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And so we're very pleased with that.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: As I mentioned, there were some areas that we could see some softness in digital advertising.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Of course, you know that part, and gaming on the App Store was affected.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: But we were very happy with what we saw in terms of the behavior of our customers with the engagement with services.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And I mentioned a number of things during the prepared remarks, the fact that, obviously, that installed base is growing, that's a positive and it's a great foundation for the future.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We are seeing more transacting accounts and more paid accounts, they're both growing double digits.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Paid accounts are growing faster than transacting accounts, so the penetration of paid accounts is increasing.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We have a great subscription business, 900 million paid subs now on the platform and growing very fast.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We doubled in 3 years.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So when we look at all those dynamics, that's the part that is really interesting to us because we really believe that the engine for services growth is there and foreign exchange is a temporary thing and -- but the fundamentals are very good.

sentence: Congratulations for your team.

sentence: Tim, I wanted to ask you about inflation pressures and labor problems here in the U.S. and globally.

sentence: In terms of the people piece, we're focused on taking care of our teams and offering them the best benefits and best compensation so that we can empower them to do the best work of their lives.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And so that's not an all-inclusive list of where we see it, but it gives you some ingredients of where we see inflation pressure.

speaker: Tim Cook
sentence: And we've obviously taken that into consideration in the gross margin guidance that Luca gave earlier in the call.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And on foreign exchange, you're right.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: I mean, it's obviously a very significant factor that is affecting our results, both revenue and gross margin.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: What do we do about situation like this, one where we have a very strong dollar?

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Of course, we hedge our exposures.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: We try to hedge them in as many places as possible around the world.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: For example, I think we've been probably the first company that started hedging our exposure in China several years ago.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: There may be a few currency, small ones, where we don't hedge because the cost is prohibitive or the market is not there.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: But in general, we tend to hedge because it gives us significant level of margin stability.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Obviously, over time, that protection reduces because the hedges roll over and we need to buy new contracts.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: But that's the primary tool that we use to offset some of the FX pressure.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: Of course, when we launch new products, in particular, we look at the FX situation.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And in some cases, for example, customers in international markets had to -- they saw some price increases when we launched the new products, which is not something that, for example, U.S. customers have seen.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And that's unfortunately the situation that we're in right now with the strong dollar.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: So that's the way we try to deal with that.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: I have to say that one of the things that we've really appreciated the most during the quarter was the fact that in spite of this very strong dollar and the difficult FX environment, we have seen very strong performance in many international markets, particularly some very large emerging markets where even in reported currencies, so in U.S. dollars, we're seeing very strong double-digit growth in places like India, Indonesia, Mexico, Vietnam, many places where we've done incredibly well.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And obviously, in local currency, those growth rates are even higher.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: It's important for us to look at how these markets perform in local currency because it really gives us a good sense for the customer response to our products, the engagement with our ecosystem and in general, the strength of the brand.

speaker: Luca Maestri
sentence: And I have to say, in that respect, we feel very, very good about the progress that we're making in a lot of markets around the world.
