sentence: I'm pleased to discuss with you our solid results for the second quarter and how our performance during the first half of 2019 positions us well for the rest of the year and beyond.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: During the quarter, we continued to deliver growth across the three segments of our broad-based business, while also optimizing our portfolio and making progress against long-term strategies.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Revenue and earnings per share were in line with our expectations.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: As expected, we did experience sales deceleration from the first quarter, primarily due to the impact of generic and biosimilar competition in our pharmaceutical business.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Income in the first half of 2019 provides us the opportunity to continue investing to fortify, accelerate and potentially add to our pipelines across all three segments.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We are committed to driving solid financial and operational performance for our shareholders while also delivering on our responsibilities to patients, employees and communities as outlined in Our Credo.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Chris will provide additional franchise and product detail, but let me provide some high level framing.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Our Pharmaceutical business continues to deliver strong growth across our oncology, pulmonary hypertension and immunology portfolios.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We are particularly pleased with the success of DARZALEX, STELARA , IMBRUVICA and the INVEGA portfolio.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: As highlighted during our May Pharmaceutical business review, our performance demonstrates our ability to consistently obtain approval for new products and line extensions.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Once again, our performance was driven by volume of transformational medicines that address high unmet medical need rather than price.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: In our Consumer segment, we accelerated growth in the second quarter in our stronghold beauty lines of Neutrogena and AVEENO.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We are also pleased with the contributions from newly acquired businesses Dr. CI: LABO and ZARBEES.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: This growth more than offset the one-time impacts related to seasonality and inventory levels we mentioned during our first quarter call.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We expect to deliver competitive growth relative to the market for the year.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: In our Medical Devices segment, we did incur some isolated supply disruptions in the quarter, which Chris will outline and the impact limited growth by 1 point.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Accounting for that, we grew above 4%, in line with last quarter and we are on track toward our goal of exceeding last year's performance.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We continue to enhance our leadership positions in platforms such as electrophysiology, energy and endocutters.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Orthopedics grew modestly during the quarter, in line with Q1, led by hips and trauma.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: That being said, we remain intent on improving our performance in orthopedics and the segment at large.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Turning to earnings, earnings per share was favorably impacted by a significant gain recorded in other income, specifically the approximately $2 billion pre-tax gain related to the sale of the Advanced Sterilization products business.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We closed this transaction in early April, and as mentioned during the first quarter call, this gain comprises a large majority of our other income guidance for the full-year 2019.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Other income for 2019 is on par with levels experienced in 2015, and consistent with past practice, we intend to utilize these gains to invest in opportunities that increase shareholder value and better position the business for long-term success.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: I'll now turn the call back to Chris to discuss second quarter sales drivers, as well as highlight notable line items in our P&L, before I return with some comments regarding our cash position, capital allocation priorities and guidance.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Worldwide sales were $20.6 billion for the second quarter of 2019, a decrease of 1.3% versus the second quarter of 2018.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Operational sales growth, which excludes the effect of translational currency, increased 1.6% as currency had a negative impact of 2.9 points.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In the US, sales decreased 2.2%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In regions outside the US, our reported growth declined by 0.3%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Operational sales growth outside the US was 5.5%, with currency negatively impacting our reported OUS results by 5.8 points.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Excluding the net impact of acquisitions and divestitures, adjusted operational sales growth was 3.7% worldwide, flat in the US, and 7.6% outside the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Turning now to earnings, for the quarter net earnings were $5.6 billion and diluted earnings per share was $2.08 versus diluted earnings per share of $1.45 a year ago.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Excluding the after tax intangible asset amortization expense and special items for both periods, adjusted net earnings for the quarter were $7 billion and adjusted diluted earnings per share was $2.58, representing increases of 21.5% and 22.9%, respectively, compared to the second quarter of 2018.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: On an operational basis, adjusted diluted earnings per share grew 25.2%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Beginning with Consumer, I will now comment on business segment sales performance for the second quarter, highlighting items that build upon the slide you have in front of you.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Unless otherwise stated, percentages quoted represent the operational sales change in comparison to the second quarter of 2018, and therefore, exclude the impact of currency translation.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Worldwide Consumer segment sales totaled $3.5 billion, growing at 4.6%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Excluding the net impact of acquisitions and divestitures, adjusted operational sales growth was 2.3%, with strong growth in the US of 4.4% due primarily to strong performance in our beauty franchise.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Growth outside the US was 0.7%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Consumer continues to grow share in the e-commerce channel, outpacing category growth rates in that channel with strong double-digit growth across all regions.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The beauty franchise grew 10.7%, or about 5% adjusted to exclude the impact of the acquisition of Dr.Ci:Labo and the Nizoral and RoC divestitures.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Our priority brands, Neutrogena and AVEENO, delivered strong performance results due to share growth, combined with strong sales in our club and e-commerce channels in the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Share growth in Neutrogena was realized in the facial moisturizing treatment and sun protection categories.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: AVEENO was further aided by retail stocking for the hair products launch.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: OGX and MAUI MOISTURE brands continued to experience solid growth, primarily resulting from new market expansions.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Over-the-counter medicines grew 2.8% globally, or 1% when adjusted to exclude the impact of the Zarbee's acquisition, which continues to perform well.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In the US, OTC adjusted operational sales growth was just over 2% and is growing share.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: However, the US was negatively impacted by retail inventory factors.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: ZYRTEC was a core contributor to sales growth and grew market share.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Additionally, Children's MOTRIN and TYLENOL in pediatric analgesics delivered strong sales and share growth.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Adult Tylenol also continues to drive significant share growth with consumption well outpacing the category, realizing double digit consumption growth, driven by rapid release gel and Tylenol arthritis products.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: However, Tylenol sales declined slightly this quarter as its consumption was more than offset by the lapping of the supply disruption associated with Hurricane Maria and the sell through of 2018 elevated retail inventory levels that occurred in response to seasonal and other retailers stocking dynamics.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Concluding the Consumer segment, babycare grew 2.2% globally.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Growth was primarily due to lapping retail destocking and other events associated with the Johnson's Baby relaunch in the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The Johnson's relaunch is stabilizing performance in all markets where it has been relaunched.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Moving on to our Pharmaceutical segment, worldwide Pharmaceutical sales of $10.5 billion grew 4.4%, enabled by double digit growth in nine key products.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Sales were aided by one-time favorable pricing adjustments outside the US worth almost 100 basis points worldwide, primarily driven by DARZALEX.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Sales declined in the US by 2% and increased outside the US by 12.9%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Generic competition for ZYTIGA negatively impacted our worldwide and US growth by about 300 and 500 basis points, respectively.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Our strong portfolio of products and commercial capabilities has enabled us to deliver global growth at competitive levels despite significant biosimilars and generic headwinds.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Our oncology therapeutic area delivered another strong quarter, with worldwide growth of 14.1%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: DARZALEX continued its strong performance, growing about 57% globally, or about 41% when removing the impact of a favorable one-time adjustment related to the completion of pricing and reimbursement discussions in certain European countries.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The US grew 24% and continues to benefit from strong market growth and about a 3 point increase in US market share across all lines of therapy.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The continued strong double-digit growth outside the US is driven by increased penetration and share gains across the 40 EMEA countries, where it is commercially available as well as Latin America and the Asia-Pacific region.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Of note, just last week, we filed a regulatory submission for the subcutaneous formulation of DARZALEX for multiple myeloma in the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: IMBRUVICA grew over 39% globally, driven largely by market share gains and strong market growth across multiple indications in the US, along with strong uptake outside the US in the European and Asia-Pacific markets.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In the US, based on first quarter data across all indications and lines of therapy, IMBRUVICA gained approximately 3 points of market share and continues to be the new patient and total patient share leader in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, which gained almost 8 points of market share in line one therapy.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Worldwide ZYTIGA growth declined by about 20%, with declines of 59% in the US, driven by generic competition, which was partially offset by growth of about 25% outside the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Strong sales growth in Europe and Asia were driven by market growth and share gains, primarily from the expanded indication in metastatic high-risk castration-sensitive prostate cancer, based on the LATITUDE clinical trial.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, we continue to be pleased with the launch progress of ERLEADA, which gained almost 4 points of market share in the US, with the penetration of prescribers split almost evenly among urology and oncology practices.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We are also pleased with the early launch progress in EMEA, where ERLEADA is now available in five countries.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: During the quarter, we filed regulatory submissions in the US and Europe for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Further we are pleased with the early launch progress of BALVERSA for the treatment of adults with locally or advanced metastatic urothelial cancer.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Our immunology portfolio delivered global sales growth of just under 6%, driven by continued strong performance in STELARA, with growth of 18% primarily from the Crohn's Disease indication.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We remain very pleased with the uptake of STELARA in Crohn's Disease, where market share has increased by over 6 points in the US compared to the second quarter of 2018.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Sales growth was partially offset by continued erosion of REMICADE of 15% due to increased discounts and modest share loss in the US to alternative mechanisms of action and biosimilars.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Lastly, TREMFYA totaled $235 million globally and is experiencing strong demand, with over 35,000 patients on therapy.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: TREMFYA achieved a 7.6% share of the psoriasis market in the US, which is up 3 points from the second quarter 2018.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In infectious diseases, our portfolio grew 5.4%, led by strong growth of SYMTUZA and JULUCA for HIV, partially offset by cannibalization and increased market competition in other products.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In neuroscience, our Paliperidone long-acting portfolio performed well, growing about 16%, with higher market share driven by increased new patient starts and strong persistency.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In addition, we are pleased with the launch performance of SPRAVATO for treatment-resistant depression.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: There are more than 1,600 sites certified with the REMS program and new treatment centers are being added daily.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: In our cardiovascular metabolism and other product portfolio, we did experience declining sales of 14.7%, primarily driven by declines in XARELTO, INVOKANA, and biosimilar competition for PROCRIT.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: XARELTO continues to increase TRx share.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: However, the share uptake was offset by the increase in the legislative rate for the doughnut-hole from 50% to 70%, along with higher Medicare and doughnut-hole utilization, resulting in an overall decline in XARELTO of 19% this quarter.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We've seen a positive response to XARELTO's new 2.5 milligram vascular for the CAD and PAD indication.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: And while we expect the penetration of this expanded patient population to occur over time, we are confident in the value this indication provides to patients.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Our total pulmonary hypertension portfolio grew by 6%, with strong performance in both OPSUMIT and UPTRAVI, growing by about 15% and 19%, respectively, on a global basis.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Both benefited from further market penetration and increased share.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: This growth was partially offset by TRACLEER, which was negatively impacted by the recent generic entry in the US, as well as continued generic competition outside of the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: I'll now turn your attention to the Medical Devices segment.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Worldwide medical devices sales were $6.5 billion, declining 4.1%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Excluding the net impact of acquisitions and divestitures, primarily the divestitures of LifeScan, and ASP, adjusted operational sales growth was 3.2% worldwide.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: As Joe mentioned, we did have some isolated supply challenges in the quarter that negatively impacted growth by about 100 basis points worldwide.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Adjusting for this, Medical Devices would have delivered growth of just over 4%, consistent with the first quarter and representative of the continued progress being made to improve performance in this segment.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Interventional solutions grew about 16% globally, led by continued strength in our electrophysiology business achieving more than 16% growth worldwide, continuing its trend of double digit growth.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Growth was strong in all regions, driven by our newer product offerings in ablation and advanced catheters, contributing to atrial fibrillation procedure market growth.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Additionally, we delivered a fourth straight quarter of double digit growth in our CERENOVUS business, driven by new product innovation including EMBOTRAP for the treatment of ischemic stroke as well strong market growth.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Vision growth of 1.5% was driven by contact lenses, which grew almost 3% globally, led by daily disposables and astigmatism lenses in the OASYS family.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Our contact lenses business remains strong, with year-to-date growth of just under 5% in both the US and OUS.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Orthopedics growth remained consistent versus Q1 of 2019, with growth of 0.6% or 0.9% when adjusting for acquisitions, divestitures and selling days.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We continue to make progress to improve growth in this franchise and we remain committed to executing our innovation and commercial plans that aim to improve performance.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Hips grew 3.3%, which we expect to represent above market performance globally, driven by our leadership position in the anterior approach and continued strong demand for our primary stem ACTIS, which is now our number one selling stem in the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Additionally, our KINCISE surgical impactor, designed to replace the handheld Mallet, is enabling hip procedures in the US.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Trauma growth of 1.7% globally was driven by market growth supported by strong adoption of newer innovation such as our Femoral Recon Nails.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The US growth rate of 3.3% is expected to be in line with the market and accelerated for the third consecutive quarter.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Growth outside the US was flat when adjusting for selling days and was also impacted by over 1 point due to timing of a tender shifting to the second half.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Spine declined over 2%, with the US being the primary driver of the decline.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: OUS growth was flat when adjusting for acquisitions, divestitures and selling days, while we continue to see some stabilization of performance driven by new products such as the VIPER PRIME system for minimally invasive surgery and EXPEDIUM VERSE, our all-in-one pedicle screw system for deformity.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We continue to pursue opportunities to further improve growth, including new innovation such as the Symfony system we plan to launch in the second half in complex cervical.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Knees declined by less than 1% in the quarter, with the US being the driver of the decline offsetting strong growth of over 5% outside the US, that is expected to represent above market performance, led by new innovation including ATTUNE Revision an S+.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The US market is realizing positive uptake from the ATTUNE Revision system, but we continue to have portfolio gaps which we're addressing to enhance performance, including the expected full commercial launch of our cementless offering later this year.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Pricing pressure continue to impact all categories in orthopedics, though was relatively stable overall compared to Q1.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: For the quarter US pure price was negative across all platforms.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Spine pure price declined approximately 4%, with hips, trauma and knees all down about 2%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Turning to the results for the surgery business, Advanced surgery delivered global growth of just over 6%, led by strong performance in both energy and endocutters, primarily driven by share gains and new products in the Asia-Pacific region.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Biosurgery declined by over 2% due to a stop shipment of SURGIFLO in the US, which impact the global biosurgery growth by a 11 points.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We will continue to work with the FDA to ensure this important technology for patients is available again in the US market as soon as possible.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Wound closure grew approximately 3% as conventional and barbed sutures gained share.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Across total general surgery, worldwide growth was negatively impacted by 250 basis points due to a field action on our intraluminal staplers.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Corrective actions were taken in the quarter and we began distributing to customers in June.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Selling days had a minor negative impact on our global growth rates in the second quarter.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: And we do not expect a significant impact in any subsequent quarter in 2019.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: As a final comment on Medical Devices, based on feedback we receive from the analyst community, we will no longer be providing utilization trends during this call.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: These estimates were based on limited external data and provide a low correlation to our actual market performance in the segments we compete.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: As a final update on utilization, we did want to provide you the latest figures for Q1, since we shared estimates last quarter.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Hospital admissions, surgical procedures and lab procedures all increased by approximately 1.5%, 1% and 1.5%, respectively.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: I would now provide some commentary on our earnings for the quarter.

sentence: Regarding our consolidated statement of earnings for the second quarter of 2019, please direct your attention to the box section of the schedule.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: As referenced in the table of non-GAAP measures, the 2019 second quarter net earnings are adjusted to exclude intangible asset amortization expense and special items of $1.3 billion on an after-tax basis, primarily driven by intangible amortization of $1 billion.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Excluding the impact of those items, our adjusted earnings per share is $2.58, an increase of 22.9% versus the second quarter of 2018.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Adjusted EPS on a constant currency basis was $2.63, up 25.2% versus second quarter 2018.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: I'd like to now highlight a few noteworthy items that have changed on the statement of earnings compared to the same quarter last year.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Cost of products sold deleveraged slightly, primarily driven by product mix, which was offset by improvement in selling, marketing and administrative margins for the quarter as a result of leverage in our Pharmaceutical and Consumer businesses.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We continue to invest in R&D at competitive levels and our investment in research and development this quarter as a percent of sales was 13%, which is higher than the second quarter 2018 by 30 basis points.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: This increase was primarily driven by higher investment in our Medical Devices business to support the development of our digital surgery platforms, including robotics.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The increased levels of income recorded in the other income and expense line was primarily driven by the gain on the ASP divestiture.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Net interest expense was lower by a $132 million, primarily driven by the positive effect of net investment hedging arrangements and certain cross currency swaps.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Regarding taxes in the quarter, our effective tax rate of 20.4% was in line with the second quarter 2018 of 20.5%.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: We encourage you to reference our 10-Q for further details on specific tax matters.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Excluding special items, the effective tax rate was 19.3% compared to 18.5% in the same period last year.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The second quarter of 2019 includes the tax impact on the gain of the ASP divestiture.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Now, looking at adjusted income before tax, in the second quarter of 2019, our adjusted income before tax for the Enterprise increased from 33.7% to 41.9% in 2019, primarily driven by the gain on the divestiture of ASP.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The following are the main drivers of adjusted income before tax by segment.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: The decrease in Pharmaceutical margins by 160 basis points was primarily driven by product mix and lower other income.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Consumer margins also decreased by 480 basis points because of lower divestiture gains that were partially offset by leveraging in selling and marketing expenses.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: Medical Devices increased from 27.8% to 57.5% in 2019 due to the gain on the ASP divestiture, partially offset by investments in digital surgery.

speaker: Chris DelOrefice
sentence: That concludes the sales and P&L highlights for Johnson & Johnson's second quarter 2019.

sentence: For your reference, here is a slide summarizing notable developments occurring in the second quarter, some of which were mentioned in my comments.

sentence: I would now turn the call back to Joe.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: With respect to cash, at the end of the second quarter, we had approximately $14 billion of net debt, consisting of approximately $15 billion of cash and marketable securities, and approximately $29 billion of debt.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: These levels are similar to the first quarter.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We simultaneously executed across all four tenants of our capital allocation strategy, which are designed and have proven historically to drive shareholder value.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Reinvestment in our business remains a top priority at Johnson & Johnson.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We invested $2.7 billion in research and development in the quarter, which, as Chris mentioned, represents a 30 basis point increase relative to net trade sales from the second quarter of 2018.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Regarding investment in inorganic opportunities, we closed the acquisition of Auris Health, and we continue to evaluate potential opportunities to further enhance our portfolio.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We also used cash in the quarter to continue returning value to shareholders.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: As announced in April, we increased our dividend for the 57th consecutive year to $0.95 per share, distributing $2.5 billion to shareholders in the quarter.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We also acted on our authorized $5 billion share repurchase program in the quarter to $0.2 billion for that purpose.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We are now slightly above 75% complete with the authorized program.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: I will now provide a few comments on the updates to our guidance for 2019.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Our results for the first half of the year have given us additional confidence in our sales performance for the full year.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: As a result, we are increasing our guidance for operational sales growth by 50 basis points to a range of 1% to 2%.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We are also increasing and tightening our operational sales growth adjusted for acquisitions and divestiture guidance to a range of 3.2% to 3.7%.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: The estimated impact of translational currency of 200 basis points has remained the same as our last update, although we are not predicting the impact of future currency movements.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Regarding adjusted pre-tax operating margin, we now expect adjusted pre-tax operating margin for the year to slightly decline as we are planning for investment in innovation that adds to, solidifies and accelerates our pipelines.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: One really good example of this is our recent acquisition of Auris Health, which I just mentioned.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Our opportunities to invest in digital surgery capabilities, coupled with other strategic investments in support of acquisitions such as Dr.Ci:Labo, are estimated to equate to about $0.10 of dilution.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: However, we have absorbed impacts like this in our current guidance.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: For net interest expense, we are lowering the range to between $0 million and $100 million due to the favorability that Chris described in his earlier remarks.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We are increasing our expectations for other income, the account where we record royalty income, as well as gains and losses arising from items such as litigation, investments by our development corporation, divestitures, asset sales and write offs.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We have more certainty given that we are halfway through the year, and having closed the Advanced Sterilization products transaction, we are comfortable increasing and tightening the range to approximately $2.7 billion to $2.9 billion, increasing the mid-point by $200 million compared to our prior guidance.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Regarding our effective tax rate, we are increasing our effective tax rate guidance to a range of 17.5% to 18.5%, which includes the updated impact to tax associated with the Advanced Sterilization products divestiture gain.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Taking all of these factors into consideration, we are maintaining our full year adjusted EPS guidance for 2019.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: The operational EPS guidance represents strong growth of over 7% at the mid-point, which is approximately 2 times our adjusted operational sales growth while simultaneously increasing investment levels to fortify our confidence in the long-term prospects of our business.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: We do not provide quarterly guidance.

sentence: However, to better inform your modeling, I will provide a few qualitative factors to consider near-term.

sentence: We expect the largest impacts from generics and biosimilars for the year in our Pharmaceuticals business to occur in the third quarter.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: This is primarily driven by expected US ZYTIGA accelerated erosion, as well as the comparison to the highest growth quarter in 2018.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Also US TRACLEER and US PROCRIT as well as VELCADE outside the US expect accelerating erosion, driven largely by generic entries in new markets and additional competitors.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Also, in the third quarter of 2013, we had the favorable impact of the US baby pipeline replenishment due to the relaunch, which will not repeat.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Lastly, as I mentioned, we are taking the opportunity to incrementally invest the higher level of divestiture gains.

speaker: Joe Wolk
sentence: Most notably, we plan to increase investment in our pipelines, and therefore, we would expect our R&D spending to be higher in the second half of the year.

sentence: As we have discussed multiple times, the growth by 2025 is going to be driven mainly through the strength of our currently marketed portfolio, as well as new indications of knees marketed portfolio.

sentence: And we expect that readout of our IBD studies in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease in 2023.

sentence: We provide a significant additional leg of growth for Tremfya; Erleada, which is now in different indications in metastatic and non-metastatic prostate cancer.

speaker: Joaquin Duato
sentence: Our Invega Sustenna franchise in the U.S., as well as our are pulmonary arterial hypertension franchise with Uptravi and Opsumit that has been affected by COVID-19, but that we expect that will continue to deliver growth.

speaker: Joaquin Duato
sentence: And I will go later about the disconnect.

speaker: Joaquin Duato
sentence: Then connected with that, we are also excited about our new product launches, specifically growth of Spravato; growth in Carvykti that I just mentioned before; and also Tecvayli, which we got the approval very recently.

speaker: Joaquin Duato

speaker: Joaquin Duato

speaker: Joaquin Duato

sentence: If I think about the main disconnect between our forecast and the Street forecast, it's our multiple myeloma portfolio.

speaker: Joaquin Duato
sentence: As I commented earlier, we see our multiple myeloma portfolio helping, treating to cure rather than cannibalizing each other.

speaker: Joaquin Duato

speaker: Joaquin Duato
sentence: We see a disconnect, as I commented, in our pulmonary arterial hypertension franchise with Uptravi and Opsumit, which have been impacted by the pandemic, but we see strong growth moving forward.

speaker: Joaquin Duato

sentence: With that, let's talk about the outlook and the year ahead, starting on Page 15.

sentence: As you'll remember from Daniel's comments in December, the 17% that we have talked about as a medium-term ROTCE target is not realistic for 2022.

sentence: Assuming we realize the forward curve, from there, we see the outcomes as being relatively symmetric, with plus or minus 175 basis points of ROTCE impact as a reasonable range relative to our central case.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: In this illustration, the downside assumes that rates stay relatively constant to current spot rates, whereas upside would be driven by a combination of a steeper yield curve and more hikes together with a more favorable deposit reprice experience.

sentence: And of course, what we are evaluating here is the impact of rates in isolation on NII.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: In our central case, markets and banking normalized somewhat in 2022 relative to their respective record years in 2020 and 2021 and resume modest growth thereafter.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: The downside case assumes a return to 2019 trend line levels with sub-GDP growth rates, whereas the upside case assumes continued growth from current elevated levels.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: As we've been discussing in consumer, the big surprise as we emerge from the worst moments of the pandemic was the lower level of card revolve even as spend has started to return.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum

sentence: And in that scenario, revolving balances could stay depressed relative to the long-term pre-pandemic averages, resulting in approximately 50 basis points of downside relative to our central case.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: Of course, there could be an upside case where revolving balances recover much faster, but we believe the risks here are more likely to be skewed to the downside.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: And then, let's touch on inflation for a second, which is, obviously, increasingly relevant.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: On balance, modest inflation that leads to higher rates is good for us.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: But under some scenarios, elevated inflationary pressures on expenses could more than offset the rates benefit, which could represent around 75 basis points of downside.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum
sentence: And while it's not on the page, another key driver is capital, where, even though we remain hopeful, our central case assumes no recalibration of the rules and that we will operate at a higher CET1, reflecting that we finished the year in the 4.5% G-SIB bucket, which equates to a 1% increase from G-SIB in the central case, although, as a reminder, that does not become binding until 2024.

sentence: This is a good opportunity to point out that QE deposit growth and growth of the overall financial system proxied by GDP growth of the factors in the original 2015 rule release, combined, represent two full G-SIB buckets.

speaker: Jeremy Barnum

speaker: Jeremy Barnum

speaker: Jeremy Barnum

speaker: Jeremy Barnum

sentence: So responses has been focused on three areas.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Helping people stay connected while we're all apart; assisting the public health response and working on the economic recovery, especially for small businesses.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I'll start with how we are assisting the public health response.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The first step here is connecting people with authoritative health information.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we built a COVID-19 information center with authoritative information from health officials and governments and messages encouraging people to stay home that are coming from public figures they trust.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we put this COVID-19 Information Center at the top of everyone's Facebook app, and so far we've directed more than 2 billion people to it.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Equally important is also limiting the spread of misinformation.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We don't allow content that puts people at imminent risk of physical harm.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So when people share hoaxes like that inhaling water, curious COVID, which is both false and will be physically harmful if anyone does that, we take that down.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: For other types of misinformation, we partner with independent fact checkers who have marked more than 4,000 pieces of content related to COVID as false, which has resulted in more than 40 million warning labels being seen across our services, and we know that these work because 95% of the time when someone sees a warning label, they don't click through to view that content.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now beyond helping people broadly access high quality informationm, we're also focused on helping governments and health authorities get better data in a privacy protective way to inform key policy decisions that they need to make as well.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we partnered with Carnegie Mellon to run a widespread symptom survey on Facebook, and we're using their findings to produce daily county-by-county maps of the symptoms that people are experiencing across the country, and soon globally as well.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And since people experiencing symptoms is a precursor to them going to the hospital or getting more seriously ill, this tool can help local governments and health officials plan how to allocate scarce resources like PPE and ventilators as well as determine when it's safe to start reopening an area or when an area will need to have tighter shelter orders if symptoms reemerge.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And just this morning we announced that we were working to connect these symptom surveys to ground truth infection rate data from large serology in PCR studies that are funded separately by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative in order to more accurately determine the true infection and exposure levels globally on a local-region basis as well.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So this is work that we're uniquely positioned to do, because Facebook is a global community and people use their authentic identities on our service.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So that means that we can make sure that the data is meaningful.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But we're very focused on doing this in ways that we know are going to be helpful to the health response and that protect people's privacy and human rights, which is why we've primarily focused on how aggregate data can help.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now outside of Facebook, Priscilla and my work at the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative with alongside leading experts in science and health continues to inform my views on the best ways for us to assist in this health response.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And also what we should expect going forward with this disease.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: All right so, next I want to discuss how we're helping people stay connected with the people they care about, even while we can't be together during this period.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So this is our core mission.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I'm proud of how we've supported people around the world during this time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We know that people especially rely on social apps in times of crisis and in times when we can't be together in person.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And right now we are experiencing both of those all around the world at the same time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we're seeing major increases and use of our services.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: For the first time ever, there are now more than 3 billion people actively using Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp or Messenger each month.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: That includes 2.6 billion people using Facebook alone and more than 2.3 billion people using at least one of our services every day.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: In many of the places that have been hardest hit by the virus, messaging volume has increased more than 50% and voice and video calling has more than doubled across Messenger and WhatsApp.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: In Italy, for example, we've seen up to 70% more time spent across our apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Instagram and Facebook Live views doubled in one week.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we've also seen time and Group video calling increase by more than a 1000% over March.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Making sure that our services are stable and reliable during this period is a top priority.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're monitoring usage closely and adding capacity in our data centers where we can.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The investments we've made in shared infrastructure that cover all of our different services over the years, has helped us manage through this, but it has been a challenge while all our teams have been working remotely.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I'm showing these numbers to give you a sense of the surge in people relying on these services that we're seeing.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Obviously, I wish the circumstances were different.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I don't expect that this exact spike in usage will sustain over a longer period of time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But in some areas, I think we are seeing an acceleration in pre-existing long-term trends like the dramatic increase in online private social communication that is likely to continue.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And if nothing else, this usage shows that for a lot of people around the world, these services are part of the social infrastructure that brings us together.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now even before COVID-19, our product strategy is already focused on building out private social platforms and enabling online commerce.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So it's well aligned with what people need now.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Last week, we announced a number of new product improvements on video presence, which has emerged as in especially critical part of the private social platform during this time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our view is that video presence includes three categories.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Video calling, Video rooms and live video.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we plan to lead and offer the best services for social uses in each of those different categories.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Video calling, is when you actually ring a person's phone or computer and it's by far the most used type of video chat.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Between WhatsApp and Messenger, there are more than 700 million daily actives participating in calls.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We are doubling the size of WhatsApp video calls from four to eight.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This is important because WhatsApp is the most popular end-to-end encrypted calling service.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So if you care about privacy and encryption and you want to be able to reach anyone, you're probably using WhatsApp.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And now you can get your whole family or a larger group together on calls.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: For video rooms we announced a completely new product called Messenger Rooms.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And the idea here is that you can create a room for any active event you want, send the link to your friends or have them discover your room on Facebook and then they can just drop in and hang out for a bit.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And this is different from any other video presence experience because it is serendipitous.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: You don't have to plan on an event and schedule in advance if you don't want.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But it could be much more spontaneous and fun and I've really enjoyed getting to use this as we've been building out Messenger Rooms internally, and I'm looking forward to getting it in more people's hands around the world soon.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Live video is also particularly important right now.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: People used to primarily live stream physical events, but it's almost known as planning physical events right now livestreaming has become the primary venue for many events, whether that's the Pope's weekly mass on Facebook Live or DJs hosting dance parties on Instagram, every day more than 800 million daily actives are engaging with live streams, across workout classes, concerts and more.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We pivoted the Facebook events team to help people create online events including enabling people and small businesses to charge people who have joined their events in order to support small businesses that rely on in-person services before.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The last area of our response that I want to discuss is how we're helping with the economic recovery, especially for small businesses.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Sheryl, will talk about this more, but with so many businesses forced to close their physical storefronts, more are looking to build their digital presences and those which already invested in their digital presences are increasingly viewing them as the primary storefronts.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we're working on a number of ways to deepen this experience, helping people buy items and services directly within our apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I mean we're going to a lot more to share on this soon.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Overall, though, our business, depends on the success of small businesses.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So this is a moment where we feel that we're well positioned to be champions for small businesses interests and supporters of important infrastructure that they're going to need in order to move online.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: One aspect of online commerce that I want to mention is the partnership that we just announced with Jio platforms in India.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The largest Facebook and WhatsApp communities in the world are in India, and we think that there is an especially important opportunity to serve small businesses and enable commerce there over the long-term.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: By bringing together JioMart, which is Jio's small business initiative to connect millions of shops across India with WhatsApp, we think that we're going to able to create a much better shopping and commerce experience.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And there's a lot more that we can do here, and I'm looking forward to making progress with the team at Jio.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now beyond our immediate plans to help respond to the pandemic.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I also want to share some reflections on how we're planning to run the company during this period.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I have always believed that in times of economic downturn, the right thing to do is to keep investing in building the future, and I believe this for a few reasons.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: First, when the world changes quickly, people have new needs and that means that there are more new segments to build.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Second, since many big companies will pull back on their investments, there are a lot of things that wouldn't otherwise get built, but that we can help deliver.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And the third, I believe that there is a sense of responsibility and duty to invest in the economic recovery and to provide stability for your community and stakeholders if you have the ability to do so.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we're in a fortunate position to be able to do this.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Along with our strong financial position and the important social value our services provide, we're planning to hire at least 10,000 more people in product and engineering roles this year, so we can continue building and making progress.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now that said, with advertiser spending less than our business performance below expectations, we do plan to moderate some areas of our expense growth especially in business functions.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We accepted our profit margins will decrease this year as we continue investing.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And Dave will share more on our financial outlook in a few minutes.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But this economic pullback has certainly reinforced for me the importance of maintaining high margins.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our financial position has allowed us to continue investing in building products and making investments like our partnership with Jio, even when the underlying economic conditions are challenging.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: As always, I am grateful to everyone on this journey with us and that's especially true during this period.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: As our services play in an especially important role right now, in helping people stay connected and assisting the public health response and working on the economic recovery, I really want to thank all of our employees who are working hard to deliver these services and everyone who has believed in us and supported our company over the years to help us get to the point where we can deliver these services for people around the world.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And with that, here is, Sheryl to talk more about our business.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Thanks, Mark, and hi everyone.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: As Mark said, this is an extraordinarily challenging time.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's a public health emergency, a global economic crisis and a time of great anxiety and personal tragedy for so many.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: My heart goes out to everyone on this call who has lost someone they love, and to everyone for the many ways so many are suffering.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Mark talked about how our company has responded during this emergency to keep people safe and informed.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: How we see our responsibilities and how we are thinking about the future.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I'm going to talk more about the impact we have seen in our business and what we are doing to help other businesses survive and recover in this changing landscape.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our total ad revenue for Q1 was $17.4 billion, which is a 17% year-over-year increase.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: After a strong start to the quarter, we saw a significant impact on our business as a consequence of the pandemic from the second week of March onwards.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This impact has not been felt evenly.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We've seen strong growth in gaming and relative stability in technology and e-commerce, which is one of our largest sectors.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: There are few contributing factors here.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: First, as people stay at home, these sectors are seeing more use of their products and services.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Second, advertisers in these sectors tend to optimize for measurable objectives and we are generating sales at lower prices due to the overall reduction in ad demand.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On the other hand, we've seen significant declines in travel and auto as these industries have been hit particularly hard.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: These trends are continuing in the first two weeks of Q2, and Dave will share more on this shortly.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Companies of all types are adapting to a world where people aren't walking into their stores or seeing their brand on billboards.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: With more people spending time on our products and services than ever before, we are focused on continuing to deliver free and paid tools to help businesses reach the right people at the right time.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And on finding new ways to support those struggling to keep the lights on and pay their employees.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: People are looking for businesses on Facebook and Instagram more than usual during this crisis.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So our free products are particularly important to the many brick-and-mortar businesses pivoting quickly online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Even in the United States, before the crisis, one in three companies didn't have a website, because they can be expensive and difficult to set up even in the best of times.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our Facebook page or Instagram business profile is free and in a matter of minutes established as a digital storefront.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Many are finding creative ways to engage their customers using our free products.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: From Jim's offering workouts on Facebook Live to stores and restaurants using WhatsApp and Messenger to reach customers with delivery options.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In Thailand, when Penguin Eat Shabu closed the doors of its nine restaurants, they started selling to go boxes.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: They promoted them with Facebook posts and customers could order through Messenger and they got 350 sales in one minute.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: A second offer led to 2,500 hot pot sales.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: After initially putting their employees on unpaid leave, these sales increased their revenue and helped restore employees to full pay.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Marketers of all sizes have more limited budgets.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So they need to make every dollar work as hard as possible.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: That means measuring as hard as possible.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: That means measuring the value of their advertising is more important than ever, which is something our personalized ads provide.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: For years we have made major investments in systems and tools that enable businesses to easily understand their return on investment.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In the current environment these investments are paying off.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We are also launching new products to help businesses adapt to changing circumstances.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our teams moved quickly to make gift cards available on both Facebook and Instagram giving customers the option to support businesses by paying upfront for products and services they can use later.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We also made it possible for people to create fundraisers for local businesses with a few simple click.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Fundraisers have been available to support non-profits and people since 2015, but given the overwhelming interest in helping small businesses, weather the storm, we made these tools available for businesses as well, something we never expected to do.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We also launched temporary service changes to make it easier for businesses to share critical information like inventory updates, shipment details, or new ways to buy.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: For example, if a restaurant needs to shift to a delivery model, they can now add food delivery links to their Facebook page or Instagram business profile.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Trading these products quickly in the current environment wasn't easy and I am grateful to our product and engineering teams who are executing so well working from home.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: The business resource hub we launched in early May is a one-stop shop where businesses of all sizes can find support in virtual training that can help them migrate online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: People can take courses on everything from how to connect with customers via messaging in Facebook Live, how to increase online sales.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We are fortunate to be in a strong financial position.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We can continue to pay all of our employees and contractors during this difficult time, which is why we believe we have a real responsibility to help others, especially small businesses around the world.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In mid-March, we announced a $100 million grant program to help 30,000 small businesses across more than 30 countries we call home.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Applications open this month and we are focused on getting cash into their hands as soon as possible.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Economic crisis hit vulnerable communities the hardest, especially woman and women of color and the families who depend on them.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: That's why, half of the grants available in the US are earmarked for women minority and veteran owned businesses.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We have also worked closely with the US government Small Business Administration to spread the word to small businesses about how to apply for relief loans reaching 30 million accounts across Facebook and Instagram with this information.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Businesses aren't the only ones facing hardship, newsrooms are too.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: At a time when critical information is needed to keep community safe, news organizations are seeing steep declines in ad revenue.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In late March, we announced a $100 million investment to support the news industry, with $25 million in grant funding for local news organizations and $75 million in marketing spend to get money to publishers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We have a responsibility to help during this uncertain time by connecting billions of people when they are separated physically, getting vital health information on a -- to people on a dramatic scale and helping small businesses survive.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to close by saying how grateful I am to our partners and teams around the world.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: During this unprecedented time we are trying to stay closer than ever to businesses large and small as they adapt to these significant challenges.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I also want to thank our teams for ensuring our services keep running and working so hard to launch new products, so we can continue making a real difference in people's lives.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This is such a difficult period for everyone and we are grateful for the important work that is being accomplished by so many.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Now here's Dave.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Thanks Sheryl and good afternoon everyone.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Echoing Mark and Sheryl's comments, my thoughts are with everyone facing challenges during this difficult and unprecedented time.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Before turning to results, I wanted to comment briefly on Facebook's operating posture during the crisis.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We took early action to ensure that all employee -- our employees were safe and moved to a global work from home stance on March 6 in the week prior to the WHO declaring COVID-19 a global pandemic.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We are currently operating with over 95% of our full-time employees working from home with safety being the number one priority for those essential workers who need to come into our data centers and other facilities.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We have been able to support our existing employees and on board new employees throughout this period.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: While we are by no means operating at 100% of capacity across every dimension of our operations, we have continued to ship new product releases, maintain service availability, review content and stay connected with our business customers.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Given the circumstances, we have been pleased with the dedication and professionalism with which the Facebook team is tackling the challenges presented by this crisis.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Now turning to the results.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: The COVID-19 pandemic is having a broad impact on our community metrics, revenue, expenses and business operations.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Our community metrics reflected increased -- reflect increased engagement as people around the world of shelter-in-place.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: It's gratifying that people are using our family of apps to stay informed and connect with people and organizations that they care about.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: In March, we estimate that on average 2.3 billion people used at least one of our services on a daily basis and that approximately 3 billion people were active on a monthly basis.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We have seen increased usage across all of our services, particularly in markets that have been most impacted by the virus, including a surge in video and voice calling on Messenger and WhatsApp.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: People around the world have increasingly turned to Facebook as well.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Daily active users reached 1.73 billion, up 11% compared to last year.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: DAUs represented approximately 67% of the 2.6 billion monthly active users in March.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: MAUs grew 228 million or 10% compared to last year.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We expect that we will lose some of this increased engagement when shelter-in-place restrictions are relaxed and life returns to a more normal cadence, which we all look forward to.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the financials.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Q1 total revenue was $17.7 billion, up 18% or 19% on a constant currency basis.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Had foreign exchange rates remained constant with Q1 of last year, total revenue would have been $275 million higher.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Q1 ad revenue was $17.4 billion, up 17% or 19% on a constant currency basis.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Again, the COVID-19 pandemic had an meaningful impact on our revenue.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Revenue was strong from the beginning of the quarter through the first week of March, when we began to see a steep slowdown in our ads business, particularly in countries that implemented shelter-in-place measures to reduce the spread of the virus.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: As Sheryl mentioned there was a great deal of variability by vertical.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: During the last three weeks of March, travel and auto were our weakest verticals and we saw relative strength in gaming technology and e-commerce.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: These trends have continued into Q2.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We've seen relatively comparable pullbacks among large and small advertisers.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: COVID-19 had an impact across the globe in Q1.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: On a regional basis ad revenue growth was strongest in Asia Pacific at 21%, followed by US, Canada, Europe and Rest of World at 16% each.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Turning now to our price and volume metrics.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: In Q1, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased 39% and the average price per ad decreased 16%.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: The growth of impressions was primarily driven by Facebook Mobile newsfeed, due to product optimizations we made prior to the pandemic as well as from increased engagement that I talked about earlier.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: The decline in average price per ad was largely attributed -- attributable to the reduction in advertiser demand during the last three weeks of March.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Other revenue, was $297 million, up 80% driven primarily by sales of Oculus products.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: As a reminder, we launched Quest in May 2019.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Turning now to expenses.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Q1 total expenses were $11.8 billion, up 1% on a reported basis.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Excluding the $3 billion expense we recorded in Q1 related to our settlement with the FTC, Q1 of last year that is, related to our settlement with the FTC, total expenses were up 35% year-over-year.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Cost of revenue increased 23% driven primarily by depreciation related to our infrastructure spend.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: R&D grew 40% and was driven primarily by investments in core product as well as our innovation efforts particularly in AR/VR.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Marketing and sales grew 38% and was driven by consumer and growth marketing.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Finally, excluding the FTC expense from Q1 of 2019, G&A grew 49%, driven partially by an increase in estimated credit losses related to COVID-19.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We had over 3,300 net new hires in Q1, primarily in technical functions and ended the quarter with over 48,000 full-time employees, up 28% compared to last year.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: As I mentioned earlier, we continue to recruit and onboard new employees successfully while in a work-from-home environment.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Operating income was $5.9 billion representing a 33% operating margin and our tax rate was 16%.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Net income was $4.9 billion or $1.71 per share.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Capital expenditures were $3.7 billion driven by investments in data centers, servers, office buildings and network infrastructure.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We had $7.3 billion of free cash flow in the quarter and we repurchased $1.2 billion of our Class A common stock.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We ended the quarter with $60.3 billion of cash in investments.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: As I mentioned last quarter that we booked the FTC expense in 2019, we did not pay the $5 billion settlement amount until the -- after the first quarter of 2020 closed.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: In addition, this past week as Mark mentioned, we signed an agreement to invest approximately $5.7 billion into Jio platforms in India.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Our strong balance sheet proved to be an important asset this quarter, enabling us to commit to a long-term growth priority in India even in the midst of a troubled global economy.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the outlook.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: With the COVID-19 crisis like all companies we are facing a period of unprecedented uncertainty in our business outlook, certainly in the nearly eight years I've been with Facebook.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We expect our business performance will be impacted by issues beyond our control, including the duration and efficacy of shelter-in-place orders, the effectiveness of economic stimuli around the world and the fluctuation of currencies relative to the US dollar.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: On the latter point alone, since the WHO declared COVID-19 as a pandemic, we have seen in the US dollar appreciate 5% relative to the foreign currencies we do business in.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Given the increasing uncertainty in our business outlook, we are not providing specific revenue guidance for the second quarter or full year 2020, rather, I would like to provide a snapshot of revenue performance in the second quarter thus far.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: There is a tremendous amount of macro uncertainty.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: So it's difficult to extrapolate performance based on a small sample of data.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: After initial steep decrease in ad revenue in March, we have seen signs of stability reflected in the first three weeks of April.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Ad revenue has been approximately flat compared to the same period a year ago, down from the 17% year-over-year growth in the first quarter of 2020.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: The April trends reflect weakness across all of our user geographies, as most of our major countries have had some sort of shelter-in-place guidelines in effect.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We are understandably cautious given that most economists are forecasting a global GDP contraction in Q2, which if history where a guide, would suggest that the potential for an even more severe advertising industry contraction.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: In terms of expenses, we are continuing to monitor the COVID-19 situation and its impact on our business and operations and we'll adjust to our plans accordingly.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We expect to realize operational savings in certain areas such as travel, events and marketing as well as from slower headcount growth in our business functions.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: However, we plan to continue to invest in product development and to recruit technical talent.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: In addition, we have committed over $300 million to date in investments to help our broader community during this crisis, which will have an impact on our financial performance this year.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: As a result, we expect total expenses in 2020 to be between $52 billion and $56 billion, down from the prior range of $54 billion to $59 billion.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: While this reflects a moderate reduction in the planned growth rate of total expenses, our overall expense growth in the face of expected revenue weakness will have a negative impact on our 2020 operating margins.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Turning now to capital expenditures.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Our significant investments in infrastructure over the past four years have served us well during this period of high user engagement.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We plan to continue to grow our capex investments to enhance and expand our global infrastructure footprint over the long-term.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: In 2020, we now expect capital expenditures to be approximately $14 billion to $16 billion, down from our prior range of $17 billion to $19 billion.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: This reduction reflects a significant decrease in our construction efforts related to shelter-in-place orders.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Given the strong engagement growth and related demands on our infrastructure, this year's capex reduction should be viewed as a deferral into 2021 rather than savings.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Turning now to tax.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We expect our full year 2020 tax rate will be in the high teens, although we may see fluctuations in our quarterly rate depending on our financial results.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Our thoughts are with those in the community who are facing health challenges during this crisis and with those healthcare workers on the front lines.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: We are also mindful of the challenges many businesses are facing in this crisis, including the 140 million small businesses who use our platform.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: Our focus is first and foremost on helping our broad community navigate these challenges.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And so all of the work we do to continue to allow targeting, all of the work we do to make the ads more personalized, all of the work we do to make free tools available, which is important for all the online businesses who use our free tools.

sentence: I mean for commerce on WhatsApp more broadly, we're very focused on making it, so that small businesses can have a presence on all of the apps, right, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger and can communicate organically with people and then increasingly can do things that can help them drive transactions.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we started rolling out things like catalogs in WhatsApp, we're working on payments to be able to complete transactions and we've rolled out a new ad format, click to messaging ads, where basically a lot of small businesses and different businesses are finding that their message threads with people perform better for driving sales than their websites or other presences, they basically buy ads inside Facebook or Instagram and send people through chat threads.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: So we are seeing I think a fairly diverse range of SMBs.

speaker: David Wehner
sentence: And I would say in terms of the diversity of our business that's, that remains very high.

speaker: David Wehner

speaker: David Wehner

speaker: David Wehner

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I can talk to the margins a bit.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Overall, I think during a period like this there are a lot of new things that need to get built.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I think it's important that rather than slamming on the brakes now, as I think a lot of companies may, that it's important to keep on building and keep on investing in building for the new need that people have and especially to make up for some of the stuffs that that other companies would pullback on, and I think that's in some ways that's an opportunity, in other ways, I think it's responsibility to keep on investing in the economic recovery.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So that's in the near term.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But the other reflection that I've had is that, I think if you're going to have a business, which is primarily advertising, which is our plan for the long-term, then I think you have to recognize that advertising is more volatile and sensitive to the macro economy, and therefore if you're going to have this kind of a business, I think you really want to maintain high margins.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So that way when we go through periods like this, you can make sure that we remain stable and healthy and able to keep on building the things that are important for the long term.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So what I guess I'd want to just be clear on is that, we are willing to accept a reduction in margins in the near term, but we understand and I personally have an appreciation for the importance of maintaining high margins over time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So it's not that we're going to kind of take things down this year and then continue taking things down a lot in the future.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I think over the coming years if we invest a lot more now, I think we are going to look for ways to manage expenses to make sure that we can maintain high margins over time.
