sentence: Those numbers give a sense of scale but some of the stories we hear show the impact.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Groups have formed where COVID long-haulers are helping each other through this scary experience where there's not much else to turn to.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Teachers are sending class assignments to students through WhatsApp.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Local bookstores and coffee shops are using Instagram to let customers know they're open for curbside pickup.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We saw people come together to raise $1.8 billion for nonprofit and personal causes through our fundraising tools last year, including $175 million for COVID-related causes alone.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I'm proud of the role that our services played in helping people support each other during what has been such a hard time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, I've spent a fair amount of time on recent earnings calls talking about our election integrity efforts.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So I'm not going to discuss them at length today, but I do want to call out that according to our estimates, we easily surpassed our goal to help 4 million people register to vote as part of the largest-ever effort -- largest effort to distribute authoritative voting information in recent history.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I want to thank everyone involved in our teams and outside involved with that effort.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So today, I'm going to focus on our product work, and specifically, I'm going to focus on four themes that I'm excited about for the year ahead: communities, private messaging, commerce tools for small businesses, and building the next computing platform.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So let's start with communities.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, I think that helping people build communities is one of the most important things that we can do.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our social fabric is made of multiple different layers through which we get our social support.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: First, we have friends and family, and that's the most personal layer.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Then we have communities we're part of, where we feel a sense of purpose and belonging, explore interests, develop skills, grow as individuals and then meet new people.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And then finally, there's the safety net that society and government provide.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And in many parts of the world, there's been an unfortunate decline in community participation over the last several decades, that second layer.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And this isn't something that we can solve alone but I think we can help.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So now that we've helped billions of people stay connected with friends and family, helping everyone find and participate in communities that are meaningful to them has been our next goal.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we even updated our mission a few years ago to reflect this, making it -- give people the power to build community and bring the world closer together.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Today, more than 600 million people are now members of a group on Facebook that they consider to be meaningful in their lives.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This has grown steadily over time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I hear all the time from people who are in parenting groups that there are major resources to navigate raising kids or from people who found a group that shares the same health condition, and they can lean on that community for knowledge and support, or from people who've moved to a new place and joined local groups to meet people and get situated.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our product focus now is to develop this community infrastructure beyond feeds and message boards to help people build and run full, self-sustaining community institutions.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we're building tools to help groups get things done together and provide support for people that span messaging, video chat, and even communities' own websites.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we're exploring different ways to raise funds, including donations, merchandise, and membership fees to help group leaders support their communities' operations and hire people for different roles that are needed to build sustainable communities for the long term.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So as we continue to focus on this, we need to make sure that the communities that people connect with are healthy and positive.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And that's something that we've been focused on for a while now.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: One way, of course, that we do this is by taking down groups that break our rules against things like violence or hate speech.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And in September, we shared that we had removed more than 1 million groups in the last year alone.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But there are also a lot of groups that we may not want to encourage people to join even if they don't violate our policies.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So for example, we stopped recommending civic and political groups in the U.S. ahead of the elections.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we're continuing to fine-tune how this works, but now, we plan to keep civic and political groups out of recommendations for the long term and we plan to expand that policy globally.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And to be clear, this is a continuation of work we've been doing for a while to turn down the temperature and discourage divisive conversation and communities.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, along these same lines, we're also currently considering steps that we can take to reduce the amount of political content in News Feed as well.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're still working through exactly the best ways to do this.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And to be clear, of course, we're still going to enable people to engage in political groups and discussions if they want to.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: These can often be important and helpful, and there can be ways that people organize grassroots movements or speak out against injustice or learn from people with different perspectives.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we want these discussions to be able to keep happening, but one of the top pieces of feedback that we are hearing from our community right now is that people don't want politics and fighting to take over their experience on our services.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So one theme for this year is that we're going to continue to focus on helping millions of more people participate in healthy communities, and we're going to focus even more on being a force for bringing people closer together.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Next, let's talk about private messaging.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: As we've discussed before, while people enjoy connecting with friends and communities in the digital equivalent of a town square in apps like Facebook and Instagram, the fastest-growing social experiences are about connecting privately in the digital equivalent of the living room in services like WhatsApp and Messenger.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So that's why we kicked off a big effort a couple of years ago to reimagine what a modern social platform would look like if you build it from the bottom-up to be privacy first.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we identified several core principles.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: A private social platform should be built around the most intimate interactions that we have, and that's one-on-one conversations.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The most important aspect of privacy and security is that your conversations should stay between you.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And that means that your conversations should always be end-to-end encrypted, and they should disappear when you're done with them.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, safety and reducing spam matter, too, and that means that we should maintain a minimum amount of metadata to build sophisticated tools to stop bad actors using these services.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And you should have choice over what services you use.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we should make messaging as interoperable as possible across our apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And finally, no matter what, we should only store people's data in countries where we know we can keep it secure, and we should continue opposing data localization in countries with weak records on human rights or privacy.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, I think that these are the privacy principles that matter most to people.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: First and foremost, people care that their conversations stay private.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But after that, people also care about safety and other convenience, too.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And from this perspective, WhatsApp and the direction that we're heading in with Messenger are the best private social apps available.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, we have a lot of competitors who make claims about privacy that are often misleading.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, Apple recently released so-called nutrition labels which focused largely on metadata that apps collect rather than the privacy and security of people's actual messages, but iMessage stores non-end-to-end encrypted backups of your messages by default unless you disable iCloud.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So Apple and governments have the ability to access most people's messages.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So when it comes to what matters most, protecting people's messages, I think that WhatsApp is clearly superior.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, since I try to use these earnings calls to discuss aspects of business strategy that I think are important for investors to understand, I do want to highlight that we increasingly see Apple as one of our biggest competitors.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: iMessage is a key linchpin of their ecosystem.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: It comes pre-installed on every iPhone, and they preferenced it with private APIs and permissions, which is why iMessage is the most used messaging service in the U.S. And now, we are also seeing Apple's business depend more and more on gaining share in apps and services against us and other developers.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So Apple has every incentive to use their dominant platform position to interfere with how our apps and other apps work, which they regularly do to preference their own.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And this impacts the growth of millions of businesses around the world.

speaker: Including
sentence: So to make sure that we remain the best, a couple of years back, we kicked off a number of long-term efforts that have started shipping recently.

speaker: Including
sentence: And more of these projects around strengthening encryption, ephemerality, interoperability, and offering other tools are going to be shipping throughout this year.

speaker: Including
sentence: So now, let's talk about commerce.

speaker: Including
sentence: Our goal here is to give every individual, entrepreneur, and small business access to the same kinds of tools that historically only the big companies have had access to.

speaker: Including
sentence: And we've always cared about this, but the pandemic has made it more urgent.

speaker: Including
sentence: So it used to be the case that only large companies could afford to have analytics or targeted advertising capacity to reach their customers.

speaker: Including
sentence: And it was expensive to build these capabilities, and it often required building teams and storing large amounts of data in-house, which most small businesses can't do.

speaker: Including
sentence: And so one of the things that I'm most proud of is that we build the tools so we can offer these same capabilities to small businesses often for free.

speaker: Including
sentence: So when you hear people say that we hold a lot of data, that's because hundreds of millions of businesses that would have otherwise had to do this individually and would have had no easy way of doing so are now using our services to help them reach customers.

speaker: Including
sentence: And when you hear people say that we're connecting data from lots of sources, that's to help small businesses reach customers more efficiently.

speaker: Including
sentence: Now, big companies often do this themselves, but small businesses can't a lot of times.

speaker: Including
sentence: So we do this for them.

speaker: Including
sentence: So when you hear people argue that we shouldn't be doing these things or that we should go back to the old days of untargeted television ads, I think that what they're really arguing for is a regression where only the largest companies have this capacity, small businesses are severely disadvantaged, and competition is diminished.

speaker: Including
sentence: So with our commerce tools, we've made it so that a business can set up a shop once, and then they will have an online storefront in both Facebook and Instagram immediately and eventually on WhatsApp and Messenger as well.

speaker: Including
sentence: And we recently expanded checkout to all U.S. businesses, making the process of buying a lot more seamless.

speaker: Including
sentence: And as the lockdowns have continued, we saw more businesses, more small businesses, and creators also use paid online events as a way to make money.

speaker: Including
sentence: WhatsApp is also an important part of our strategy here.

speaker: Including
sentence: More than 175 million people message a WhatsApp business account every day.

speaker: Including
sentence: And we're building new features to make it even easier to transact with businesses in the app.

speaker: Including
sentence: We introduced carts, which lets people browse catalogs, select multiple products and send the order as a message to a business.

speaker: Including
sentence: And the more people that interact with businesses, the better tools that we're going to need to provide for businesses to help them support their customers.

speaker: Including
sentence: Many businesses need more than a phone to manage their customer service.

speaker: Including
sentence: So we're building tools to let businesses store and manage their WhatsApp chats using our secure hosting infrastructure if they would like.

speaker: Including
sentence: And we're in the process of updating WhatsApp's privacy policy in terms of service to reflect these optional experiences.

speaker: Including
sentence: Now, to clarify some confusion that we've seen, this update does not change the privacy of anyone's messages with friends and family.

speaker: Including
sentence: All of these messages are end-to-end encrypted, which means we can't see or hear what you say, and we never will unless the person that you message chooses to share it.

speaker: Including
sentence: And business messages will only be hosted on our infrastructure if the business chooses to do so.

speaker: Including
sentence: So we want everyone to know the lengths that we go to, to protect your private messages.

speaker: Including
sentence: So we are moving the date of this update back to give everyone time to understand what the update means.

speaker: Including
sentence: Finally, let's discuss our work building the next computing platform.

speaker: Including
sentence: This is one of the areas that I'm most excited about our progress heading into 2021.

speaker: Including
sentence: If you look at the history of computing, every 15 years or so, a new major platform emerges that integrate technology more naturally and ubiquitously into our lives, starting with mainframes and PCs and browser-based computing, and then mobile.

speaker: Including
sentence: And I believe that the next logical step here is an immersive computing platform that just delivers this magical sense of presence that you're really there with another person or in another place.

speaker: Including
sentence: Our phones can't deliver this, and neither can any other technology that has come before it.

speaker: Including
sentence: This is going to unlock the types of social experiences that I have dreamed about building since I was a kid, and it's what we're building toward at Facebook Reality Labs.

speaker: Including
sentence: We launched Quest 2 in October, and it is on track to be the first mainstream virtual reality headset.

speaker: Including
sentence: We designed it so that anyone could jump in with the best and most immersive experience out there and at a price that makes it available to as many people as possible.

speaker: Including
sentence: Now, I think that Facebook has done more than any other company to help bring virtual reality to the mainstream, and it has been great to see so many people embrace this, especially this year during the pandemic.

speaker: Including
sentence: We're seeing people use it to play games with friends when they can't be together in person, to do workouts in their living room, or to meet with colleagues while they're working from home.

speaker: Including
sentence: So there are a lot of reasons that Quest 2 was one of the hot holiday gifts this year.

speaker: Including
sentence: We're also seeing a growing ecosystem of developers building amazing new experiences for the platform.

speaker: Including
sentence: Right now, more than 60 Oculus developers are generating revenue in the millions, and that's nearly twice as many as a few months ago.

speaker: Including
sentence: In previous quarters, I've talked about our long-term future goals when it comes to virtual reality, but I think that this quarter's results show that this future is here.

speaker: Including
sentence: Augmented reality glasses are going to be a key part of this vision, too.

speaker: Including
sentence: We're still working on some of the foundational technology to underpin these and the ultimate product is still some years away, but this year, we are excited to deliver a first glimpse of what will be when we launch our first pair of smart glasses from Ray-Ban in partnership with Luxottica.

speaker: Including
sentence: And during this pandemic, we've also seen Portal has proven to be a great way for people to stay connected especially over the holidays as families had to celebrate apart.

speaker: Including
sentence: This year, we're focused on expanding the role of Portal and virtual reality presence into the workplace, bringing more features that can improve remote presence, collaboration, and productivity.

speaker: Including
sentence: 2021 has a lot of unknowns.

speaker: Including
sentence: We don't know when vaccines are going to be widely available, when our teams will be back in the office or when our lives are going to start feeling normal again.

speaker: Including
sentence: But what I do know is that we're going to keep investing in and innovating on the big themes that I discussed here in order to put more power in the hands of people and small businesses.

speaker: Including
sentence: I personally believe that technology can unlock progress and opportunity and that the full story of the Internet has not yet been written.

speaker: Including
sentence: That's why I'm hopeful for the year ahead and grateful that you are all in this journey with us.

speaker: Including
sentence: And now, here is Sheryl to talk about our business.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Thanks, Mark, and hi, everyone.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Like Mark, I hope everyone is safe and healthy.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This was a strong quarter for our business as the acceleration of online commerce we've seen during the pandemic continued into the holiday season.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our total revenue for Q4 was $28.1 billion, which is a 33% year-over-year increase, our fastest growth rate in over two years.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: After a really difficult year for so many businesses, this holiday period was important.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And while many businesses are still struggling, the good news is that Q4 was stronger than expected for retail.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In the U.S., the National Retail Federation reported that sales in November and December went up 8% year over year and online sales were up 24%.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This holiday period was also longer.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Compared to previous years, advertisers started spending earlier and sustained that spend well beyond Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We saw robust performance across regions, as well as an improvement in brand advertising.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: The strength of our Q4 performance is a result of years of investments in free and paid tools to help businesses succeed online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Even before the pandemic, businesses were going digital, but COVID made this a necessity.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Almost overnight, businesses had to create digital storefronts, figure out how to take online orders, and find new ways to reach their customers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: For many small companies, these steps or even just setting up a website or a mobile app can be difficult and expensive.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our free and paid tools help solve these problems for businesses around the world.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: With so many businesses struggling when the pandemic hit, we asked our teams what do businesses need and how can we help.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: First, they need the tools to get their business up and running online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So what can we do to make ours simpler and more effective?

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And can we build new ones to help them?

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Second, they need the digital skills and know-how to succeed.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So how can we help more businesses with training and resources?

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And third, they need their voices to be heard.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So can we use our scale to amplify their voices and tell their stories?

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We've been asking these questions throughout the last year and into Q4.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On the first, we accelerated our work on tools to make it easier for people to find brands and products they love and for businesses to manage their online presence and connect with customers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Mark talked about some of the new tools we've launched, like shops and paid online events.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In the fall, we also rolled out Facebook Business Suite, a new interface to help businesses manage their pages or profiles across our apps.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We also continued to invest in making our products as effective as possible so businesses can get more value for every dollar they spend.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Personalized ads are privacy-safe and help businesses reach customers where they are, which has been more important than ever during the pandemic.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: One notable area of progress this past year was in Stories ads, which have become more effective for direct-response advertisers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: One business that used Stories ads is Carlota Flower Lab, a florist in Los Reyes, Mexico.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Before COVID, they made 70% of their revenue from face-to-face workshops.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So when the pandemic hit, founder Paola Mendoza had to get creative.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: She used personalized ads on Instagram to reach new audiences and even found her first international customers with campaigns targeting California and Texas.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: One campaign for Dia de los Muertos, the Day of the Dead in November, led to a 24 times return on ad spend, helping Paola triple her annual revenue in 2020 despite COVID.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On the second, resources and training, we did some big things in 2020.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We created a Business Resource Hub, a one-stop shop for resources and trainings for small businesses that we've continued to build out through the end of the year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We committed to reach 1 million members of the black community and 1 million members of the Latinx and Hispanic communities in the U.S. with free digital skills training through our Elevate program by 2023.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we reimagined our Boost with Facebook events to reach businesses virtually with 100 million people tuning in throughout the year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This included our 12-week season of support to help businesses across 16 countries prepare for the holidays.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On the third, a great example of how we amplify the voices of our businesses in Q4 is our #BuyBlack Friday campaign, one of my favorite campaigns ever.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In the U.S., black-owned businesses closed at twice the rate of others after the start of the pandemic.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So we wanted to help people shop with them over the holidays.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We created ways for people to find black businesses in their local area, a gift site featuring products from black businesses across the U.S., and even a #BuyBlack Friday show on Facebook Live that was seen by 15 million people.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: One of the small businesses we featured is a vegan skincare brand called Redoux from New York City.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Its founder, Asia Grant, appeared on the #BuyBlack Friday show, and that became one of her most successful sales days ever.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: The campaign gave her record revenue and web traffic, and she was even able to hire more people, something that's so important given current unemployment rates.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Business owners like Asia and Paola have worked hard to adapt and grow online, but lots of businesses will continue to struggle in 2021.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So we're going to keep listening to them and building on what we did last year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: That means improving our products and tools to help businesses seamlessly manage their online presence, advertise across our apps, and communicate with customers through business messaging.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It means making more training available through programs like She Means Business for women and Elevate for diverse communities.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And it means finding more ways to amplify their voices, whether it's sharing the stories of small businesses worried that Apple's iOS 14 changes will hurt their ability to reach customers or showcasing small businesses and gift guides and products like businesses nearby.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to close by saying how grateful I am to all the businesses around the world who work with us.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Your partnership helps us build the tools you need so you can continue to grow and hire.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And as always, I'm grateful to our incredible teams who have done so much to help businesses survive this difficult year, including coming up with great ideas like #BuyBlack Friday.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I hope that 2021 is a better year for everyone.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Now, here's Dave.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Thanks, Sheryl, and good afternoon, everyone.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q4 was a strong quarter, capping off a solid year for our business as full-year 2020 revenue grew 22% to $86 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We have been encouraged to see improved demand for our ads during the second half of the year after facing significant headwinds at the onset of the pandemic.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our results reflect the ongoing strength in the digital economy and the value we're providing to millions of businesses who use our services to reach consumers and generate sales.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Let's begin with our community metrics.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In December, we estimate that approximately 2.6 billion people use at least one of our services on a daily basis and that approximately 3.3 billion people use at least one on a monthly basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Facebook daily active users reached 1.84 billion, up 11% or 188 million compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: DAUs represented approximately 66% of the 2.8 billion monthly active users in December.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: MAUs grew 299 million or 12% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Consistent with our outlook, U.S. and Canada DAU declined 1 million sequentially as usage continued to normalize from peak COVID levels experienced earlier in the year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning to the financials.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: All comparisons are on a year-over-year basis unless otherwise noted.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q4 total revenue was $28.1 billion, up 33% or 32% on a constant-currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We benefited from a currency tailwind and had foreign exchange rates remained constant with Q4 of last year, total revenue would have been $339 million lower.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q4 ad revenue was $27.2 billion, up 31% or 30% on a constant-currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The growth in advertising revenue was largely driven by a strong holiday shopping season for retail, which benefited from the ongoing shift to online commerce.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: On a user geography basis, ad revenue was strongest in Europe, which grew 35% and benefited from currency tailwinds; U.S. and Canada grew 31%, and Asia Pacific grew 29%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Rest of world growth improved 25% but continues to be significantly impacted by currency headwinds.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In Q4, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased 25% and the average price per ad increased 5%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Impression growth was driven by both Facebook and Instagram.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The increase in average price per ad was driven primarily by Facebook mobile feed, as well as pricing improvement in Instagram Stories.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Other revenue was $885 million, up 156% due to strong Quest 2 holiday sales.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We've been encouraged by the positive reception of Quest 2 since its October launch.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to expenses.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q4 total expenses were $15.3 billion, up 25% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In terms of specific line items, cost of revenue increased 49% driven primarily by hardware costs related to Quest 2 sales, core infrastructure investments, and payments to partners.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: R&D increased 34% driven primarily by hiring and investments in core products, as well as our consumer hardware efforts.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Marketing and sales increased 8%, driven by hiring and marketing spend.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Lastly, G&A expenses decreased 13% as we lapped charges related to the BIPA legal settlement recorded in the fourth quarter of 2019.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In the past year, we added a record 13,600 net employees and reached our goal of adding 10,000 employees in tech and product roles.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We ended the year with over 58,600 full-time employees, up 30% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We continue to be pleased with our ability to recruit, onboard, and retain talent in this environment.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Fourth-quarter operating income was $12.8 billion, representing a 46% operating margin.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our tax rate was 14%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Net income was $11.2 billion or $3.88 per share.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Capital expenditures were $4.8 billion, driven by investments in data centers, servers, office facilities, and network infrastructure.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Free cash flow was $9.2 billion, and we ended the quarter with $62 billion in cash and marketable securities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: For the full year, we repurchased $6.3 billion of our Class A common stock and had $8.6 billion remaining in our prior authorization as of December 31.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Today, we announced a $25 billion increase in our stock repurchase authorization.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We continue to face significant uncertainty as we manage through a number of crosscurrents in 2021.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We believe our business has benefited from two broad economic trends playing out during the pandemic.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The first is the ongoing shift to online commerce.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The second is the shift in consumer demand toward products and away from services.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We believe these shifts provided a tailwind to our advertising business in the second half of 2020, given our strength in product verticals sold via online commerce and our lower exposure to service verticals like travel.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Looking forward, a moderation or reversal in one or both of these trends could serve as a headwind to our advertising revenue growth.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: At the same time, in the first half of 2021, we will be lapping a period of growth that was negatively impacted by reduced advertising demand during the early stages of the pandemic.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: As a result, we expect year-over-year growth rates in total revenue to remain stable or modestly accelerate sequentially in the first and second quarters of 2021.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In the second half of the year, we will lap periods of increasingly strong growth, which will significantly pressure year-over-year growth rates.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We also expect to face more significant ad targeting headwinds in 2021.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: This includes the impact of platform changes, notably iOS 14, as well as the evolving regulatory landscape.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: While the timing of the iOS 14 changes remains uncertain, we would expect to see an impact beginning in the late first -- beginning late in the first quarter.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: There is also continuing uncertainty around the viability of transatlantic data transfers in light of recent European regulatory developments.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And like other companies in our industry, we are closely monitoring the potential impact on our European operations as these developments progress.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to expenses.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2021 total expenses to be in the range of $68 billion to $73 billion, unchanged from our prior outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: This is driven by investments in technical and product talent, as well as continued growth in infrastructure costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We continue to expect 2021 capital expenditures to be in the range of $21 billion to $23 billion driven by data centers, servers, network infrastructure, and office facilities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our outlook includes spend that was delayed from 2020 due to the impact of the pandemic on our construction efforts.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to tax.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We continue to expect our full-year 2021 tax rates to be in the high teens.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In closing, 2020 was a unique operating environment that introduced a number of unforeseen challenges.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We have been pleased with our team's ability to adapt in order to maintain the reliability of our services, deliver new products and experiences, and support the millions of businesses who use our platforms to reach consumers.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: With that, Mike, let's open up the call for questions.

sentence: With Instagram Shopping, we launched a new Shop tab on Instagram in Q4, and this is built on other shopping efforts we've had.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg

sentence: So small businesses are very reliant on personalized ads, the ability to use data in a very privacy-safe way to get the customers who are interested in their products and services.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And that makes sense.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Big businesses, we can buy an ad to the whole country.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We can buy an ad to a whole region.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Small businesses can't.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: They have to find the precise audiences they want.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And I think one of the mainstays of our business is we've enabled that targeting in a very privacy-safe way without giving information without permission to advertisers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And what's happening with IDFA is that small businesses are really concerned because they're worried that they're not going to be able to buy effective advertising.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: If all personalized ads went away, small businesses would see a 60% cut in website sales.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Now, we don't think Apple's contemplating going that far that quickly, but that is the general direction of what would happen.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And you can see that that would be very detrimental to their business.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's also very detrimental to economic growth because so much of our job growth comes from small businesses.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I think it's worth noting it's not just about advertisers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Some of these changes also impact developers and other forms of businesses.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We are starting to hear from creators and developers who are worried that some of their free services will have to start charging or shut down, force them into subscriptions or other in-payments for revenue.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Now, not all small businesses are aware of these challenges, but we are hearing from more and more of them.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So we're very concerned.

sentence: More than 2.7 billion people now use one or more of our apps each day, and more than 200 million businesses use our tools to reach customers.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And this has been an intense year, and I am proud that we continue to deliver value for people and businesses around the world.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now over the past couple of quarters, our business has been performing better than we expected.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And this has given us the confidence to increase our investments meaningfully and in a few key areas that have the potential to change the trajectory of the company over the long term.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So on today's call, I'm going to talk about the opportunities that we're pursuing in augmented and virtual reality and around commerce, business messaging, and creators.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So first, let's talk about building the next computing platform.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now I believe that augmented and virtual reality are going to enable a deeper sense of presence in social connection than any existing platform.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: They're going to be an important part of how we will interact with computers in the future.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we're going to keep investing heavily in building out the best experience this year, and this accounts for a major part of our overall R&D budget growth.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Quest 2 is doing better than we expected, even after the holiday season.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We continue to see good engagement, and we keep shipping updates that make Quest better and better, including Air Link, which enables wireless streaming of games and content from PCs and support for 120-hertz refresh rates.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now achieving Quest's high quality in a wireless form factor has been a major breakthrough.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Having wires wrapped around you just really breaks the sense of presence in immersion.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And the technology to deliver a great experience wirelessly is very advanced, and most companies aren't going to be able to deliver this.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But we believe that it is the minimum bar for a high-quality experience.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This quarter, we also shared more about our future investments, including neural interfaces for interacting with AR.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we started testing our new avatar system, which will be a key part of how people express themselves and connect.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: One interesting trend is that we're seeing the app ecosystem broaden out beyond games into other categories as well.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The most used apps are social, which fits our original theory for why we wanted to build this platform in the first place.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're also seeing productivity and even fitness apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So for example, we launched a tool so people can subscribe to services like FitXR to do boxing and dancing in VR, just like they would for biking on Peloton.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We introduced App Lab so developers can ship early versions of their apps directly to consumers without having to go through the Oculus store.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And between App Lab and streaming from PCs, we're pioneering a much more open model of app store than what's currently available on phones today.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now over time, I expect augmented and virtual reality to unlock a massive amount of value, both in people's lives and the economy overall.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: There's still a long way to go here, and most of our investments to make this work are ahead of us.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But I think that the feedback that we're getting from our products is giving us more confidence that our prediction for the future here will happen and that we're focusing on the right areas.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now beyond AR and VR, I want to call out some of the other long-term opportunities that we're really focused on, especially in commerce and business messaging.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Commerce has been growing in our services for a while, but it has become a lot more important as the pandemic has accelerated a broader shift toward businesses moving online.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: In the last year, we've seen online storefronts stay open, even when physical stores closed.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And going forward, online commerce will continue to offer an increasingly personalized and convenient experience.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Commerce ads continue to do very well and drive a meaningful amount of our overall business.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We built Marketplace into one of the world's leading services for people to buy and sell.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I am pleased to share today that more than 1 billion people visit Marketplace each month.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And now we're investing in building for the future of commerce, so we launched Shops last year.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And as I recently shared, there are now more than 1 million monthly active shops and over 250 million monthly shops and visitors.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We are also focused on building more native commerce tools across our apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We recently updated WhatsApp catalog, so businesses can keep them updated from their computers and to include what's in stock.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We launched carts on WhatsApp last year, and people have used them to send orders more than 5 million times.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're also building a broader infrastructure to support commerce, everything from payments to customer service and support.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And WhatsApp Payments is now live in India, and we have gotten approval in Brazil to launch shortly, too.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're starting to see a meaningful shift in the way that people communicate with businesses.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: For a lot of people, online commerce is less about websites and shops and more about messaging.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So people want to get support and make purchases right from a chat.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Smaller businesses want to show their products and take orders via messages, and larger businesses want reliable and secure infrastructure to communicate with their customers.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Businesses using the WhatsApp business API are already sending more than 100 million messages per day.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Over the last year, during the height of COVID, total daily conversations between people and businesses on Messenger and Instagram grew by more than 40%.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: More than 3 million advertisers are already using click-to-message ads to direct people to Messenger.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And since we introduced click-to-WhatsApp ads, nearly 1 million advertisers have already started using them, too.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And now the next step here is we're going to make it possible to create those click-to-WhatsApp ads from -- directly within the WhatsApp business app.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The next step is to make it easier for businesses to adopt all these services and to give them the tools that can handle messages and customer relationships.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our acquisition of customer is going through regulatory approvals, and we're looking forward to offering businesses a native way to manage their customer relationships on our platform.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now I want to be clear that we have a long way to go to build out a full-featured commerce platform across our services.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And this is a multiyear journey, but I am very committed to getting there.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This modern commerce system is going to bring together a number of areas where we either already have strong offerings like in ads, community tools, and messaging, with areas like shops and business messaging and payments that we are focused on ramping up now.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: As part of this, we're also investing more in building out better customer support for our products.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: For the last several years, we focused a lot on content moderation and privacy work.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I view customer support as the next pillar of the trust and safety work for our services.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The last area that I want to discuss today is around creators.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I think that a positive vision for the future of the economy is one where more people get to do creative work that they enjoy rather than jobs that they don't.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And to get there, we need to build out the creative and monetization tools to support this creator economy.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: People create an incredibly diverse set of content across our services from long-form writing to live conversations to documentaries and augmented reality filters.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And our goal is to support the full range of human expression and to be the best platform for millions of creators to make a living.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now, part of this is going to be delivering a suite of tools and products that span all of the ways that people want to create and consume content.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I believe that the intersection of every media type and every audience size, there is a compelling experience to build.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: For example, I recently discussed our audio road map.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we already support audio calls for private audio communication, but now we're also building out live audio rooms, which we think will be especially useful for groups and communities.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're building sound bites for sharing and consuming short-form audio clips broadly, and we are supporting podcasts for sharing and listening to long-form audio.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we're also partnering with Spotify to launch a music player in the Facebook app.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we also need to connect these experiences with easy options for monetization, whether that's subscriptions, tipping, or enabling creators to give product recommendations and enable commerce.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And with Instagram and Facebook, we have a unique ability to bring creators and commerce together, and we will share more on that later this year.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now together, these efforts around creators, commerce, and the next computing platform are a few of the big areas that we were doubling down on going forward.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And in each of these, there is a unique opportunity to help people connect in deeper ways and to support a stronger economy for everyone.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I'm optimistic that our work in all of these areas will help accelerate some of the positive emerging trends that we are seeing in the world.

sentence: And now I'm going to hand it over to Sheryl.

sentence: Thanks, Mark, and hi, everyone.

sentence: I hope you're all safe and healthy.

sentence: This was a really strong quarter for our business.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our total revenue for Q1 was $26.2 billion, which is a 48% year-over-year increase.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We've seen good growth in all regions, and we continue to see strong results in verticals that have performed well during the pandemic, like e-commerce, retail, and CPG.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our performance has been driven, in large part, by the continued digital transformation as more and more businesses shift online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: For years, we've invested in products and tools to support this shift.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And these investments have helped many businesses reinvent themselves during the pandemic.

sentence: Many of them tell me how they've used Facebook to adapt and grow.

sentence: At a virtual roundtable with SMBs from Detroit this quarter, I spoke to La'Asia Johnson, who runs an all-natural skincare company called Elle Jae Essentials.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: When COVID hit and she had to close her store, she started a Facebook group called The Garden, which now has more than 1,000 members.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: They give her product ideas.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And when she makes the projects they suggest, as she says it, they sell quicker than she can keep them on the shelves.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: By pivoting online, she's been able to replace all of the income she lost from her store.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I also spoke to Ita Reyes, who runs a yoga studio in nearby Ann Arbor.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: She started doing outdoor classes during the pandemic and needed to get the word out.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: She couldn't afford to advertise to everyone in the city, and not everyone in the city wants to do yoga so she uses personalized ads.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This enables her to advertise to people in the area who are interested in yoga or meditation.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's all done in a privacy protected way.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We show her ad to those people, and we don't share their information with her, and then they sign up for her classes.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Like everyone else, the business owners I talk to want to know what will happen next.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Many are all in online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So even when things fully reopen, they want to be able to do more online than they did before.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So understandably, they're asking us what we can do to help them, not just now, but over the long run.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Part of the answer is continuing to improve our tools and products and creating new ones to suit their needs.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And part of it is helping them navigate the headwinds that are coming down the line, whether it's the iOS 14 changes or potential regulations.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On the first part, tools, and products.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We are all in, too.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: From day one of COVID, we fast-tracked our work to help people buy and sell online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Initially, we focused on getting the experience right for sellers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: As Mark said, we launched Shops nearly a year ago.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We've continued to develop new features to help personalize the shopping experience and worked with partners to make transactions as seamless as possible.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we've created new formats like live shopping, which bring to life the unique commerce experiences our platforms can offer.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Now we're equally focused on getting the experience right for consumers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're rolling out the Shop tab in more countries and exploring new immersive formats like product tags and drop stickers that enable more people to shop with creators and brands they love.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're also constantly developing and improving our ad products to help businesses reach people where they are and get the best possible return on investment.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We continue to see strong growth in Stories ads and video ads, which we've invested in heavily.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We've also seen strong growth across ads in Facebook Watch, which now has more than 1.25 billion people visiting every month.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: As the number of people watching video grows, we're developing more opportunities for businesses and creators to reach them.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're expanding paid online events to more countries.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're enabling more people to run in stream ads, including in live videos.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we're developing ads in short-form videos, where we're testing the ability for content creators to monetize their Facebook Stories with ads that look like stickers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On the second part, headwinds.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Yes, there are challenges coming to personalized advertising, and we've been pretty open about that.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're doing a huge amount of work to prepare.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're working with our customers to implement Apple's API and our own aggregated events measurement API to mitigate the impact of the iOS 14 changes.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're rebuilding meaningful elements of our ad tech so that our system continues to perform when we have access to less data in the future.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we're part of long-term collaborations with industry bodies like the W3C on initiatives like privacy-enhancing technologies that provide personalized experiences while limiting access to people's information.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's also on us to keep making the case that personalized advertising is good for people and businesses and to better explain how it works so that people realize that personalized ads are privacy protected.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Small businesses don't have to understand the alphabet soup of acronyms they'll need to comply with, but they do need to have confidence that they can still use our tools to reach the people who want to buy what they're selling in a privacy-safe way.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're confident they can and that they can continue to get great results as digital advertising evolves.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: With the rollout of vaccines, there's reason to be hopeful.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: But the pandemic is still causing real heartbreak and hardship for people in many countries.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And in particular, like Mark, my thoughts are with our friends and colleagues in India and Brazil right now.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: If the last year has taught us anything, it's to not make assumptions and to not expect things to get better for everyone at the same time.

sentence: Whatever happens, we'll continue to keep people connected, support the public health response and invest in ways to support businesses now and in the long term.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to close by saying how grateful I am to all the businesses who work with us, big and small, who we learn from every day, and to our incredible teams who have supported millions of businesses through this turbulent time and set them up for success now and in the future.

sentence: We estimate that approximately 2.7 billion people used at least one of our services on a daily basis in March and that approximately 3.4 billion people used at least one on a monthly basis.

sentence: DAUs represented approximately 66% of the 2.85 billion monthly active users in March.

sentence: Turning to the financials.

sentence: All comparisons are on a year-over-year basis, unless otherwise noted.

sentence: Q1 total revenue was $26.2 billion, up 48% or 44% on a constant currency basis.

sentence: And had foreign exchange rates remained constant with Q1 of last year, total revenue would have been $706 million lower.

sentence: The growth in advertising revenue was largely driven by continued strength in product verticals such as online commerce.

sentence: Our year-over-year ad revenue growth also benefited from lapping pandemic-related demand headwinds experienced during March of last year.

sentence: In Q1, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased 12%, and the average price per ad increased 30%.

sentence: Lastly, G&A expenses increased 2% with growth in employee-related costs partially offset by lapping higher bad debt expenses related to COVID in the first quarter of last year.

sentence: We added over 2,000 net new hires in Q1, primarily in technical functions.

sentence: First-quarter operating income was $11.4 billion, representing a 43% operating margin.

sentence: Capital expenditures, including capital leases, were $4.4 billion, driven by investments in data centers, servers, network infrastructure, and office facilities.

sentence: We repurchased $4.1 billion of our Class A common stock in the first quarter, and we ended the quarter with $64.2 billion in cash and marketable securities.

sentence: In terms of sustainability, I'm pleased to report that Facebook's global operations have now reached net zero emissions and are 100% supported by renewable energy.

sentence: This is an important milestone for our business, but we also recognize there's more work to do in the years ahead.

sentence: And we remain committed to our next goal of decarbonizing our entire value chain in 2030.

sentence: Additional information on our ongoing efforts across environmental, social, and governance areas can be found in our recently filed proxy statement.

sentence: It includes things like #BuyBlack collections in the Facebook and Instagram shop tabs and a weekly #BuyBlack Friday show with live shopping segments from up-and-coming Black-owned small businesses.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to close by saying how grateful I am to our partners around the world and to our incredible teams who are working so hard to help people and businesses throughout this period.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Now, here's Dave.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Thanks, Sheryl, and good afternoon, everyone.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We delivered solid results in the third quarter in the face of a challenging mobile platform landscape and an evolving macroeconomic environment.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Let's begin with our community metrics.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our global community continued to grow even as we lap elevated user growth in the third quarter of last year related to the pandemic.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We estimate that approximately 2.8 billion people used at least one of our services on a daily business -- basis in September, and that approximately 3.6 billion people used at least one on a monthly basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Facebook daily active users reached 1.93 billion, up six percent or 110 million compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: DAUs represented approximately 66 percent or 2.91 billion monthly active users in September.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: MAUs grew by 170 million or six percent compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning to the financials.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: All comparisons are on a year-over-year basis unless otherwise noted.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q3 total revenue was $29 billion, up 35 percent or 34 percent on a constant currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We benefited from a currency tailwind, and had foreign currency -- foreign exchange rates remained constant with Q3 of last year, total revenue would have been $259 million lower.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q3 ad revenue was $28.3 billion, up 33 percent or 32 percent on a constant currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: On a user geography basis, year-over-year ad revenue growth was strongest in Rest of World at 50 percent.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Europe, North America, and Asia Pacific grew 35 percent, 31 percent, and 28 percent, respectively.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Europe, Asia Pacific, and Rest of World benefited from currency tailwinds, though to a lesser degree than in the prior quarter.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In Q3, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased nine percent, the average price per ad increased 22 percent.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Compression growth was driven primarily by developing markets, especially in Asia Pacific.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Pricing growth benefited from advertiser demand and lapping COVID-related pricing weakness during the third quarter of last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Though as Sheryl noted, growth was hindered by three primary headwinds.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: First, advertising spend was negatively impacted by performance and measurement headwinds related to Apple's ATT changes.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Second, we are seeing some macro headwinds as growth in online commerce has moderated from the elevated levels experienced earlier in the pandemic and businesses faced supply chain disruptions.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Third, COVID resurgences in Southeast Asia have led to additional lockdowns and a curtailment of economic activity.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Other revenue was $734 million, up 195 percent, driven by strong Quest 2 sales.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to expenses.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q3 total expenses were $18.6 billion, up 38 percent compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In terms of the specific line items, cost of revenue increased 38 percent, driven mostly by consumer hardware costs, core infrastructure investments, and payments to partners.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: R and D increased 33 percent, driven primarily by hiring to support our core products and consumer hardware efforts.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Marketing and sales increased 32 percent, mainly driven by marketing spend and hiring.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Lastly, G and A expenses increased 65 percent, driven primarily by higher legal-related costs and employee-related costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We added over 4,700 net new hires in Q3, primarily in technical functions.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We ended the quarter with over 68,100 full-time employees, up 28 percent -- up 20 percent compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Third-quarter operating income was $10.4 billion, representing a 36 percent operating margin.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our tax rate was 13 percent.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Net income was $9.2 billion or $3.22 per share.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Capital expenditures, including finance leases were $4.5 billion, driven by investments in data centers, servers, network infrastructure, and office facilities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Free cash flow is $9.5 billion and we ended the quarter with $58.1 billion in cash and marketable securities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We repurchased $14.4 billion of our Class A common stock in the third quarter and had $8 billion remaining on our prior authorization as of September 30th.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Today, we announced a $50 billion increase in our stock repurchase authorization.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Starting with our results for the fourth quarter of 2021, we plan to break out Facebook Reality Labs or FRL as a separate reporting segment.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: As we've discussed, we are dedicating significant resources toward our augmented and virtual reality products and services, which are an important part of our work to develop the next generation of online social experiences.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The new segment disclosures will provide additional information on the performance of FRL and the investments we are making.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Under this reporting structure, we'll provide revenue and operating profit for two segments.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The first segment, family of apps, will include Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, and other services.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The second segment, Facebook Reality Labs, will include augmented and virtual reality-related hardware, software, and content.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: As Mark noted, we expect our investment in FRL to reduce our overall operating profit in 2021 by approximately $10 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We are committed to bringing this long-term vision to life and we expect to increase our investments for the next several years.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Ahead of the fourth-quarter earnings call, we will share additional details about the reported -- reporting format of our segments' financials.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the revenue outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect fourth-quarter 2021 total revenue to be in the range of $31.5 billion to $34 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our outlook reflects the significant uncertainty we face in the fourth quarter in light of continued headwinds from Apple's iOS 14 changes and macroeconomic- and COVID-related factors.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In addition, we expect non-ads revenue to be down year over year in the fourth quarter as we lap the strong launch of Quest 2 during last year's holiday shopping season.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: As previously noted, we also continue to monitor developments regarding the viability of transatlantic data transfers and their potential impact on our European operations.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the expense outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2021 total expenses to be in the range of $70 billion to $71 billion, updated from our prior outlook of $70 billion to $73 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We anticipate our full-year 2022 total expenses will be in the range of $91 billion to $97 billion, driven by investments in technical and product talent and infrastructure-related costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2021 capital expenditures to be approximately $19 billion, updated from our prior estimate of $19 billion to $21 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: For 2022, we expect capital expenditures to be in the range of $29 billion to $34 billion, driven by our investments in data centers, servers, network infrastructure, and office facilities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: A large factor driving the increase in capex spend is an investment in our AI and machine learning capabilities, which we expect to benefit our efforts in ranking and recommendations for experiences across our products, including in feed and video, as well as improving ads performance and relevance.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect our Q4 2021 tax rate to be in the high teens.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Absent any changes to US tax law, we would expect our full-year tax rate in 2022 to be similar to the full-year 2021 rate.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Please note that our outlook for 2022 expenses, capital expenditures, and tax rate are preliminary estimates as we have not yet finalized our 2022 budget.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In closing, this was another solid quarter for our business despite facing some headwinds.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And we believe the investments we're making in our current services, as well as new products and experiences, will enable us to remain the best place for people to connect and for businesses to advertise, both now and in the years ahead With that, France, let's open up the call for questions.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And, you know, currently, we're seeing good growth globally, you know, strength in a number of different markets.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: But we've been making, you know, a lot of progress on Reels and have been happy with it, you know, on Instagram.

speaker: Dave Wehner

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: On the monetization front, we're just starting to roll out ads in Instagram, so it's earlier on that front and we really haven't gotten to a monetization point with Reels on Facebook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Sheryl, did you want to take the iOS 14 question?

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Yeah, I can take that.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I mean, when you start at the top of this, you really have to think about what personalized ads are, and we think they're better for people and businesses and they're especially important to small businesses.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: They also can be delivered, can be done in a very privacy-safe way.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: There are two big challenges coming from these iOS changes.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: The one is targeting and one is measurement.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I'm taking the second one first.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On measurement, we think we can address more than half of that underreporting by the end of the year and make more progress in the years ahead.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We estimate we're underreporting iOS web conversions.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We believe that real-world conversions like sales and app installs are higher.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And so, we have to do the work to help clients measure these properly in order for them to really understand the outcomes they're getting and improving performance.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And again, we think we can get, you know, a good chunk of that in this year and more in the next year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Targeting is a longer-term challenge.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our direct-response products are built on user-level conversions.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And as a result of the iOS changes, we don't see the same level of conversion data coming through.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So, we have to rebuild our targeting and optimization systems to work with less data.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So, this is a multi-year effort.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're developing privacy-enhancing technology to minimize the amount of personal information we learn and using more aggregate or anonymous data, while still allowing us to show those relevant personalized ads and measure of effectiveness.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In order for this to really work and benefit all businesses, it can require some cross-industry collaboration and more commerce tools and those are going to be longer-term efforts.

sentence: Maybe, Sheryl, following up there in terms of thinking, in terms of quarters or years on both the targeting and the measurement piece, can you help us just go one level lower in terms of what you're building, in terms of what's in your control to put on into the advertising ecosystem versus what might just take time for advertisers to adopt and get comfortable with and better understand the data that drive their business outcomes and how they allocate advertising budget?

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're building some of our own commerce tools and those are tools we can build that we need other people to adopt.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And then some of the targeting opportunities we see offset, take, you know, tools we can build or tools we can build in industry collaboration.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're really working as part of several industry collaborative groups on what those tools will look like and how those get adopted.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: So, those, obviously, take more partnership and are less in our direct control.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: On the outlook on expenses in 2022, you know, it's, obviously, early but we wanted to give an, you know, an initial outlook of our expected expense range since we typically do that in Q3.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: You know, Mark outlined we have a lot of priorities that we're investing against across the business.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: That includes, you know, a lot of areas in the core sort of family of apps but also in apparel.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We've got a lot of priorities in, you know, advertising, AI, commerce, privacy.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: So, when you kind of pull all these things together, we've got a pretty robust spending plan next year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The, you know, primary driver is going to be accelerating headcount growth in 2022.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: So, that's going to be something you'll see headcount coming in above 20 percent, obviously, that we have this quarter.

speaker: Doug Anmuth
sentence: Mark, just given the significant investments in both P and L expenses and capex, and clearly, you're talking about the heavy focus on metaverse over the long term, just hoping you could help us recap kind of the 1-year, 3-year, and then 5-year aspirations from a product perspective as you've done in the past.

speaker: Doug Anmuth
