sentence: Do you have any commentary on revenue growth in '22 to go along with that?

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I can talk about the metaverse and Reality Labs part of this.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So, for the next, you know, one, three years, especially, I think what you'll see is us putting more of the foundational pieces into place.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This is not an investment that is going to be profitable for us anytime in the near future.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But, you know, we basically believe that the metaverse is going to be the successor of the mobile internet, that it's going to enable social experiences that are the ultimate expression of what we try to build, which is allowing people to feel really present with the people they care about no matter where they actually are.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So, we think it's going to unlock a massively larger creative economy of both digital and physical goods that would exist today and allow millions of people to be able to do work doing what they love and enabling a whole different economy around that that I think is going to be another important pillar of our business over the next decade.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So, on the next, you know, one to three years, you know, I mean, I almost -- I wouldn't focus on the sort of business outcomes there quite as much as I would just, you know, that the products and the infrastructure that we're putting in place.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So, there's -- there are new platforms, there's hardware components, there's the whole virtual reality product line, there's the augmented reality product line.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: You know, we're kind of starting to put those pieces in place.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: There's the operating system and development models for all these new creative tools.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: There's the commerce part of what we're doing around this and how they time to the broader commerce effort across family of apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And then there's all the social platform work that we're doing with our Horizon effort that touches a bunch of different areas of what we're doing.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But I think you'll see all of those pieces start to be built out and start to mature a bit over the next few years.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And then, you know, if we do a good job on this, and I would say later in this decade, is when we would sort of expect this to be more of a real business story.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But I think what we kind of think about it for the near term is are we delivering the product experiences that are completely groundbreaking and that people try this latest thing, that is amazing and can see a glimpse of where this is going.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And that will pave the way for the future.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The business North Star that I mentioned in my opening remarks are, you know, we hope that by the end of the decade that we can, you know, help a billion people use the metaverse and support hundreds of billions of dollars of digital commerce.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I think if we can do that, then this will be a good investment over there for the long term.

speaker: Dave Wehner

sentence: I think Reels is a big part of that strategy and, you know, we've now got that -- we've got that rolled out in over 100 countries since launching in August of last year.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So, I think that that's going to be a big part of the focus here.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And as we'll -- I'm excited over the next, you know, year or two to see how that grow into something.

sentence: And we've been steadily working on this and onboarding more creators and more people to it and we're adding more worlds all the time.

sentence: Our total ad revenue in Q4 was 32.6 billion, which is up 20% year over year.

sentence: Throughout 2021, we saw solid growth, which continued in Q4.

sentence: But there were a number of dynamic factors that created headwinds for us this past quarter in addition to those Mark described around competition and our shift to short-form video.

sentence: We were lapping a period of strong demand in 2020 that benefited from very strong growth in online commerce, which has since slowed.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg

sentence: We've also heard from advertisers about other macro trends that contributed to the headwinds in Q4, including global supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, and inflationary pressures.

sentence: Like others in our industry, we faced headwinds as a result of Apple iOS changes.

sentence: As we described last quarter, Apple created two challenges for advertisers: one is that the accuracy of our ads targeting decreased, which increased the cost of driving outcomes; the other is that measuring those outcomes became more difficult.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg

sentence: We brought Shops to Groups, and we started testing Live Shopping for creators, an early glimpse of the immersive shopping experiences that will be possible in the metaverse.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our commerce strategy remains focused on three areas: continuing to be the best place for advertisers to find customers and get strong ROI; making it easier to sell on our platform; and improving the customer experience.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We still have a lot of work to do compared to other mobile and web shopping experiences, but we're seeing promising early signs.

sentence: It's great to see businesses and consumers using social and immersive shopping experiences like Product tags, Drops, and Live Shopping.

sentence: In November, they launched exclusively on Instagram for 24 hours and hosted a Live Shopping event: a conversation between John Mayer and Laundress co-founder Lindsey Julia Boyd, where people could buy the new products as they talked about them live.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Overall, we're pleased with the engagement we saw with our commerce tools over the holiday season and view Q4 as a promising milestone in our multiyear journey.

sentence: And we've seen lots of demand from consumers who want to use our messaging apps for everyday services like utilities, financial services, education, and travel.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're continuing to invest in new tools to make it easier for people to help and make purchases right from a chat.

sentence: In the future, I think that people will increasingly turn to AI-based discovery engines to entertain them, teach them things and connect them with people who share their interests.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I believe that our investments in AI, all the different types of content we support, and our work to build the best platform for creators to make a living will increasingly set our services apart from the rest of the industry and drive our success.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we're also finding that having an ambitious vision around building the world's discovery engine is attracting a lot of the most talented AI folks to work on this program.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Next, let's talk about Ads.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Sheryl will discuss this in more detail, but I want to highlight that this is also a large AI investment for us.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: There are three main trends to highlight in our Ads business right now.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: First, we're managing headwinds from the shift to short-form video that I just mentioned.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: In the near term, this is a drag on revenue because real monetization is less than theater stories.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But I expect that that will improve over time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We've seen this type of media format transition multiple times before.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Back in 2012, when we transition from desktop feed to mobile feed, we saw mobile feed growing massively, but not monetizing well yet, and we leaned into it, went through some tough quarters, and then it became the foundation of our business today.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Similarly, in 2018, when people started using Stories more instead of Feed, but Stories didn't monetize as well as Feed yet, we still doubled down on Stories, had another tough period but came out stronger than ever.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we've run this play before, and we're running it again now.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're focused on growing Reels as a major part of the discovery engine vision and we expect that this expansion and engagement to shift from a short-term headwind to a tailwind at some point.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now while this is playing out, we're also managing the headwinds from signal loss that we've discussed a lot recently.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This means growing first-party understanding of what people are interested in by making it easier for people to engage with businesses and our apps, whether that's completing purchases on Facebook or Instagram or messaging businesses on WhatsApp or Messenger.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: It also means making sure that we build the best privacy-enhancing technologies to provide accurate targeting and measurement to advertisers, even when purchases aren't happening within our apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're making major AI investments to build the most advanced models and infrastructure in the industry.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Over the next year or two, we hope that this drives better recommendations for people, higher returns for advertisers, and increases our revenue growth, even in the face of signal loss.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Over the longer term, I think that these large technology investments can provide a sustainable competitive advantage over others in the industry.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The last priority that I want to discuss today is the Metaverse.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Because while we're focusing on the biggest opportunities and challenges of today, I think it's important to build the foundation for the next era of social technology as well.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The centerpiece of our strategy is the social platform that we're starting to build with Horizon.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: It's still early, but as we build out the experience, the next focus will be on growing the community.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We plan to launch a web version of Horizon later this year that will make it easy for people to step into the Metaverse experiences from a lot more platforms, even without needing a headset.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I think the best experience will be on virtual and eventually, augmented reality platforms, and especially on our platform like Quest, where, in an upcoming release, from the moment you put on your headset, you're going to be embodied with your Meta avatar and ready to interact in a horizon with your friends right from your Quest home.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But making this available everywhere will mean that you can interact with anyone on whatever devices or platform that they want to use.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our other focus for Horizon is building out the Metaverse economy and helping creators make a living, working in the Metaverse.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We expect to be meaningfully better at monetization than others in the space and we think that that should become a sustainable advantage for our platforms as they develop.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: On the hardware side, Meta Quest 2 continues to be the leading virtual reality headset.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Later this year, we'll release a higher-end headset code-named Project Cambria, which will be more focused on work use cases and eventually replacing your laptop or work setup.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This premium device will have improved ergonomics and full color pass-through mixed reality to seamlessly blend virtual reality with the physical world.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're also building in eye tracking and face tracking, so that your avatar can make eye contact and facial expressions, which dramatically improves your sense of presence.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: It's also a good example of why we're developing hardware in addition to the social platforms.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're bringing Horizon to more platforms, but if you want to be able to make eye contact or have your physical facial expressions just automatically get translated to avatar in real time, then our hardware will provide the best Metaverse experience, whether you're playing a game or meeting with coworkers in Horizon workrooms.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We'll share more details about Project Cambria in the months ahead as we get ready to launch it.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I believe the areas that we've discussed today are the right places for us to be doubling down on our work.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The questions we face are not going to be resolved overnight.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But we've also faced a number of these challenges before, so I'm confident that we can navigate this period while continuing to invest in our future.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I'm grateful for everyone on our team who is executing on this important work for our partners and for our investors who believe in us and the future that we're building together.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And now, here is Sheryl.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Thanks, Mark, and hi, everyone.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our total ad revenue in Q1 was $27 billion, which is up 6% year over year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We saw solid growth in APAC and Rest of World, but a more challenging environment in North America and Europe.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Despite the headwinds Mark described a moment ago, we saw meaningful growth in areas like video ads and click-to-messaging ads.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: The changes to the ads landscape over the last year have caused significant disruptions to the way many businesses advertise online.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our teams are working closely with our partners to help them navigate this new environment so they can continue to get great return on investment.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we're focused on building products and tools that grow their businesses and ours over the long term.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to pick up on what Mark said about our ad strategy.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: As he described, it's focused on three main areas: one, growing video monetization, especially short-form video like Reels; two, evolving our ad systems to do more with less data; and three, investing in AI and machine learning to support our ads infrastructure.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Half of the time spent on Facebook is video and video services on Facebook were a significant source of revenue growth in the first quarter.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: People already watch a lot of longer-form video content that's eligible for industry ads, which we monetize well.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Stories monetization continues to grow across Facebook and Instagram.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And with Reels growing quickly, there's also a big opportunity as we get better at monetizing short-form video over time.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We've accelerated our efforts to improve the Reels ad format.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our experience monetizing Stories is directly applicable here.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're leveraging what we learned with Stories ads to create ads for Reels that have a native format, perform well and are easy for advertisers to create.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're working closely with our partners to help them make the most of the opportunity with video, like experimenting with new formats and with campaigns that utilize multiple types of video ads.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: A great example is the U.S. restaurant chain Wendy's.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: They used a range of video formats across Feeds, Stories, Reels, and in-stream to promote their March Madness campaign, driving consumers to the first virtual Wendy's restaurant in Horizon Worlds.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We also worked with them to promote the campaign in Horizon World itself, with a virtual welcome screen directing people to what they called the Wendyverse.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: The campaign was a big success, reaching 52 million people and improving Wendy's brand and message awareness across a number of metrics.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Second, evolving our ad system.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our focus is on paving the way for the next era of personalized advertising, and there's work we're doing over the near, medium, and long term.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In the near term, we're working closely with advertisers to help them navigate the new landscape, while we evolve and improve our ad solutions.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: For example, we're encouraging partners to integrate with our conversions API to create a direct, reliable, and privacy safe connection between their marketing data and Meta.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we've recently introduced a faster and easier way for SMBs to integrate with it called the Conversions API Gateway.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: One way we're helping advertisers get better insights with less data is with conversion modeling.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This can help them understand measurement and campaign performance, even when we're not able to see or aggregate certain conversions.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're also helping businesses connect directly with customers and grow more on-site data conversions through products like click-to-message ads.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This is where you click on an ad on your Facebook or Instagram feed and it opens a chat with the business in Messenger, Instagram Direct, or WhatsApp.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's already a multibillion-dollar business with healthy double-digit year-over-year growth in Q1.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: A great example is Deichmann, Europe's largest footwear retailer.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: They've built a fully automated virtual shoe assistant to give customers personalized footwear recommendations and promoted it through Click-to-Messenger ads on Facebook.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: They had an 85% click-through rate and saw 30% more incremental purchases than with their usual link ads.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In the medium term, we see an opportunity to grow other on-site conversion products like lead ads, which make it easier for businesses to generate leads and shop ads, which direct you to a brand's digital storefront on Facebook or Instagram.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's still very early for shop ads, but we think driving people to shops can be a compelling objective for commerce advertisers as we continue to improve our on-site commerce tools.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Over the longer run, we're also developing privacy-enhancing technologies, which will help us minimize the amount of personal information we process, while still allowing us to show people relevant ads and measure performance for advertisers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we're collaborating across our industry on these and other standards that will support this next era of personalized advertising.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Third, AI and machine learning, which are crucial components of these privacy-enhancing technologies and will drive improvements over time to our ads ranking and measurement capabilities.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're significantly increasing our investment in AI and machine learning across the company this year, and a large portion of this is going toward ads.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We continue to innovate in order to deliver better-performing ads in general, and these investments will help us do that while processing less individual-level data.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We also have a range of automated tools to make it easier for advertisers to create, manage and improve the performance of their ad campaigns.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're constantly working to improve these tools and make them simpler for advertisers to use.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Taken together, we think our range of solutions can help advertisers get better results now and over the longer term.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're confident our apps will continue to be the best places for advertisers to reach people where they get measurable outcomes long into the future.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: As ever, I want to say thank you to our partners, large and small, and to our teams, who are working so hard to deliver great results for businesses everywhere.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Now here's Dave.

sentence: Thanks, Sheryl, and good afternoon, everyone.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Let's begin with our consolidated results.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: All comparisons are on a year-over-year basis, unless otherwise noted.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q1 total revenue was $27.9 billion, up 7% or 10% on a constant currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Had foreign exchange rates remained constant with Q1 of last year, total revenue would have been about $893 million higher.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q1 total expenses were $19.4 billion, up 31% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In terms of specific line items, cost of revenue increased 17%, driven primarily by core infrastructure investments, payments to partners, and content-related costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: R&D increased 48%, mainly driven by hiring to support family of apps and Reality Labs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Marketing and sales increased 16%, mainly driven by hiring and marketing spend.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And lastly, G&A increased 45%, driven mainly by legal-related costs and employee-related costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We added over 5,800 net new hires in Q1, the majority in technical functions.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We ended the quarter with over 77,800 full-time employees, up 28% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The first-quarter operating income was $8.5 billion, representing a 31% operating margin.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our tax rate was 16%, net income was $7.5 billion or $2.72 per share.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Capital expenditures, including payments -- principal payments on finance leases were $5.5 billion, driven by investments in data centers, servers, network infrastructure, and office facilities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Free cash flow was $8.5 billion, we repurchased $9.4 billion of our Class A common stock in the first quarter, and we ended the quarter with $43.9 billion in cash and marketable securities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Now moving to our segment results.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: I'll begin with the family of apps segment.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q1 total family of apps revenue was $27.2 billion, up 6%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q1 family of apps ad revenue was $27 billion, up 6% or 10% on a constant currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Growth decelerated from the fourth quarter due to a variety of factors.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Prior to the war in Ukraine, we faced expected headwinds related to the continued slowdown in our online e-commerce vertical, which had grown quickly during the COVID-19 pandemic as well as ongoing targeting and measurement challenges impacting advertising spend.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We experienced a further deceleration in growth following the start of the Ukraine war due to the loss of revenue in Russia as well as a reduction in advertising demand, both within Europe and outside the region.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We believe that war introduced further volatility into an already uncertain macroeconomic landscape for advertisers.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Foreign exchange rates were also a headwind to growth in the quarter.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: On a user geography basis, year-over-year ad revenue growth was strongest in Rest of World and Asia Pacific at 21% and 20%, respectively; North America grew 1%; and Europe was flat year over year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Europe advertising revenue was disproportionately challenged by the factors related to the war in Ukraine.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In Q1, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased 15% and the average price per ad decreased 8%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Impression growth was driven primarily by Asia Pacific and Rest of World.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The year-over-year decline in pricing was driven primarily by the ongoing mix shift in ad impressions toward regions and services that monetize at lower rates.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Family of apps other revenue was $215 million, up 9% as revenue growth from the WhatsApp business API offset a decline in payments-related revenue earned from Games.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: family of apps expenses were $15.7 billion, up 27%, driven mainly by employee-related expenses, infrastructure costs and legal costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: family of apps operating income was $11.5 billion, representing a 42% operating margin.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: we estimate that approximately 2.9 billion people use at least one of our family of apps on a daily basis in March and that approximately 3.6 billion people use at least one on a monthly basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Facebook daily active users were 1.96 billion, up 4% or 82 million compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: DAUs represented approximately 67% of the 2.94 billion monthly active users in March.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: MAUs grew by 83 million or 3% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Europe DAUs and MAUs declined sequentially and were negatively impacted by the loss of users in Russia following the government's block of Facebook in the country.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect this trend to continue in the second quarter and this will likely cause global MAU to be flat to down sequentially.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Within our Reality Labs segment, Q1 revenue was $695 million, up 30%, driven by Quest 2 sales.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Reality Labs expenses were $3.7 billion, up 55% driven by employee-related costs, R&D operating expenses, and cost of goods sold.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Reality Labs operating loss was $3 billion in the first quarter.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect second quarter 2022 total revenue to be in the range of $28 billion to $30 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: This outlook reflects a continuation of the trends impacting revenue growth in the first quarter, including softness in the back half of the first quarter that coincided with the war in Ukraine.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our guidance assumes foreign currency will be approximately a 3% headwind to year-over-year growth in the second quarter based on current exchange rates.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In addition, as noted on previous calls, we continue to monitor developments regarding the viability of transatlantic data transfer and their potential impact on our European operations, and we are pleased with the progress on a political agreement.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the expense outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2022 total expenses to be in the range of $87 billion to $92 billion, lowered from our prior outlook of $90 billion to $95 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2022 expense growth to be driven primarily by the family of apps segment followed by Reality Labs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2022 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases to be in the range of $29 billion to $34 billion, unchanged from our prior estimate.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Absent any changes to U.S. tax law, we expect our full year 2022 tax rate to be above the Q1 rate and in the high teens.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In closing, our advertisers are adjusting to a new digital advertising landscape brought about by recent mobile platform changes, while navigating a complex set of macroeconomic challenges.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Given the resulting revenue headwinds, we have adjusted our plans for hiring and expense growth this year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We continue to see a lot of opportunity across our investment priorities and remain committed to dedicating additional talent and capital toward these areas while ensuring our investment plans are appropriately calibrated to the operating environment.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: With that, France, let's open up the call for questions.

sentence: In terms of cannibalization, Reels does pull time away from other surfaces, but we do believe it's additive to overall engagement.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And so we're seeing a similar pattern there.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: But if you look back, engagement for both Facebook and Instagram, remain above the levels they were at pre-pandemic and that's true both globally and in the U.S. So I think we're pleased with that.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: On the capex front, let me just sort of address the overall ramp.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: It's true we are investing significantly in AI and machine learning investments to power ranking and recommendations for things like Ads, Reels, and Feed.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And so that does add to the capex intensity of the business.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And we do think there is additional capital intensity of the business as we make significant investments in AI and machine learning on top of just additional capacity growth.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We're not sharing an outlook beyond 2022 at this point.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: France, you can go to the next question.

sentence: Operator Our next question is Eric Sheridan with Goldman Sachs.

sentence: Please go ahead.

speaker: Eric Sheridan
sentence: Thank you so much for taking the question.

speaker: Eric Sheridan
sentence: Maybe one big picture and one more micro question.

speaker: Eric Sheridan
sentence: Mark, I think one of the questions we get the most from investors is when you think about where you're trying to go with the Metaverse longer term, how do you think about the investment cycle versus the monetization cycle when you think about creating hardware, both on the physical side and the distribution layer for hardware versus the content and the creator cycle you need to solve for on the Metaverse over the medium to long term?

speaker: Eric Sheridan
sentence: And second, I don't know if I missed it or not, but I think last quarter, you called out on the Apple privacy changes, that the headwind might get worse in Q1 than it was in Q4.

speaker: Eric Sheridan
sentence: Can you give us an update on how those headwinds continue to evolve?

speaker: Eric Sheridan
sentence: And whether what you over the last couple of years have somewhat future-proofed against future changes that Apple might make in the iOS ecosystem?

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Yes, I can give some context on the first one, and then Dave can speak to the second question.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I think that the cycle here between investment and meaningful enough revenue growth to be near or very profitable is going to be long.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I think it's going to be longer for Reality Labs than for a lot of the traditional software that we've built.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And if you think about -- just a bit of context that may be useful on why we've ramped expenses so much is especially with the success that we've seen with Quest 2, we're now basically funding product teams to be building our future products, two or three versions into the future.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Because when you're designing hardware, it's -- these are multiyear plans that you're building and kind of figuring out all the pieces that are going to go into that.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So we have multiple teams in parallel that we've sort of now spun up.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This goes for VR as well as augmented reality and the other work that we're doing and is sort of driven by the success that we feel like we're seeing in the markets and the technology is starting to be ready to really ramp up.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So those expenses, we're experiencing today.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I mean, having those teams operating is something that you see weigh on the results and is one of the reasons why I think the growth rates and expenses have been so high, and I think we'll continue investing more over some period.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But at some point, we will have all those product teams fully staffed for a few versions into the future and then the growth rates there will come down.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But it's not going to be until those products really hit the market and scale in a meaningful way and this market ends up being big that this will be a big revenue or profit contributor to the business.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So that's why I've given the color on past calls that I expect us to be later this decade, right?

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Maybe primarily, this is laying the groundwork for what I expect to be a very exciting 2030s when this is like -- when this is sort of more established as the primary computing platform at that point.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I think that there will be results along the way for that, too.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But I do think that this is going to be a longer cycle.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Some of the software parts of what we're doing in the Metaverse will, I think, have near-term opportunities to monetize.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I think we'll see how that goes.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Certainly, Horizon will roll out across all platforms and there will be a number of things that we can do there that will have shorter cycles that might resemble a little bit more what we're used to with apps.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But overall, I think that that's kind of the context that I want everyone to have on that.

sentence: Eric, I'll take the second part -- the second question that you had.

sentence: We expect -- we've expected ongoing privacy headwinds from the iOS changes, and we continue to see them.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Those are obviously factored into our Q2 outlook, along with the impact on demand that we're seeing from things like the war in Ukraine.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: More specifically, ATT continues to be a headwind, but we're also seeing incremental headwinds from iOS 15 and other regulatory changes.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And again, we factored all of those headwinds into our Q2 outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Of course, any outlook on platform headwinds depends in part on the platforms themselves and how they write and enforce their policies.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: So I'd sort of put that caveat in as well.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: When you look at what we're doing to mitigate those near-term, we're working on improvements to our current solutions and Sheryl talked about some of those like privacy-enhanced technologies.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Medium term, we see the opportunity to move clients more toward on-site conversions.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We're seeing a lot of success in things like Click-to-Messaging ads, lead gen ads and then more nascent effort in shop ads.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And then longer term, we're rebuilding our ads stack to employ more machine learning and AI to be more effective at ads with less data.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: So we think we've got a response that we're building into the new environment, and we're optimistic about the future.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now on our last call, I discussed that based on the revenue growth we were seeing in 2021, we kicked off a number of multiyear projects to accelerate our business.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I still believe that these projects are important.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But given the more recent revenue trajectory that we're seeing, we are slowing the pace of these investments and pushing some expenses that would have come in the next year or two off to a somewhat longer time line.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And given the continued trends, this is even more of a focus now than it was last quarter.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our plan is to steadily reduce headcount growth over the next year.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Many teams are going to shrink so we can shift energy to other areas inside the company.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I want to give our leaders the ability to decide within their teams where to double down, where to backfill attrition and where to restructure teams while minimizing thrash to the long-term initiatives.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The fact that we hired a lot of people earlier this year means that our reported year-over-year headcount growth will still be substantial for the next few quarters, but it should continue to decline over time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now this is a period that demands more intensity, and I expect us to get more done with fewer resources.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We're currently going through the process of increasing the goals for many of our efforts.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Previously challenging periods have been transformational for our company and helped us develop our next generation of leaders.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I expect this period to be no different.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I expect that we're going to find a way to keep investing in our top priority areas.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I think we're going to come through this period as a stronger and more disciplined organization.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now next, I want to discuss how we're doing in our high-priority areas.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: To understand where we're going, it's important to keep in mind that there are two major technological waves that we're riding in our business.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The first wave of driving our business today is AI, and then the second longer-term wave is the emergence of the metaverse.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: One of the main transformations in our business right now is that social feeds are going from being driven primarily by the people and accounts you follow to increasingly also being driven by AI recommending content that you'll find interesting from across Facebook or Instagram, even if you don't follow those creators.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Social content from people you know is going to remain an important part of the experience and some of our most differentiated content.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But increasingly, we'll also be able to supplement that with other interesting content from across our networks.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Reels is one part of this trend that focuses on the growth of short-form video as a content format.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But this overall AI trend is much broader and covers all types of content, including text, images, links, group content and more.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And building a recommendation system across all these types of content is something that we're uniquely focused on.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Right now, about 15% of content in a person's Facebook feed and a little more than that of their Instagram feed is recommended by our AI, from people, groups, or accounts that you don't follow.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we expect these numbers to more than double by the end of next year.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: As our AI finds additional content that people will find interesting, that increases engagement and the quality of our feeds.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And since we're already efficient in monetizing most of these formats, this should increase our business opportunity over that period as well.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Reels engagement is also growing quickly.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I shared last quarter that Reels already made up 20% of the time that people spend on Instagram.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This quarter, we saw a more than 30% increase in the time that people spent engaging with Reels across Facebook and Instagram.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: AI advances are driving a lot of these improvements.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And one example is that after launching a new large AI model for recommendations, we saw a 15% increase in watch time in the Reels video player on Facebook alone.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So I think that there are many improvements like this that we're going to be able to continue to make.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: As we are building out our discovery engine though, I want to be clear that we are still ultimately a social company focused on helping people connect.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: One social trend that we're seeing is that instead of people just interacting in comments in their feeds, most people find interesting content in their feeds then they message -- and then they message that content to friends and interact here.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And this creates this flywheel of discovery and then social connection and then inspiring those people to create more content themselves.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: In Instagram, for example, we see that Reels makes up more than half of content reshared into messages.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So our strategy isn't about public versus social content and interaction.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: It's really about enabling a flywheel that compounds both.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We faced a number of challenges here in the near term, but the investments that we're making should give us a comparative advantage over the longer term.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: One near-term challenge is the growth of short-form video.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Reels doesn't yet monetize at the same rate as Feed or Stories.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So in the near term, the faster that Reels grows, the more revenue that actually displaces from higher monetizing surfaces.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now in theory, we could mitigate the short-term headwind by pushing less hard on growing Reels, but that would be worse for our products and business longer term since we're confident that Reels will grow engagement overall and quality and will eventually monetize closer to Feed.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Our work on ads monetization efficiency for Reels is actually making faster progress than we'd expected.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: We've now crossed a $1 billion annual revenue run rate for Reels ads, and Reels also has a higher revenue run rate than Stories did at identical times post-launch.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So the bottom line is I think we're on track here and we just need to push through this one.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The second challenge that we face here is the signal loss from Apple's iOS changes.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And as I've discussed before, our approach here is to grow first-party understanding of people's interests by making it easier for people to engage with businesses in our own apps, whether that's through business messaging, shops or new ad products.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: For example, click to messaging as part of our business messaging strategy that's grown quickly with 40% of our advertisers already using this format.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The AI wave that we are riding is a tailwind for all of these solutions.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Advances in AI enable us to deliver better-personalized ads while using less data.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So it powers automated messaging and creation tools to let businesses run better-performing campaigns, which is particularly important for small businesses that don't have big marketing departments and that have been hit hard by Apple's policy changes.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now overall, there's a lot of work to do here and a lot of the investment is in AI compute capex.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But I'm confident that if we invest in building the new infrastructure that we need, then we're going to come out of this downturn with even more superior ad products and a meaningful technology advantage over other industry players.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now of course, the third challenge that we're facing here is the macro economy.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we can't control the timing of when things will bounce back, but I'll note that periods like this are when marketers reevaluate their budgets and are even more focused on finding the highest-performing advertising.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And in the last recession, we invested in our ads business through the downturn and came out stronger on the other side, and I'm focused on making sure that we do the same today.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now if AI is the major technological wave that we're riding today, then the last priority that I want to discuss is about the Metaverse technological wave that is currently building.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And the Metaverse is a massive opportunity for a number of reasons.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Most importantly, it enables deeper social experiences, where you feel a realistic sense of presence with other people, no matter where they are.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Whether you're playing games or working for hours at a time or if you're just jumping in for just a minute at a time to say hi to a friend or collaborate on a project quickly.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: By helping to develop these platforms, we're going to have the freedom to build these experiences the way that we and the overall industry believe will be best rather than being limited by the constraints that competitors place on us and on our community and on small businesses.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And given some of the product and business constraints that we face now, I feel even more strongly now that developing these platforms will unlock hundreds of billions of dollars, if not trillions over time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This is obviously a very expensive undertaking over the next several years.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: But as the metaverse becomes more important in every part of how we live from our social platforms and entertainment to work and education and commerce, I'm confident that we're going to be glad that we played an important role in building this.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: The next milestones to look out for here are the continued expansion of Horizon, our social metaverse platform, and the continued improvement of our Avatars platform, how you express yourself and interact in the metaverse as well as the commerce around that.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: These are some of the areas that we're most focused on.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we're going to be launching a web version of Horizon that will be accessible on all platforms later this year, which should dramatically increase the number of people who can use Horizon.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we also just launched our Avatars store with digital clothes from leading fashion houses.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we're going to continue expanding that selection and the fidelity of our Avatar system overall.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: On the hardware front, later this year, we'll release Project Cambria, and the experience here is getting pretty awesome.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: It will be a high-end device focused on professional users and work with high-resolution color mixed reality.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: I'm really looking forward to getting this one out.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: This is just one milestone in the long-term path, but I think people are going to be pretty blown away by this.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: So those are the areas that I'm most focused on right now and that I think are going to have the greatest impact on our products and business over the next few years and much longer.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Periods like this can be tough, but I really think that the additional focus and discipline are going to make us stronger over time.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Now in addition to our business, this is also a period of transition for our leadership team.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And before I hand it over to Sheryl for what will be her last earnings call, I want to thank her for everything that she has done for Meta, for our community, and for so many small businesses around the world.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: It's really hard to overstate how big of an impact that Sheryl has had on so many different parts of what we do and on me personally.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: At the same time, and Marne are our talented leaders who I've worked with closely for many years.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: They're the type of people who I've kept giving more and more responsibility to and they just keep crushing it, so the expanded roles are well deserved.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And I think that they're going to do a great job carrying our business forward and expanding it in some exciting new ways.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And we also shared the news this afternoon that Dave Wehner will be transitioning into a new role as our chief strategy officer, overseeing our strategy and corporate development teams.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Dave has done great work as our CFO, and I'm really looking forward to continuing to work with him in this new role.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: And as part of this, we're also promoting Susan Li to be Meta's new chief financial officer starting later this year.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: Susan is an incredibly talented executive and I think she'll be an excellent CFO.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: She already runs our financial planning process and plays an important role on our leadership team, and this transition is something that we've been working on for years.

speaker: Mark Zuckerberg
sentence: With that, I'm going to hand it over to Sheryl.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Thank you, Mark, for those kind words and for being a great leader and friend for the last 14 years.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It has been an enormous privilege to work for you to help build this remarkable company.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I'd like to focus on Q2 before making some wider observations about the business.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our total revenue in Q2 was $28.8 billion, a decrease of 1% year over year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Foreign exchange trends had a significant impact in Q2, in particular, the depreciation of the euro relative to the dollar.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: On a constant currency basis, we would have seen 3% revenue growth year over year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Similar to last quarter, we saw solid growth in APAC and other parts of the world outside of North America and Europe, where it's been a more challenging environment.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: These continue to be turbulent times for the global economy.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Many of the macro factors having an impact on our revenue are continuations of things we've seen in previous quarters, such as the continued impact of the war in Ukraine and the normalization of e-commerce after the pandemic peak.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: But there are also new challenges with rising inflation and uncertainty around a looming recession.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We know that recessions put pressure on marketers to make sure their ad budgets are spent in the smartest way possible.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're focused on helping them run efficient marketing campaigns to get the best possible return on investment, including helping them shift their ad strategies on our platform in line with user trends and our own evolving ad solutions.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to pick up on some of the themes Mark just touched on that show how we're doing this: Reels monetization, evolving our ad system, and AI and machine learning.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: First, Reels monetization.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We launched ads and Reels last year.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's growing quickly and we see it as an area where there is significant potential for growth in the future.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: It's going to take time but we have a playbook from our experience with Stories.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Our focus right now with Reels is ramping up ad load, improving performance and making sure the ads are easy for advertisers to create.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're also using AI to better understand the content being published in Reels, so users can connect to the content that is most relevant to them and marketers can also show more relevant ads.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: A good example of a brand seeing results with Reels ads is Wild Alaskan Company, a sustainable seafood delivery business that is consistently adopting and testing our latest ad tools.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: When they tested adding Reels to their campaign, they saw a 36% increase in return on ad spend, a similar uplift in new subscribers and a 26% lower cost per new subscriber.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Second, adapting our ad system to do more with less data.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: In the short and medium term, we're working to improve and evolve our ad solutions.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're helping advertisers improve the performance of their ads by growing on-site data conversions with products like lead ads, which make it easier for businesses to generate leads and with business messaging products like click-to-message ads, where you click on an ad in your Facebook or Instagram feed and it opens a chat with the business in Messenger, Instagram or WhatsApp.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Business messaging is an area where we see big potential.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We estimate that 1 billion users are messaging with a business each week across WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Click-to-message is already a multibillion-dollar business for us and we continue to see strong double-digit year-over-year growth.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: These ads are proving particularly popular with SMBs in emerging markets like Brazil and Mexico, many of whom are new advertisers to Meta who come to us to advertise solely in this format.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're making it easier to create these ads directly from the WhatsApp Business app, which will help small businesses looking to find customers and grow.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And big brands are incorporating business messaging into their campaigns like Paramount Studios, who used Click to Messenger to promote their blockbuster movie Top Gun Maverick and drive ticket sales.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: As more brands turn to messaging, paid messaging provides new ways to sell, support and market right on the chat thread.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're also investing in privacy-safe ways to improve targeting and measurement.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: For example, we're continuing to invest improving our conversions API, which creates a direct, reliable and privacy-safe connection between advertiser's marketing data and Meta.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And over the longer term, we're developing privacy-enhancing technologies to help minimize the personal information we process while still allowing us to show relevant ads and measure performance.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: One example is Private Lift, which we're currently beta testing with a number of large advertisers.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: This is a measurement solution which helps advertisers understand how their campaigns are performing while adding extra layers of privacy to limit the information that can be learned by the advertiser or Meta.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: While we develop these solutions, we're also collaborating across our industry on technologies and other standards that will support privacy-safe personalized advertising over the long term.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Third, on AI and machine learning.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to emphasize Mark's point that this is a really important part of how we improve our ads ranking and measurement capabilities.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: AI-driven products like advantage detailed targeting and advantaged look-alikes help to increase the audience for an ad campaign if it's likely to improve performance.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: AI is also an important part of how we continue to grow video monetization.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: A moment ago, I touched on how we're using it in Reels.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We've also launched AI-based tools to make it simpler to create video ads for Instagram Stories, and we're continuing to test ways for advertisers to transform static images with music and motion so they appear more like video.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Turning to the business more broadly.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: There's no doubt that we're going through a transition period and doing so at a time of global economic uncertainty.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: But despite the current challenges, I'm very confident for the long term.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We're facing a cyclical downturn but over the long run, the digital ad market will continue to grow.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Advertisers will go where they get the highest return on investment and ability to drive their business.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We believe we will continue to show up very favorably compared to other advertising options.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Meta is a company that has shown extraordinary resilience.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We have demonstrated time and time again that we are prepared to move quickly and at scale to respond to changes in consumer behavior, the macroeconomic landscape, and the needs of our advertising partners.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And we have demonstrated time and time again than when we build products, they scale globally.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We have made big transitions like the shift from desktop to mobile or from Feed to Stories.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: We innovate relentlessly and are always laser-focused on execution, delivering tools and products that help advertisers drive business results.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: The investments we're making in Reels, our discovery engine, business messaging, retooling our ad system, and especially in helping to build the metaverse represent enormous opportunities for our business and our partners.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to thank the teams that have helped us achieve remarkable success for our business and the millions of other businesses who have grown using our tools and products.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I want to thank our partners, large and small, who we learn from every day.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And I want to thank our investor community.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: Your support has helped us to be the innovative and resilient business that we are.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: I look forward to continuing to serve on Meta's board, where I'll have a front-row seat to Meta's success in the years ahead.

speaker: Sheryl Sandberg
sentence: And now here's my amazing colleague, Dave.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Thanks, Sheryl, and good afternoon, everyone.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Let's begin with our consolidated results.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: All comparisons are on a year-over-year basis, unless otherwise noted.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q2 total revenue was $28.8 billion, down 1% or up 3% on a constant currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Had foreign exchange rates remained constant with Q2 of last year, total revenue would have been approximately $1.3 billion higher.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q2 total expenses were $20.5 billion, up 22% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In terms of the specific line items, cost of revenue decreased 4% as growth in core infrastructure investments and content-related costs were more than offset by a reduction in Reality Labs loss reserves as a result of the announced price increase of Quest 2.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: R&D increased 43%, mainly driven by hiring to support Family of Apps and Reality Labs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Marketing and sales increased 10%, mainly driven by hiring and marketing spend.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Lastly, G&A increased 53%, mainly driven by legal-related and employee-related costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We added over 5,700 net new hires in Q2, the majority in technical functions.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We ended the quarter with over 83,500 full-time employees, up 32% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our second quarter growth rate reflects our hiring progress earlier this year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: However, we anticipate headcount growth will slow throughout the rest of the year due to the reduction in our hiring plans.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Second-quarter operating income was $8.4 billion, representing a 29% operating margin.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our tax rate was 18%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We recorded a loss of $172 million under interest and other expenses, driven mainly by unrealized losses and equity investments.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Net income was $6.7 billion or $2.46 per share.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $7.7 billion, driven by investments in servers, data centers, and network infrastructure.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The big step-up in capex, both year over year and sequentially related to server spend, including for our AI infrastructure.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Sustainability remains a key focus of our infrastructure efforts.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: And in June, we published our third annual sustainability report.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The report demonstrates continued progress on our sustainability initiatives.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Free cash flow was $4.5 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We repurchased $5.1 billion of our Class A common stock in the second quarter, and we ended the quarter with $40.5 billion in cash and marketable securities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Moving now to our segment results.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: I'll begin with the Family of Apps segment.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q2 total Family of Apps revenue was $28.4 billion, down 1%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Q2 Family of Apps revenue was $28.2 billion, down 1% or up 3% on a constant currency basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Advertising revenue growth slowed throughout the second quarter as advertiser demand softened.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The deceleration has been broad-based across verticals, and we believe businesses are lowering their advertising spend in response to the increased economic uncertainty.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Foreign currency headwinds also increased throughout the second quarter.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: While it wasn't a factor contributing to the deceleration in Q2, we're also continuing to face targeting and measurement headwinds such as Apple's iOS changes, which we believe are contributing to the growth challenges across the digital advertising industry.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: On a user geography basis, year-over-year ad revenue growth was strongest in Asia Pacific and Rest of World at 13% and 11%, respectively, with both regions benefiting meaningfully from strong growth in click-to-messaging ads.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: North America and Europe declined 4% and 12%, respectively.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Foreign currency was a headwind in all international regions, with Europe and Asia Pacific experiencing the largest impacts.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In Q2, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased 15% and the average price per ad decreased 14%.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Impression growth was driven by Asia Pacific and Rest of World.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: The year-over-year decline in pricing was driven by a reduction in advertiser demand, the mix shift in ad impressions toward lower monetizing services in regions and foreign currency depreciation.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Family of Apps other revenue was $218 million, up 14%, driven by the WhatsApp business API.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Family of Apps expenses were $17.2 billion, up 23%, driven mainly by employee-related expenses, legal costs and infrastructure costs.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Family of Apps operating income was $11.2 billion, representing a 39% operating margin.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We estimate that approximately 2.9 billion people used at least one of our Family of Apps on a daily basis in June and that approximately 3.6 billion people used at least one on a monthly basis.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Facebook daily active users were 1.97 billion, up 3% or 60 million compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: DAUs represented approximately 67% of the 2.93 billion monthly active users in June.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: MAUs grew by 39 million or 1% compared to last year.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Europe DAUs and MAUs declined sequentially and were negatively impacted by the loss of users in Russia and Ukraine.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Within our Reality Labs segment, Q2 revenue was $452 million, up 48%, driven primarily by Quest 2 sales.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Reality Labs expenses were $3.3 billion, up 19% due to growth in employee-related costs and R&D operating expenses that were partially offset by the previously mentioned reduction in loss reserves.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Reality Labs' operating loss was $2.8 billion in the second quarter.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect third quarter 2022 total revenue to be in the range of $26 billion to $28.5 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: This outlook reflects a continuation of the weak advertising demand environment we experienced throughout the second quarter, which we believe is being driven by broader macroeconomic uncertainty.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We also anticipate third quarter Reality Labs revenue to be lower than second-quarter revenue.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Our guidance assumes foreign currency will be an approximately 6% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth in the third quarter based on current exchange rates.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In addition, as noted on previous calls, we continue to monitor developments regarding the viability of transatlantic data transfers and their potential impact on our European operations.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Turning now to the expense outlook.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2022 total expenses to be in the range of $85 billion to $88 billion, lowered from our prior outlook of $87 billion to $92 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We've reduced our hiring and overall expense growth plan this year to account for the more challenging operating environment while continuing to direct resources toward our company priorities.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We expect 2022 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases to be in the range of $30 billion to $34 billion, narrowed from our prior range of $29 million to $34 billion.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: Absent any changes to U.S. tax law, we expect our full year 2022 tax rate to be above the Q2 rate and in the high teens.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: In closing, we're in the midst of an economic cycle that is having a broad impact on the digital advertising business.

speaker: Dave Wehner
sentence: We're being disciplined on spending while still investing in those areas that will position to drive growth as the economic environment improves.

speaker: Dave Wehner

sentence: Power Platform is becoming the next-generation business process automation and productivity suite for domain experts in all functions.

sentence: We have taken a unique approach to what is an expansive and high-growth TAM, bringing together robotic process automation, low-code, no-code tools, virtual agents, and business intelligence.

sentence: Revenue increased 84% year over year.

sentence: Telstra, T-Mobile, Toyota North America, and Unilever have all built centers of excellence for Power Platform with thousands of workers who are using those low-code, no-code tools to build apps and workflows for everything from COVID-19 screening to product quality control.

sentence: This quarter, we introduced new industry clouds for financial services, manufacturing, and nonprofits, building on the momentum of existing clouds for healthcare and retail.

sentence: And our pending acquisition of Nuance will bring our solutions directly into the physician-patient loop, which is central to healthcare delivery.

sentence: Hybrid work will require a new operating model.

sentence: In markets where employees have returned to the workplace, including Australia, China, New Zealand, South Korea, and Taiwan, we have seen usage continue to grow.

sentence: Teams is transforming not only internal collaboration but companies how they do business.

sentence: We added support for shared workspaces with people outside the organization, and we are seeing Teams used for everything from virtual retail showrooms and personal shopping to interactive webinars.

sentence: We introduced Microsoft Viva this quarter, creating a new market category for employee experience.

sentence: Viva brings together knowledge, learning, communication, and insights in an integrated experience directly within Teams and Microsoft 365.

sentence: Companies like Coca-Cola and Unilever will use Viva to help their employees thrive in a new era of hybrid work.

sentence: Office 365 now has nearly 300 million paid seats.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: And organizations across the private and public sector like the City of Helsinki, Bausch Health, Stryker are increasingly choosing our premium offerings for advanced security, compliance, voice, and analytics.

sentence: People are turning to Windows PCs more than ever to stay connected, productive, and secure.

sentence: The threat landscape has never been more complex or challenging and security has never been more critical to our customers.

sentence: This is driving increased demand for our end-to-end capabilities across identity, security, compliance, and management backed by cloud-scale AI and human expertise encompassing all clouds and all platforms.

sentence: What differentiates us and drives customer value is the interconnection between identity, endpoint, apps, cloud, data, and infrastructure across our cloud-native XDR and SIEM.

sentence: Our approach enables organizations to adopt a zero-trust architecture while also reducing the complexity, cost, and risk created by stitching together point solutions.

sentence: Our Azure AD paid customer base has more than doubled year over year to over 300,000, new capabilities in Microsoft 365 Defender help organizations better understand, prevent and mitigate active threats.

sentence: Just last week, we added cloud gaming via the browser expanding our reach across PC and mobile.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: In closing, we're innovating across the entire tech stack as we differentiate and lead in areas that will be critical to the success of every customer going forward.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: I'm optimistic about our opportunity ahead.

sentence: From Heineken to Hilton, to Zurich Insurance, organizations continue to choose our premium E5 offerings for advanced security, compliance, voice, and analytics.

sentence: We've seen a structural shift in PC demand.

sentence: More than ever, people are turning to PCs to exercise their agency and unleash their creativity, whether it's meeting in virtual reality or for remote work, writing code or collaborating in documents, livestreaming video or playing games, or for graphic design and engineering design.

sentence: As new use cases are born every day and existing ones see a resurgence, we're experiencing a PC renaissance with increase in time spent on PCs and PCs per household.

sentence: Three months in, we're delighted by the response to Windows 11.

sentence: We're seeing more usage intensity and higher quality than previous versions of our operating system, and Windows took share this quarter.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: We are delivering Windows in new ways to meet evolving customer needs.

sentence: This quarter, we introduced Windows 11 SE, a cloud-first operating system purpose-built for schools.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: And with Windows 365, we are bringing the operating system to the cloud, helping businesses like Coats North America and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals stream the full Windows experience to any employee device.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: There are now more than 1.4 billion monthly active devices running Windows 10 or Windows 11, and they're a powerful on-ramp for both our first-party and third-party services.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Windows 11 users engage with the Windows app store at nearly three times the rate of Windows 10.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: And across Bing and Edge, we are creating differentiated, high-value experiences for consumers and advertisers in key verticals, including shopping.
