sentence: Just one year since the launch of coupon and price comparison features in Edge, we already have surfaced more than $800 million in savings.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: More broadly, we are expanding our opportunity in advertising.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Over the past 12 months, our total advertising revenue, inclusive of LinkedIn, surpassed $10 billion ex-TAC.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: And with our acquisition of Xandr, we will bring to market new advertising solutions that combine our deep audience understanding and customer base with Xandr's large-scale, data-driven platforms.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Now on to security.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Cybercrime is the number one threat facing every business today.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Our aim is to help organizations implement a comprehensive "zero trust" architecture that protects people, devices, applications, and data holistically across their heterogeneous cloud and client environments.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: We protect our customers in two interconnected ways: first, we incorporate security by design into every product we built; and, second, we deliver advanced end-to-end cross-cloud, cross-platform security solutions, which integrate more than 50 different categories across security, compliance, identity, device management, and privacy, informed by more than 24 trillion threat signals we see each day.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Among analysts, we are a leader in more than -- more security categories, now 19, than any other provider.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Our multicloud, multiplatform innovation is driving growth.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Across commercial and consumer, more than 1 billion monthly active users now rely on Microsoft account to securely access their favorite products and services with just one login.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: More than 15,000 customers now use our cloud-native SIEM, Microsoft Sentinel, to stop threats before they happen, up over 70% year over year.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: And all-up, the number of customers that use our advanced security solutions accelerated this quarter to over 715,000.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: More than half have four or more workloads, up 75% year over year, underscoring our end-to-end differentiation.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: On average, customers save 60% compared to multivendor solutions.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: As a result of our customers' trust, our security business revenue surpassed $15 billion over the past 12 months, up nearly 45% year over year.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Now on to gaming.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: The big bets we have made across content, community, and cloud over the past few years are paying off.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: We saw record engagement, as well as revenue this quarter.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Game Pass has more than 25 million subscribers across PC and console.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Our differentiated content is driving the service's growth, and we released new AAA titles this holiday to rave reviews and record usage.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: Eighteen million have played Forza Horizon 5 to date, and more than 20 million have played Halo Infinite, making it the biggest Halo launch in history.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: And with our planned acquisition of Activision Blizzard, announced last week, we are investing to make it easier for people to play great games wherever, whenever, and however they want, and also shape what comes next for gaming as platforms like the metaverse develop.

speaker: Satya Nadella
sentence: In closing, as digital technology as a percentage of global GDP continues to increase, we are innovating and investing across a diverse and growing  TAMs with a common underlying technology stack and an operating model that reinforces a common strategy, culture, and sense of purpose.

sentence: We built Omniverse Avatars to make it easy for people to integrate some amazing technology for computer vision, for speech recognition, natural language understanding, gesture recognition, facial animation and speech synthesis, recommender systems, all of that integrated into one system and running in real time.

sentence: Chips are enablers, but chips don't create markets, software creates market.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: At this point, I explain over the years that accelerated computing is very different than general purpose computing and the reason for that is because you can't just write into compiler and compile quantum physics into a chip.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: I mean, it doesn't.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: You can't just compile Schrodinger's equation and have it distributed across multiple GPUs, multiple nodes and have a new SaaS. You just -- you can't do that for computer graphics, you can't do that for artificial intelligence, you can't do that for robotics, you can't do that for the most of the interesting applications in the world and because we really run out of steam with GPUs and that people are saying that not because it's not true, it is abundantly clear that the amount of instruction in parallel that you can squeeze out of a system is although not zero is incredibly hard, it's just incredibly hard.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And there is another approach and we have been advocating accelerated computing for some time and now people really see the benefit of it, but it does requires a lot of work and yet the work basically says for every domain, for every application we have -- for every application in large domain that you'll use, you have to have a whole stack.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so whenever you want to open a new market by accelerating those applications or that domain of applications, you have to come up with a new stack and the new stack is hard, because you have to understand the application, you have to understand the algorithms, the mathematics, you have to understand computer science to distribute it across, to take something that was single threaded and make it multi-threaded and make something that we've done sequentially and make it process in parallel.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: You break everything, you break storage, you break networking, you break everything.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so it takes a fair amount of expertise and that's why we're saying that over the years, over the course of 30 years we have become a full-stack company, because we've been trying to solve this problem practically through decades.

speaker: Jensen Huang

sentence: Yeah, thanks a lot, C.J. As you know, A100 is a very different type of GPU.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: This is our first universal computing GPU.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It's great at high performance computing, it's great at data analytics, it's great at training and also for our highest-end GPUs, it is also the first time that it is incredible for inference.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It's some 20 times faster than previous generation.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It introduces some really exciting new computational formats like TF32, TensorFloat 32 for training and with multi-instance GPU, turning our GPU -- one GPU into a whole bunch of smaller GPUs, autonomous GPUs to improve performance and reducing latency.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so the capability is really quite exciting.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: We're seeing strength in hyperscalers as they continue to accelerate their adoption of AI.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Some of the new applications we've spoken about a couple of times before is the transition to deep learning for conversational AI, speech recognition to natural language understanding all the way to speech synthesis is now based on AI -- based on deep learning.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The other area that is growing incredibly fast is deep learning recommender models.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Just about everything that we do on the Internet is based on recommenders.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: There are hundreds of different recommenders out there whether you are shopping or recommending music or recommending news or recommending search and so all of the recommending ads.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so all of these different types of applications are driving value.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: For the first time, we saw our industrial application -- industrial data center growing to be larger than hyperscale and we're seeing industrial applications across scientific computing where simulation-based approaches are now being fused with AI approaches for weather simulation, genomics, molecular dynamic simulation, quantum chemistry, even simulating quantum computing which is one of the really exciting areas.

sentence: I mean we're going to see several couple of years of continued growth yet ahead of us as AI gets adopted in clouds and industries.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Vivek, we're entering the third phase of AI.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The first phase of AI was when we invented the computing platforms, the new chips, the new systems, the system software, the new middleware, the new way of working, the new way of developing software, which the industry -- the world is now starting to call MLOps.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The way that software is developed and the way that it is deployed is completely different than in the past.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: In fact, I heard a great term, Software 2.0 and it makes a lot of sense.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It's a computer that is writing software.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The way that you develop software is completely different, the way compute is different and that was our first phase and that started in the journey that was some eight, nine years ago now.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The second phase was the adoption of using this in an industrial way for clouds and we strongly revolutionized these services whether it's speech oriented services or search oriented services, just recommender services, the way you shop, the way you use the Internet is completely different to and so that's really the second phase and those two phases are still continuing to grow and you're still seeing the growth associated with that.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The third phase is the industrialization of AI and some of the great examples when I say kind of the smartphone moment, I meant that it's a device with AI, its autonomous and its connected to a cloud service and its continuously learning.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: So some of the exciting example that I saw -- that I've seen and we're working with, with companies all over the world, we have some 7,000 AI start-ups that we're working with and almost all of them are developing something like this and large industrial companies whether it's John Deere or Walmart, they are all developing applications kind of like this and basically it's an autonomous system, autonomous machine.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: In our case, it's called Jetson, it's a robotics machine.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: If that robotics machine is a car, then its called DRIVE and it's running an autonomous -- an AI application on top, an AI skill on top and it could be moving things around, it could be picking and placing, it could be just watching a warehouse and monitoring traffic and keeping traffic flow going.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It could be connected to a car and whenever the car -- whenever the fleet of cars needs to be retrained because of the new circumstance that was discovered, the cloud service would do the relearning and then would deploy it into all of the autonomous devices.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so in the future we're seeing that these industries whether you're in retail or in logistics or transportation or farming, ag tech to lawnmowers -- consumer lawnmowers.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: They're not going to just be products that you buy and use from that point forward, but they will likely be a connected device with an AI service that runs on top of it and so these industries are so excited about it because it gives them an opportunity to change the way that they interact with their customers.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Rather than selling something once, they sell something and provide a service that's on top of that and they could stay engaged with the customers.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The customers could get a product that's improving all of the time just like your smartphone and that's kind of like -- that's kind of the reason, that's the reason why I've been calling it the smartphone moment for all these industries and we saw what happened to the smartphone revolution and then we saw what happened to the smart microphone, the smart speaker revolution.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: You're going to see smart lawnmowers, smart tractors, smart air conditioners, smart elevators, smart buildings, smart warehouses, robotic retail stores.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The entire retail store is like a robot and they will all have autonomous capability, they'll all be driven by AI.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so what's new for the industry therefore is that all of the enterprises in the world used to have computers for IT to facilitate -- to host their employees and their supply chain, but in the future all of these industries whether you are in medical imaging or lawnmowers, you're going to have data centers that are hosting your products just like the CSPs and so that's a brand new industry and we have a platform that we call EGX, which is the 5G Edge AI systems and we have the autonomous system we call AGX, which is [Indecipherable] and between those two systems and the software stack that we have on top of it, we're in a great position to help these industries one at a time transform their business model from the object-oriented business model, a theme based business model to a connected device business model.

sentence: We have different versions of our products for Gaming, for Professional Visualization, for high performance computing, for deep learning, it stands to reason we have to build a different version for CMP and we can sell it directly the way that we go to market would be to go to directly to the industrial miners and it's a great benefit to them so that they don't have to chase around spot markets, it's a great benefit to the gamers because they want to game and the game demand is just incredible, it's off the chart and so I think this is going to be really beneficial to everybody.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The recent hash rate growth was really a result of several dynamics.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The first dynamic is the installed base.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Most people thought that once the mining GPUs come back into the aftermarket, a small part does that, some people do that, but the vast majority of them keep them and the reason for that is because obviously they believe in Ethereum and they are industrial miners, that's what they do and so they keep it around for when the profitability returns and they could kick start their mining gear.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: That's what we saw in the latter part of last year.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: We saw the hash rate starting to grow.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Most of that was resulting from the installed miners reactivating their equipment.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It wasn't until earlier this year that we started to see demand in our own GPUs and when that starts to happen, there are several different dynamics.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The primary source these days come from powerful ASICs and then there are some that comes from our GPU and other GPUs in the marketplace.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so I think that this is going to be a part of our business.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It won't grow extremely large no matter what happens and the reason for that is because when it starts to grow large, more ASICs come to the market, which kinds of mutes it and when the market becomes smaller, it's harder for ASICs to sustain the R&D and so the spot miners, industrial miners come back and then we'll create CMPs.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so we expect it to be a small part of our business as we go forward.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: One of the important things is to realize that in the near-term because we're in the beginning parts of our Ampere ramp, only two quarters into a multi-year cycle.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: There's a fundamental difference in hyperscale use of HPC or AI versus the industrial use of HPC and AI.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: In the world of hyperscalers and Internet service providers, they're making recommendations on movies and songs and articles and search results and so on and so forth.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And the difference in the improvement in hyper speed, the deep learning and artificial intelligence large recommender systems can provide us, they're really working for them.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: In the world of industry, the reason why artificial intelligence is transformative, recognizing that most of the things I just mentioned earlier, it's not really dynamic in the world's largest industries, whether it's healthcare or logistics or transportation and retail, the vast majority of the reasons why in some of the physical sciences industries, whether it's energy or transportation and such or healthcare, the simulation of physics, the simulation of the world was not achievable using traditional first principle simulation approaches.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: But artificial intelligence or data-driven approaches has completely shaken that up and put it on its head.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And some examples, whether it's using artificial intelligence so that you could feed up the simulation of the prediction of the protein structure of an -- or the 3D structural protein, which was recently achieved by a couple of very important networks, it's groundbreaking.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And by understanding the protein structure, 3D structure, we understand it -- we can better understand its function and how it would adapt to other proteins and other chemicals.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And it's a fundamental step of the process in drug discovery and that has just taken a giant leap forward.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: In the areas of clinical science, it is now possible to consider using data-driven approaches to create models that overcome this -- not overcome but accelerate and make it possible for us to simulate much, much larger simulations of multiphysics geometry-aware simulations, which is basically climate science.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: These are really important fields of work that wouldn't have been possible for another decade at least.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And just as we made it possible using artificial intelligence, the realization of real-time ray tracing in every field of science, whether it's climate simulation, energy discovery, drug discovery, we're starting to see the industry recognizing that the fusion of the first-principle simulation and data-driven artificial intelligence approaches is going to get a giant leap up.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And that is a second dynamic.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The other dynamic for industry is for the very first time, they could deploy AI model out to the edge to do a better job with agriculture, to do a better job with asset protection and warehouses, to do a better job with automating retail.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: AI is going to make it possible for all of these types of automation to finally be realized.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so, the dynamics are all very different.

speaker: Jensen Huang

sentence: It's a simulator that is physically accurate and physically based and was made possible because of two fundamental technologies we invented.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: One of them is of course RTX, the ability to physically simulate light behavior in the world, which is ray tracing.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The second is the ability to compute or simulate the physics of -- simulate the artificial intelligence behavior of engines and objects inside the world.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: So we have the ability now to simulate physics in a realistic way and to create an architecture that allows us to do it in the cloud, distribute in a computed way and to be able to scale it out to very large systems.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The question is, what would you do with such a thing?

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The simulator -- simulation of virtual worlds with portals, we call them connectors, portals based on an industry standard open standard that was pioneered by Pixar.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And as we mentioned earlier, we're partnering with Pixar and Apple to make it even broadly adopted -- even more broadly adopted.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: It's called UFD, universal field description.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Theyre basically portals or worm holes into virtual worlds.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And this virtual world we're simulating, it could be a concert for consumers, it could be a theme park for consumers, [Technical Issues] in the world of industries, we could use it for simulating robots, different robots could learn how to be robots inside these virtual worlds before they're downloaded from the simulator to the real world.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: You can use it to simulate factories, which is one of the early works that we done with BMW that I showed at GTC.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Factory of the future that is designed completely in Omniverse, simulated in Omniverse, robots trained in Omniverse with goods and materials that are original, cad data put into the factory, the logistics plan like an ERP system -- this is an ERP system of physical grids and physical simulation simulated through this Omniverse world.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And you could plan the entire factory in Omniverse.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: This entire factory now becomes what is called a digital tool.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: In fact, it could be a factory, it could be a stadium, it could be an airport, it could be an entire city, it could be a fleet of cars.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: The digital twin would allow us to simulate new algorithms, new AI, new -- and optimization algorithms before we deploy it into the physical world.

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: And so, what is Omniverse?

speaker: Jensen Huang
sentence: Well, Omniverse is going to be an overload, if you will, of virtual worlds that increasingly people call the metaverse.

sentence: And if you have heard several companies talk about the metaverse.

speaker: Jensen Huang

speaker: Jensen Huang

sentence: So I'm fairly sure that at this point Omniverse and the metaverse is going to be a new economy that is larger than our current economy.

sentence: New enrollment in this study has been paused while we provide additional information to the FDA regarding three cases of peripheral neuropathy observed in the ongoing Phase 1 MagnetisMM-1 study.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Patients who are deriving clinical benefits from elranatamab may continue treatment.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: In rare disease, our Phase 3 lead-in study for the gene therapy fidanacogene elaparvovec in hemophilia B has now been fully enrolled with more than 40 patients.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We remain on course to complete dosing and expect to conduct a planned interim analysis for a potential data readout in this year, in 2021.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We also continue to progress our hemophilia A gene therapy, giroctocogene fitelparvovec, which was developed in collaboration with Sangamo Therapeutics.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We anticipate presenting two-year Phase 1, 2 data in the fourth quarter of 2021.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Additionally, we are pleased to report that our lead-in study for our Phase 3 AFFINE study is in hemophilia A now fully enrolled, which could lead to a pivotal readout in 2022.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: For our gene therapy candidate for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, we now have an approved generic name, fordadistrogene movaparvovec, and we are progressing our Phase 3 trial, CIFFREO.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: To date, we have opened 15 trial sites in eight countries -- Italy, Spain, Israel, the UK, South Korea, Japan, Russia and Canada.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: In the US, we are actively working with the FDA to address outstanding questions related to our investigational new drug application, including technical aspects of our potency assay matrix, so that we can begin enrolling patients in Phase 3 US study sites.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: While we have high confidence in our current quality control overall and with a potency assay matrix which has been accepted in countries outside of the US, the FDA has additional technical requests that we are working to address as quickly as possible.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We understand the sense of urgency among many families in the US who are hoping for sites to open soon.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: While we cannot speculate at this time as to when sites may open in the US, we do not expect a resolution in the first half of 2021.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We are working with a sense of urgency and hope to reach alignment with the FDA as soon as possible.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: In the interim, we will continue to progress our trial globally and enroll patients at other sites, which we believe will allow our program to remain on track to potentially enable approvals around the world, including the US.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Now, I would like to address a key policy issue in which we continue to be actively engaged: affordable access.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We expect the Biden administration will soon announce a human capital component to their infrastructure package that will include health provisions.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Pfizer is mobilizing to work with the administration, as well as lawmakers in both political parties on meaningful solutions for patient access.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Specifically, there are three key areas where we would like to see Congress and the administration focus -- rebate reform, capping beneficiary cost-sharing in Medicare Part D and incentivizing the uptake of biosimilars.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: At the state level, we have focused our efforts on meaningful solutions to directly address patient affordability challenges.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: This includes legislation to require 100% of negotiated rebates to be passed through to consumers at the pharmacy counter.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We have also worked with state policymakers to advance legislation in several states, ensuring that patient assistance provided by manufacturers will count toward the patient's deductible and out of pocket maximums.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Looking ahead, we remain focused on being nimble and investing in our R&D organization so we can build on the strong improvement in the clinical success rates that had been seen over the past five years and, potentially, translate that success into strong commercial launches that benefit patients.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Excluding any impact from our COVID-19 vaccine, we are on track and continue to expect a revenue CAGR of at least 6% on a risk-adjusted basis through the end of 2025, as well as double-digit growth on the bottom line.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We remain very confident in our ability to achieve these growth rates because of the strength of both our current product portfolio and our R&D pipeline.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: At the same time, we will continue to pursue business development opportunities with the potential to further enhance our long-term growth prospects.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Just last week, for example, Pfizer acquired Amplyx Pharmaceuticals, a privately held company dedicated to the development of therapies for debilitating and life-threatening diseases that affect people with compromised immune systems.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Amplyx's lead compound is a novel investigational asset under development for the treatment of invasive fungal infection.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And now I will pass the stage to our CFO, Frank D'Amelio.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Thank you, Albert.

sentence: Good day, everyone.

sentence: I know you've seen our release so let me provide a few highlights regarding the financials.

sentence: Clearly, the COVID-19 vaccine has had a dramatic positive impact on our year-over-year results, and Albert has addressed the key points on the COVID-19 vaccine landscape.

sentence: Revenue and adjusted cost of sales was significantly impacted by COVID-19 vaccine sales and the associated 50% gross profit split with BioNTech, which we recognize on the cost of sales line.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Revenue increased 42% operationally in the first quarter of 2021 driven by COVID-19 vaccine sales and solid performance from a number of our other key growth drivers.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: The adjusted cost of sales increase shown here reduced gross margin by 10 percentage points compared to the first quarter of 2020, which primarily reflects the impact of the COVID-19 vaccine gross profit split, which accounted for approximately 8 percentage points, and to a much smaller extent, product mix.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Looking at the business excluding the COVID-19 vaccine contribution, we saw a continuation of solid revenue growth for the business in the quarter, which nicely supports our projected revenue CAGR of at least 6% through the end of 2025.

speaker: Frank DAmelio

sentence: In addition, compared with the prior-year quarter, first-quarter 2021 revenues were favorably impacted by approximately 400 million as a result of the first-quarter 2021 having three additional selling days in the US and four additional selling days in international markets.

sentence: This increase in selling days will be offset in fourth quarter of 2021, resulting in essentially the same number of selling days in full-year '21 as compared to full-year 2020.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: However, the favorable impact on quarter-over-quarter comparisons in first-quarter 2021 from selling days was partially offset by the non-recurrence of favorable revenue impacts related to COVID-19 in first-quarter 2020, including increased demand for certain products of approximately 150 million and additional wholesaler inventories of approximately 100 million.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Given these factors, the net favorable impact on first-quarter 2021 revenues was approximately 150 million or approximately 1.5 percentage points of operational growth, which in effect reduces the strong 8% operational growth rate to about 7%.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Reported diluted EPS for the quarter was up 44% compared to the year ago quarter, while adjusted diluted EPS grew 47% for the quarter.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Foreign exchange movements resulted in a 3% positive benefit to revenue and a 1% benefit to adjusted diluted EPS.

sentence: Let's move to our revised 2021 guidance.

sentence: We've again provided total company guidance, which includes the business with the COVID-19 vaccine, and then we provided some additional sub-ledger detail on our assumptions regarding the projected COVID-19 vaccine contribution so you can also see our projection for the business without the COVID-19 vaccine.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: To start, the adjustments we've made to our total company guidance are almost entirely due to the anticipated impact of the COVID-19 vaccine and R&D spending on incremental COVID-19 programs and non-COVID-19 mRNA programs, along with a small increase in the revenue outlook for the business excluding the COVID-19 vaccine.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: For adjusted cost of sales, the ranges have increased to 38 to 39%, which incorporates the incremental anticipated COVID-19 vaccine revenue which has a significantly higher cost of sales due to the gross margin split with BioNTech as compared to the rest of the business.

sentence: The projected COVID-19 vaccine revenue as a percentage of total company revenue has increased to 36% as compared to 25% in our initial 2021 guidance.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: On adjusted SI&A, we have maintained our initial guidance of 11 to 12 billion.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: In addition, we increased our adjusted R&D guidance range to $9.8 billion to 10.3 billion to incorporate anticipated spending on incremental COVID-19-related programs and other mRNA-based projects that are not part of the BioNTech partnership.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Working this through with a projected 15% effective tax rate yields an increased adjusted diluted EPS range of $3.55 to $3.65 or 59% growth at the midpoint compared to 2020, including an expected 4% benefit from foreign exchange.

sentence: Let me quickly remind you of some assumptions and context on the projected COVID-19 vaccine contribution and our collaboration agreement.

sentence: As referenced earlier, the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine collaboration construct is a 50-50 gross margin split.

sentence: We now expect that we can manufacture up to 2.5 billion doses in '21, subject to continuous process improvements, expansion at current facilities and adding new suppliers and contract manufacturers.

sentence: As of mid-April, we have contracted for approximately 1.6 billion vaccine doses to be delivered in 2021 and still have contracts for potential additional doses under review.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Based on the approximately 1.6 billion doses, we are now forecasting approximately 26 billion in COVID-19 vaccine revenue this year.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: We continue to have 3 pricing tiers for government contracts depending on the relative wealth of nations.

sentence: Our cost of sales for the COVID-19 vaccine revenue continues to include manufacturing and distribution costs, applicable royalty expense, as well as a payment to BioNTech representing the 50% gross profit split.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: We continue to expect that the adjusted income before tax for the COVID-19 vaccine contribution to be in the high 20s as a percentage of revenue.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: This margin level also includes the anticipated spending on additional mRNA programs.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: As I noted earlier, the COVID-19 vaccine is now projected to account for 36% of total revenue for 2021, up from 25% in our initial guidance for the year.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Let me add that if we contract for additional delivery of doses during the year, we will provide a guidance update in our subsequent earning releases.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: If we remove the projected COVID-19 vaccine contribution from both periods, you will see that we slightly increased 2021 revenue range to be between 44.6 and 46.6 billion, representing approximately 6% operational revenue growth at the midpoint.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: In terms of adjusted diluted EPS, we continue to project a range of $2.50 to $2.60, which represents approximately 11% operational growth at the midpoint.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: These growth rates are all consistent with how we've been publicly positioning the business post the Upjohn separation.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: You likely saw our announcement that we have maintained our dividend payment for the second quarter at its current level despite Viatris announcing their expected dividend payment.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: For those continuing to own Viatris shares, this effectively represents an increase in the dividend income, and our board felt that the strength of our business supported maintaining our dividend.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: For the foreseeable future, we expect our board to continue to support annual dividend increases at approximately this year's level.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Obviously, we have no say as to what Viatris does with its future dividend.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: In summary, a tremendous start to 2021.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: The COVID-19 vaccine continues to benefit millions of people around the world, and the business is on track for anticipated solid top and bottom line growth.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: We remain focused on advancing our pipeline, supporting in-market brands and looking to deploy capital responsibly with a focus on initiatives that can solidify our long-term revenue and earnings growth outlook.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: With that, I'll turn it back to Chuck.

speaker: Chuck Triano
sentence: Thanks, Frank and Albert, for your prepared remarks.

speaker: Chuck Triano
sentence: At this point, operator, let's move to our Q&A session, please.

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: Congratulations on the quarter.

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: So first question I had for you.

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: What are your thoughts on the slowing vaccination rates in the US?

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: Do you anticipate things to pick up again?

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: And will we reach that level of herd immunity in the US here?

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: And then second question I had was on vaccine sales and how you think about it beyond 2021 and 2022.

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: What gives you confidence that there's going to be a tail here?

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: And how does that tail look relative to the $26 billion that you're going to potentially have this year?

speaker: Louise Chen
sentence: And then last question I had for you is just on how you're thinking about FDA concerns around JAK safety.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Thank you very much, Louise.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Let me make some comments on the slowing vaccinations and maybe a little bit on the '22, '23 revenues.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: I will ask Mikael Dolsten to add some comments over there.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And then, for also JAK, I will ask him to make some comments about the same.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Look, I think the US has done a tremendously good job and they have reached vaccination level that we didn't think that they will.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: The truth is that as we are vaccinating more and more people, the people that are reluctant to get a vaccine are enriching the remaining pool.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: So it's normal to expect that we will see a drop in the vaccination.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: But I believe that the entering of additional pools like younger people post the expected approval of our 11 to 15 years old, vaccination also will provide an additional increase in the vaccination rates.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: All in all, I think US is doing a very good job and their focus of all should be to convince those people that they have still fear about the vaccine that they must do the right thing.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Now, beyond '22 and '23, first of all, we believe, as we said multiple times, that there will be a need for boosters.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And there is a need likely from now all the way to 6 months and then believe that likely annual vaccinations or, let's say, regular vaccinations would be required.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Clearly, this belief is based on the totality of the evidence and not on studies that they had read out right now to convince that this is the case.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: The totality of the evidence are having to do with the fact that we still have very high efficacy of 90%, above 90% in our six months, but it is lower at 91% than 95% that we had in the beginning.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: So there are some indications that there is a drop in the efficacy over time.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We know from immunogenicity studies of neutralizing antibodies that also there is a drop on these antibodies, and that affects not only people that they are vaccinated but also naturally infected.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We also know that after six months, the increase of reinfections to people that they had previous infections is increasing.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And we also know that we are, right now, our vaccine at least effective against all the variants that we have seen but there is a drop in neutralizing titers, which means that to maintain good efficacy against the variants, you need to increase the immunogenicity and this is why we are doing the studies with the boosters.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: So the totality of the events are pointing out to this.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And this is the reason why basically all governments of the world are now discussing with us about procurement agreements for '22, '23 and '24.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: But I will ask also Mikael Dolsten to make some comments on why we think that the boosters and repeated vaccinations is a likely scenario and also a comment on the JAK safety.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Thank you, Albert.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: I thought you outlined, in an excellent manner, that we have identified a handful of key point related to immunity when induced by convalescent after injection of vaccine that will, over time, as expected, show some decline.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Antibodies will show some decline as their half-life are limited.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Of course, protection contains other immune mechanism.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: When you put all of this in context that SARS-CoV-2 is globally circulating to extent we have rarely seen or ever seen in our lifetime of a virus, and the inability to control across the globe will, of course, lead to numerous changes in the viral mutation rate.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So it just punctuates what Albert said, we need continuously to keep up a very high immune pressure against the virus to stay ahead of the curve.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: And the best way to do that is with regular boosting.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: And finally, herd immunity, while we would like to see it establish, what you hear from a lot of public health data and global health data emerging is that it will be really difficult in large continent to establish such a high immunization rate across all ages and to ensure as you immunize one part of the continent that immunity is maintained at another part.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So I think we would really need to rely on regular immunization and of course, other public health measures rather than hoping that herd immunity across the globe can be established.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Finally, on the JAK safety, already in February 21, FDA made it public about our data in 1133 related to increased risk of serious heart-related problems and certain cancer when compared to another type of medicines, the TNF inhibitors.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So these data are clearly not new.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: FDA, EMA and other agencies work in dialogue with us to finalize the outcome of this review.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: On the other hand, I think the JAK class has shown to be an important contribution as an oral alternative for many patients, and you avoid other issues such as drug antibodies with the biologicals.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So we continue to wait for finalization of the outcome of the 1133 trial.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We think each JAK inhibitor is unique and need to be assessed by itself.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: And we continue to believe that with proper labeling and given the tremendous experience of Xeljanz since 2012, it will continue to have a potential to be an important medicine.

speaker: Chuck Triano
sentence: Operator, next question, please.

speaker: Chuck Triano
sentence: Operator Your next question comes from Terence Flynn from Goldman Sachs.

speaker: Terence Flynn
sentence: Thanks for taking the questions and thank you for all the work on the vaccine front.

speaker: Terence Flynn
sentence: I just had a follow-up on the booster question.

speaker: Terence Flynn
sentence: Do you think that will be uniform across different groups or will there be any differences by baseline characteristics such as age in terms of the timing of a need for a boost?

speaker: Terence Flynn
sentence: And then would you expect FDA and CDC to issue a recommendation on the need for boosters sometime this year?

speaker: Terence Flynn
sentence: And then my second question for Albert or Frank is just would welcome your perspective on the potential impact of tax rate changes in the US and any thoughts on how that might change your capital allocation strategy and/or views on inversions.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Mikael, why don't you take the question for the boosters?

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: I think we cannot, of course, predict what CDC and similar agencies will do.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: But what seems to be the general public dialogue and which, of course, builds on experience with other viral epidemics, and this is, of course, a pandemic, is that you would likely start with those that are most susceptible, older adults, those with chronic diseases such as cardiovascular, obesity, COPD, asthma, many that are immune-impaired.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: And of course, that constitutes a very large population.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: While you may start with those, if we are to really maintain control of the virus, it will be very reasonable to assume the importance of also vaccinating younger groups.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Although severe COVID is less common in younger groups, some patients may suffer severely from such infection, and they are at risk also of acquiring long COVID syndrome, which can cause significant impairment of participation in functional life for young individuals, as well as old.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So all in all, yes, regular boost of entire population is a clear possibility.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Priority is to start, of course, with the many vulnerable from age to chronic diseases, which is a large number of adult populations.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Thank you, Mikael.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And Frank, would you like to take the question about the tax?

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Thank you, Albert.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: So I think it's premature to comment on what impact the proposed tax reform would have in how we view capital allocation and inversion simply because these kinds of proposals typically go through multiple iterations, multiple discussions, multiple negotiations.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: Obviously, we're staying very close to this, doing all the analytics that you would expect us to do.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: But I think what's really important is how we think about taxes and tax policy.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: 2017 tax reform leveled the playing field for US multinationals against foreign competitors.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: And that was an enabler, from my perspective, of much of what we've done with capital deployment, particularly in the US We committed to 5 billion of capex investment between 2018 and 2022.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: We committed a few billion of that risk capital in order to develop the COVID vaccine, funding of our US qualified pension plan that we did last year to the tune of over 1 billion.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: All of those, from my perspective, were enabled by the level playing field that we now get to compete on against our foreign competitors.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: So what we want from tax reform, when all is said and done, is we want a level playing field to continue so that we have the ability to compete on a level playing field.

speaker: Frank DAmelio
sentence: So that's my answer, Albert.

sentence: Now, let me speak a little bit about the policy of the prices, and then I will ask Frank to comment a little bit on the pricing.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And if Angela needs to add something, please feel free.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And then, on the two other areas, clearly, Mikael will speak about the resistance and the mRNA.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: On the pricing reforms, these are our standard positions.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: But I will try to explain how I feel about the pricing reforms.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And I have said it in multiple occasions.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: We don't think that status quo is good for anyone.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: I don't think it's good for the industry.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: I don't think it's good for the Americans because there is a problem with the current way, the current system.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And this is a problem that basically every American is paying for their medicines, and this is unique to medicines, not to other medical interventions, is paying out of their pocket like if they don't have insurance, although they do have insurance.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And this is the fundamental thing that needs to change because the medicines contribution to the overall healthcare, it is 12%.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: So by definition, cannot be the big issue but it is becoming the big issue in the discussion because everybody has to pay this thing from out of pocket almost, unlike other intervention.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: So what this change could look like?

sentence: And for us, a change could take different forms.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: It could be consistent from different areas, may not be the rebate reform, which I think it is one of the systemic issues that we are having with drug pricing, but it could be that out-of-pocket caps.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: The fundamental thing is that there will be a cost that the industry, I'm sure, will be willing to take our fair share as long as all the savings, all the contributions that we are doing right now from this industry will go to the pockets of the American patients.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And this is a fundamental difference with people that we're discussing right now because we are hearing a lot of suggestions that they want to tax the pharmaceutical companies or tax the insurance companies, but the proceeds will just fall in the black hole of the federal budget, which is not what we want.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: I believe that there is room for agreement both with the two sides of the aisle and with this administration.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: And we will continue working on finding the solution that will, I repeat, make medicines affordable for the patients and not throw money to the black hole of the federal budget.

sentence: I should also mention it was negative 5% in the US Now, in terms of our guidance, which is what you asked, Geoffrey, our guidance assumed the pricing decrease, negative impact, I'll call it in the range of low to mid-single digits.

sentence: Mikael, can you speak a little bit about the resistance mechanism in the mRNA or RSV?

sentence: Yeah, thank you.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: As you discussed here, Geoffrey, of course, there is tremendous viral amount across the globe fueled by the spread in large population areas like India.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We do see several different lineages of SARS-CoV-2 established.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: They, however, seem to share the most critical mutations.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Most of the variants have up to 10 mutations and they can combine from different ways.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So far, we believe that our B2, the current vaccine, is very effective in controlling all known mutations.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: But as Albert alluded to, we believe it's very important to keep up very high neutralizing antibody levels in addition to the nice T cell immunity.

sentence: As the pandemic continue, up to now, mutations have been selected mainly because the virus is trying to spread more quickly.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The virus will now face vaccinated immunity in maybe '22, '23 increasingly.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So we need to be prepared that there could be new unexpected mutations to come.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: And that's why Pfizer is leaving no stone untouched and also have variant vaccine developed and could be an alternative later if that scenario would emerge.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: But right now, it seems like the current vaccine is very effective against all these variants despite each having up to 10 different mutations.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: On the RSV, well, we had very robust titers with our protein-based RSV vaccine in maternal vaccination, very good tolerability and antibodies passed efficiently through the cord blood.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: And we are enrolling now well in Phase 3.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We also have initiated a Phase 2 challenge study with RSV that will read out mid of the year, and that could possibly lead to progression swiftly into Phase 3.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: So we are pretty advanced with the protein-based, looks very good.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: But of course, we have now an mRNA platform that we would like to use for multiple opportunities.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We expect to put into the clinic two first-in-human novel vaccines every year for the next two years.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten

sentence: And Steve, it's true that in order to achieve what was achieved with this vaccine, the ingenuity of our people was a key component but also a lot of personal sacrifice had to be involved.

sentence: India wanted to do additional studies in order to approve this vaccine over there which, clearly, we were not ready to allocate resources doing something like that when we were allocating all the resources to do things into the variants, the kids, pregnant women and I can go on, things that we haven't done it before.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Let's begin with COVID-19.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The pandemic continues to evolve into a disease, which is causing significant disease burden, including high rates of acute disease, medical care utilization, hospitalization, and deaths during the entire year.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: A growing number of patients affected by acute COVID infections are developing chronic disease and suffering from long COVID symptoms affecting multiple organs, such as the lungs, heart, kidney, brain, and the vascular system.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We have seen major waves of variants of concern emerge quickly, become dominant, then be superseded by the next variant.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Omicron and its sublineages are the most antigenically distant compared to prior variants of concern, more transmissible, and show evidence of partial immune escape from existing vaccines.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: As the composition of SARS-CoV-2 changes, it is essential we advance new approaches to extend the level of protection that Comirnaty originally conveyed.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: In a clinical trial, we evaluated the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of mono- and bivalent Omicron BA.1 modified vaccines administered as a fourth dose in more than 1,900 participants over age 55.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We are also evaluating different doses of mono- and bivalent BA.1 in participants 18 to 55 years of age.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: While we saw promising responses to both mono- and bivalent versions in the over-55 population, we moved forward with bivalent following guidance from regulators.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The BA.1 vaccine candidate elicited a superior immune response for BA.1 compared to the current version of the vaccine, a seroresponse rate which exceeded non-inferiority, and neutralization activity which increased substantially.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The BA.1 vaccine neutralized wild-type and Delta similarly to the current version of the vaccine, suggesting that Omicron-modified version maintained response for the ancestral and other viral variants.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Based on these data and following guidance from regulators, we have completed regulatory submissions in Europe, U.K., and Canada for the 30-microgram bivalent vaccine individuals 12 and older and plan submissions in other markets soon.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The data also showed this vaccine candidate neutralized Omicron BA.4 and 5, though to a lesser extent than BA.1.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: This suggested a need to develop both a BA.1-modified vaccine and a BA.4/5-modified vaccine.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We studied BA.4/5 monovalent and bivalent booster candidates in mice and found a substantial increase in neutralization responses to all Omicron variants of concern.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Neutralizing titers against BA.4/5 increased 11-fold for the monovalent and 4.8-fold for the bivalent compared to monovalent BA.1 vaccine.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: These data were shared at the recent FDA Advisory Committee meeting as a potential surrogate to help expedite development of a BA.4/5 vaccine.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We plan to submit the BA.4/5 bivalent vaccine candidate for Emergency Use Authorization in the U.S. in preparation for the fall booster campaign.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: To adapt more rapidly, we've agreed with FDA that this submission will be based on safety and immunogenicity data generated in adults with an Omicron-modified BA.1 vaccine and supported by BA.4/5 bivalent-specific preclinical data and BA.4/5 bivalent chemistry, manufacturing, and controls data.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: This strategy is bolstered by previous experience showing that overall responses have been similar between human clinical and mouse data, our clinical experience with Beta- and Omicron-modified vaccine candidates, and by leveraging our mRNA platform and manufacturing experience for the current vaccine.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: To support future potential U.S. licensure and global registrations, we plan to initiate a clinical study to evaluate the BA.4/5 bivalent vaccine.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The clinical study design is under discussion with FDA.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We aspire to continue leading with the science and are working to identify vaccines that would help provide strong and durable protection as new SARS-CoV-2 variants emerge.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We aim to deliver a next-generation COVID-19 vaccine that can provide durable antibody and T cell immune protection against severe disease and hospitalization for at least one year.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We plan to take a stepwise approach by designing and testing different candidates that engage multiple arms of the immune system, including antibodies and T cells.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: First, yesterday, we announced the start of a Phase 2 study evaluating a bivalent modRNA vaccine candidate, which consists of RNAs encoding novel enhanced pre-fusion spike proteins for the SARS-CoV-2 ancestral strain and an Omicron variant.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The enhanced spike protein encoded from the mRNA has been modified with the aim of increasing the magnitude and breadth of antibody neutralization response that could better protect against COV19.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We project delivering key clinical data this fall.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Second, we plan to initiate a proof-of-concept study with a potential pan-SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate by the end of the year.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: This combines the super-stabilized spike sequences with a T cell-enhancing construct, aiming to extend durability of protection against severe disease and new emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Last month, we submitted a new drug application to U.S. FDA seeking approval for the treatment of COVID-19 in both vaccinated and unvaccinated adults and pediatric patients 12 years and over, weighing at least 40 kilograms and at high risk for progression to severe illness.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We anticipate a PDUFA date in the first quarter of 2023.

sentence: We plan to generate further data in those who are immunocompromised, hospitalized with severe COVID-19, and at increased risk for poor outcomes due to the disease or who are pregnant.

sentence: Finally, we're working with FDA to finalize a protocol to study patients who may be in need of retreatment.

sentence: We believe the occurrence of COVID-19 rebound is uncommon and not uniquely associated with any specific treatment.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We know that currently available vaccines are not optimal in addressing the unmet need as each year, many people are infected, hospitalized, and die, resulting in tremendous public health and economic impact.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: In part, this is because the flu vaccine development cycle is inefficient.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: And even when the current seasonal vaccine strains match circulating strains well, they typically confer only 40% to 60% protection.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Potential advantages of the mRNA platform include: shortened timeline to enable a quicker response each season; improved strain matching; faster and more reliable manufacturing; and broader immune response from both antibody and T cells, the latter needed particularly in older adults.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Based on our experience with COVID-19, T-cell responses appear to be critical for the protection against severe disease and hospitalization in infectious viral disease.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Here, we show Phase 2 T cell data for our quadrivalent modRNA flu vaccine candidates in subjects 65 and older.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We believe this is the first evidence of a flu vaccine candidate inducing substantial responses for both CD4 and CD8 T cells.

sentence: On the left, at day seven, the CD4 T cell response was more than twofold for all four flu strains for our vaccine compared to a current high-dose vaccine now recommended in the U.S. for adults 65 and older.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Over half of the cohort receiving our vaccine candidate had a more than twofold response.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: On the right, at day seven, the CD8 T cell response and responder rates were greater for all four strains for our vaccine candidate versus the comparator.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Our belief is that these encouraging T cell responses, combined with higher seroconversion rates for flu A strains, which are the most predominant circulating strains and have pandemic potential, may translate into improved efficacy over current seasonal flu vaccines, particularly in those 65 and older.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Based on these data, we plan to initiate the Phase 3 efficacy study this year.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We are excited to share that new data on our oral GLP-1 receptor agonists, two abstracts on twice-daily danuglipron and one on our once-daily candidate known as 1532, have been accepted for the European Association for the Study of Diabetes Conference in September.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: These investigational medicines were decided in-house by Pfizer's innovative chemistry and discovery teams.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: In a Phase 1 study in adults with type 2 diabetes, after only six weeks of treatment, 1532 drug robustly reduced mean daily glucose to almost near-normal levels.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Participants also experienced weight loss of up to five kilograms compared with two kilograms for placebo.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We believe this to be a potentially best-in-class profile across both injectables and orals.

sentence: Similar changes in body weight were observed in participants with nondiabetic obesity.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: 1532 is characterized by favorable once-daily pharmacokinetics, low risk for drug-drug interaction, robust efficacy across multiple metabolic endpoints, and GLP-1 receptor agonist class-like tolerability, which overall encouraged us to plan for a Phase 2 study to pick the winning candidate prior to a potential Phase 3 study start.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: These development programs may lead to potential indications in type 2 diabetes, obesity, NASH, and cardiovascular risk reduction in type 2 diabetes and obesity patients.

sentence: Over the 12 past months, we have built a strong inflammation and immunology portfolio with diverse products to help address multiple drivers of disease and unmet need.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Cibinqo was approved for atopic dermatitis in adults and last week, received priority review designation in U.S. for adolescents 12 to 18 years.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We are nearing a regulatory submission for etrasimod in ulcerative colitis.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We have submitted regulatory application in U.S., Europe, and U.K. for ritlecitinib for alopecia areata and are awaiting acceptances.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We also plan to start a Phase 3 study of ritlecitinib in vitiligo this year.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We are pleased to now share promising new updated data from our anti-interferon beta monoclonal antibody in specialized rheumatology.

sentence: Patients with dermatomyositis show elevated Type I interferon gene signature in blood, skin, and muscle correlating with disease activity in skin.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: As we continue our development of these candidates, a potential breakthrough therapy for hard-to-treat dermatomyositis which attacks skin and muscles, we believe it may have the ability to address a broader set of inflammatory autoimmune diseases, possibly including polymyositis and lupus.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: On our third quarter 2021 call, I shared data from our ongoing Phase 2 dermatomyositis study focused on skin inflammation and showing significant reduction in disease activity when compared with placebo in just three months of treatment.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Now both doses met the primary efficacy endpoint in skin-predominant disease.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The disease also manifests with progressively debilitating muscle weakness and fatigue.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Early data suggests that in a small cohort of patients with muscle-predominant disease, our candidate resulted in numerically better efficacy scores across all key muscle endpoints, including patient-reported outcomes, after three weeks.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten

sentence: Now a promising update on elranatamab, our investigational B cell maturation antigen CD3-targeted bispecific antibody.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: At ASCO, we presented data from a Phase 1 trial in people with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, whose disease is refractory to at least one agent in each of the three major classes of medications approved for the disease.

sentence: Elranatamab elicited a durable minimal residual disease, or MRD, negativity, meaning no disease was detected after treatment in all evaluable patients who experienced a complete response or stringent complete response.

sentence: MagnetisMM-1 results and emerging data for MagnetisMM-3, which is studying triple-class refractory multiple myeloma, supports further development across a broader program with potential registration-enabling studies, MagnetisMM-5 in patients with double-class exposed multiple myeloma and MagnetisMM-7 in newly diagnosed post-transplant patients with multiple myeloma.

sentence: During this morning's call, I will touch on some of our highlights from 2022 and share some thoughts regarding Pfizer's exciting new year and long-term growth plans.

speaker: Albert Bourla
sentence: Our key growth drivers for the full year 2022 included global sales of Paxlovid, strong growth for Comirnaty developed markets, the launch of Prevnar 20 for the adult population in the U.S., the continued strong growth of Eliquis globally, the strength of our Vyndaqel family globally, and the addition of newly acquired products, Nurtec ODT, Vydura, and Oxbryta.

sentence: These projections include our forecasts for several important potential product launches, including our RSV vaccine for older adults, potential Prevnar 20 pediatric indication, and products and candidates that came to us through recent business development activities, including etrasimod for ulcerative colitis, Nurtec, and zavegepant for migraine, and Oxbryta for sickle cell disease.

sentence: Recognizing the importance of these potential launches, as well as those expected in 2024 to both Pfizer and the patients who rely on our innovations, we are increasing the support we are putting behind them by investing an incremental 1.3 billion in SI&A expenses in 2023.

sentence: As Albert mentioned, we are in a position of unprecedented strength in our history and I'm excited to share a high-level overview of an evolved strategy for Pfizer R&D to focus our resources on transformative programs which could be most impactful for patients, drive improved return on R&D investment, and create the most value.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: I'm pleased to share some examples with you today.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We are pursuing potentially transformative efficacy in our inflammation and immunology franchise, with the potential launches of etrasimod in ulcerative colitis and ritlecitinib in alopecia areata, which both have the potential to be blockbusters, and a planned phase 3 study start of anti-interferon beta in dermatomyositis and other idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Our next wave of innovation includes two monoclonal antibody candidates for atopic dermatitis, which exemplify our multispecific platform and in-house biomedicine design expertise.

sentence: Two assets currently in phase 1 clinical trials each target three cytokines in a single therapeutic, so we refer to them as trispecifics.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: I will talk more about elranatamab and GBT-601 in a moment, so will highlight here that we expect multiple data readouts for TTI-622 in hematological malignancies, two phase 3 readouts for inclacumab in sickle cell disease in the second half of 2024, and a Phase 3 readout for marstacimab in patients with hemophilia A or B in the second quarter of 2023.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: We recently presented strong updated phase 2 data on elranatamab, our investigational B-cell maturation antigen, or BCMA, CD3-targeted bispecific antibody, for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma in heavily pre-treated patients who had received at least three classes of prior therapies.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: This candidate, which has the potential to be a leader in the BCMA bi-specific class, demonstrated a high objective response rate of 61% in patients with no prior BCMA-targeted treatment, early and deep responses, and a manageable safety profile.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: Given factors currently limiting the availability of novel therapies in the triple-class exposed setting, elranatamab has the potential to reach a broader and greater number of patients as an off-the-shelf option with reduced dosing frequency that is administered subcutaneously, offering more convenience than intravenous administration.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: With FDA breakthrough therapy designation granted last year, elranatamab could potentially be approved this year.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: As there is blockbuster potential and patient value beyond the triple-class refractory population, our clinical strategy aims to move to earlier lines of therapy and combination approaches with the potential, if successful, for multiple approvals to expand eligibility and duration of therapy.

speaker: Mikael Dolsten

speaker: Mikael Dolsten
sentence: The most recent data from our phase 1 multiple ascending dose study showed improvements in hematocrit and hemoglobin levels over time, mean hemoglobin occupancy of more than 32% for the 100 milligram maintenance dose and more than 41% for the 150 milligram maintenance dose, and improvements in red blood cell health with the higher maintenance doses.
