speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I'm really excited to join you on this morning's call, and I look forward to meeting with many of you in the months ahead.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As Brian mentioned earlier, our third quarter financial results were outstanding, reflecting unexpected strength across multiple parts of our business.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As a result, we delivered EPS well above our expectations and we have increased the midpoint of our full-year adjusted EPS guidance by $0.30 compared with the previous range.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Third quarter comparable sales increased 4.5%, about 1-percentage point higher than both our second-quarter growth and our expectations.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: When you compound this growth on top of our 5.1% increase last year, you'll see the comparable sales have grown nearly 10% over the last two years.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among sales channels, store comparable sales increased 2.8% in the quarter, more than 1-percentage point faster than our second quarter pace of 1.5%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Digital comp sales grew 31% in the quarter on top of 49% last year and contributed 1.7 percentage points to our total Company comp.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you know, we focus first on driving traffic in our business, because it indicates the continued relevance of our brand and growing engagement among our guests.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's why we're pleased that traffic continues to be the primary driver of our growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Comparable traffic was up 3.1% in the third quarter, driven by increases in both our stores and digital channels.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Growth in average ticket drove another 1.4 percentage points of our comp growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the operating income line, we saw a rate increase of about 80 basis points compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This was well ahead of our expectations, reflecting multiple beneficial factors.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The first was category mix, which contributed about 30 basis points of gross margin improvement in the quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This was the result of exceptional strength in apparel, combined with soft sales trends in our electronics and entertainment categories.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On top of the mix benefit from stronger-than-expected apparel sales, we also saw a rate benefit within that category, as the business delivered a higher-than-expected mix of full-price sales.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Outside of category mix, we also enjoyed a favorable mix and fulfillment which took two forms.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The first was a stronger-than-expected mix of sales in our stores, which is our lowest cost fulfillment channel.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the third quarter, all of the upside to our comp expectations occurred in our stores.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In addition, within our digital fulfillment options, same-day services drove 80% of our growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And as we've outlined in prior calls, these options have much more favorable cost and profit dynamics compared with shipping to our guests' homes.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On top of category and fulfillment mix, our buying teams continue to develop merchandising strategies that deliver strong margin performance based on our ongoing efforts to optimize costs, pricing, promotions and assortment within each of their individual categories.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In total, our third quarter gross margin rate was up about 110 basis points from a year ago, reflecting the benefits I've cited above, combined with a favorable comparison over some elevated costs reflected in last year's gross margin results.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Specifically, as you'll recall, last year we experienced elevated supply chain expenses in the third quarter, driven by meaningful investments in toy and baby inventory and a rapid buildup of holiday receipts, reflecting the earliest possible timing for the Thanksgiving holiday.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This year given the moderation in our inventory levels and a much later timing for Thanksgiving, we did not experience the same spike in our supply chain costs.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Moving down the P&L, our third quarter SG&A expense rate increased about 20 basis points compared with last year, in line with our expectations.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This increase reflected the retiming of both marketing expenses and store labor from the second quarter, driven primarily by the October launch of Target Circle.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Year-to-date, our SG&A expense rate has improved about 30 basis points from last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This improvement reflects outstanding expense discipline across the organization along with the benefit of lower asset impairments, which are offsetting the impact of investments in store service and training along with wage pressures, driven by very tight labor market conditions across the country.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the depreciation and amortization expense line, we saw an increase of $45 million or 8.5% compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This increase reflects a number of factors including base investment trends, our decision to roll out new flexible store fixtures which accommodate incremental peak capacity for Pick Up and Drive Up orders and the impact of timing compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In total, third quarter operating margin dollars were up more than 22% from last year, reflecting the combination of unexpectedly strong sales and rate performance.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Interest expense was down slightly in the third quarter, reflecting lower average debt balances, while our income tax provision increased approximately 100% compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This increase reflected higher pre-tax earnings this year, combined with the impact of discrete items in last year's results, which made last year's effective tax rate unusually low.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Altogether, our operations generated adjusted EPS of $1.36, an increase of nearly 25% compared with $1.09 last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Third quarter GAAP EPS from continuing operations of $1.37 was up more than 18% from last year when we recorded $0.07 of benefit from the discrete tax items mentioned previously.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now I want to turn to cash flow and our priorities for capital deployment.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And I first want to briefly reiterate those priorities, which have remained consistent for decades.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We first look to fully invest capital in projects that meet our strategic and financial criteria.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Second, we support our dividend and seek to extend the Company record of annual increases in dividend per share, something we've accomplished every year since 1971.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And finally, we use share repurchase to return any excess cash beyond those first two uses with the goal of maintaining our middle A credit ratings.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Turning first to capex, we now expect to spend somewhat less than our original plan of $3.5 billion in 2019 and have an updated spending expectation of approximately $3.1 billion for this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Savings from our original plan are primarily driven by efficiencies we've realized on a portion of our capital projects, combined with a smaller benefit from the retiming of some project spending in the next year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we look ahead, we continue to expect to invest about $3.5 billion in capex in 2020, reflecting our plan to complete nearly 300 additional store remodels for the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In 2021 and beyond, we expect to moderate the pace of our remodels to a range of about 150 to 200 stores per year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With this moderation and the number of remodel projects, we expect our pace of capex will move into the $2.5 billion to $3 billion range annually, closer to the amount of D&A we record on our cash flow statement.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Turning next to inventory.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our third quarter balance sheet showed a decline of nearly $1 billion or about 8% compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: However, given that this inventory position was about 8% higher than two years ago, the year-over-year decline is largely a reflection of the specific inventory investments we made in advance of the fourth quarter last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we approach this year's peak season, we feel very good about both the level and make up of our inventory, which should position us to extend the strong sales and earnings performance we've seen so far this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So with that as context, let's review our capital deployment priorities that played out so far in 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Through the first three quarters of the year, our operations have generated more than $4.1 billion in cash, up more than $500 million from the same period last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We have deployed that cash, along with a portion of our cash on hand at the beginning of the year to fund $2.4 billion of capex paid just under $1 billion in dividends and repurchased about $900 million of our shares.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Over time, the quality of our capital deployment is reflected in our after-tax return on invested capital, which we reported on a trailing 12-month basis.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This measure can be helpful as you evaluate the quality of our Company's business model and the productivity of their investments over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On that basis Target's performance stands tall.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: For the trailing 12 months through the third quarter, our business generated an after-tax return on invested capital of 15.1% excluding discrete impacts from Federal tax reform.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This is the performance many of our peers would love to report.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now let's turn to our outlook for the fourth quarter and how that translates into our full-year performance.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our outlook is based on a bottoms up view of fourth quarter sales and profit drivers, many of which are distinctly different from the rest of the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Specifically, considerations on our outlook for the fourth quarter include the headwind from six fewer holiday shopping days, the benefit from Target Circle, the rapid acceleration in the fourth quarter digital penetration, a much higher sales mix of toys and electronics compared with the rest of the year and the highly promotional nature of the competitive environment.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Altogether, based on recent trends and our evaluation of all of these factors, we expect our business to generate fourth quarter comparable sales growth of 3% to 4%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the operating margin line, our fourth quarter outlook anticipates a small rate increase, driven by a moderate improvement in our gross margin rate, partially offset by smaller increases in both our SG&A and D&A expense rates.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This performance would translate into a mid-to-high single-digit increase in operating margin dollars and an expected range for adjusted EPS of $1.54 to $1.74.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And today, based on our third quarter performance and fourth quarter outlook, we raised our full-year guidance range for adjusted EPS to $6.25 to $6.45.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The midpoint of this new range is $0.30 higher than the midpoint of our prior guidance range.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: If we achieve performance at the midpoint of our expectations that would translate into full-year comparable sales growth of about 4%, operating income dollar growth in the low teens and EPS growth in the mid-to-high teens.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: All of these metrics are much stronger than we anticipated at the beginning of the year, driven by upside in sales, category mix and fulfillment mix within our digital channels.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: At the beginning of the year, Cathy articulated our longer-term financial expectations for the durable financial model we have been developing over the last several years.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This model is based on the ability under normal economic conditions for our business to generate low-single-digit growth in sales, mid-single-digit growth in operating income and high-single-digit growth in EPS or better.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Based on what we've seen so far this year, we are clearly on track to deliver performance meaningfully better than this baseline model in 2019, reflecting some of the unique dynamics we've seen so far.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This outperformance is a testament to the quality of the business model that our teams have been working so hard to create.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And the effort of our teams is something we never take for granted.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It's been remarkable to work closely with these teams and see how they've embraced the change, believing it's the right long-term path for our business.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Results like we are seeing this year are a testament to their efforts and the passion they have for our guests and our brand.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Good morning, and welcome to our 2021 financial community meeting.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We're eager to share our insights on the extraordinary year that just passed as well as our vision for what's next, but I couldn't start today without reflecting on the fact that a year ago at this time, the pandemic was just beginning to unfold, and an in effort to keep everyone safe and to limit travel, we decided to convert this meeting to a virtual format.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: While we miss hosting our in-person gatherings, it's prudent to stick with virtual presentations once again this year, but we're looking forward to resuming our live events, including this one and our annual shareholders' meeting in 2022.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: As I look back over the past year, a year when so much care and compassion was called for, I see purpose coupled with capabilities as the essential enabler of our response.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: The story of Target in 2020 is the story of a team that wanted nothing more than to take care of those around us, drawing on capabilities that were equal to that ambition after years of building and investment.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: I want to start today by publicly recognizing and thanking our team.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: I'm incredibly proud of the resilience, empathy, care, and concern they've shown for each other, our guests, and communities through a very challenging 12 months and counting.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: None of what we'll share today would have happened without them.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Even before the dramatic challenges of last year took hold, our team had been busy building the retail platform of tomorrow, but 2020 accelerated everything and, as such, our guests are already benefiting from and loving that platform today.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: At the heart of the platform was a belief that consumers would continue to flock to our stores for multi-category one-stop shopping, a friendly, well-trained, and knowledgeable team, and joyful experiences.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: As we designed our strategy and invested accordingly, we relentlessly asked ourselves what products and services those stores should offer, where they should be located, how their operations should be tailored to meet neighborhood needs, and ultimately how to make our stores work together with all of our other assets as one shopping platform that would keep guests turning to Target, however, they want to shop.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In answering those questions, we did two things at once.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We placed the physical store more firmly at the center of our omnichannel platform and we created a durable, sustainable, and scalable business model that puts Target on a road of our own.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Our goal was to use our proximity, nearly 1,900 stores within 10 miles of the vast majority of the U.S. consumers, to offer the fastest and easiest digital fulfillment in retail, and the capabilities we've built to become America's easiest place to shop also cracked the essential question of how to grow our digital sales exponentially while maintaining the overall profitability of our business.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: When we began this journey, we didn't know we would be facing a global pandemic, mass quarantines, rapid unemployment, and the need to limit the number of people in public spaces, and yet when those threats emerged in 2020, we were ready, and without hesitation, millions of American families turned to Target like never before.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: That happened because of decisions we made four and five years ago, and today Christina Hennington, our recently named chief growth officer, along with John Mulligan and Michael Fiddelke will join me in mapping out how our team's efforts in recent years created a new baseline from which we'll continue to climb higher for our guests.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Here's what I hope you'll take away from our story: first, that our team's ability to act and react in 2020 was years in the making.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Without our multi-year road map to develop new capabilities and bring them to scale, 2020 could have exposed essential gaps in our business model.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Instead, it proved beyond a doubt the durability of our model and it signaled our potential for continued growth in years ahead.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: The second takeaway stems from a question I've heard frequently, especially in 2020: Brian, what's the secret to Target's growth trajectory?

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: What you'll see in our presentation today is that the one thing that's driving our success is a focused commitment to several things: an integrated collection of strategies and capabilities that all work together and are very difficult to replicate, and ultimately make Target unique.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: I'll start today with a high-level recap of our full-year results.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: When we gathered virtually for this meeting last year, I shared how our revenue had grown by $5.4 billion since 2017 and that we were consistently gaining share in many of our core merchandising categories; in other words, we were already starting to see steady growth from our investments.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: When we left that meeting, no one knew that COVID-19 would be declared a pandemic in the United States only a couple of weeks later.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In hindsight, it's hard to believe that we only received one COVID-related question that day.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: But today as we look back on 2020, the business highlights are clear.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Our revenue during the year increased another $15 billion.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We gained meaningful market share across all five of our merchandising categories, totaling about $9 billion.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Our full-year comparable sales were up more than 19% with a store comp of more than 7% in a year when people were staying home to stay safe, and a digital comp of 145%.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Standing at this meeting three or four years ago, it would have been hard for any of us or any of you to imagine digital penetration of 18% without a dramatic deterioration in our P&L, yet today we announced record-high full-year adjusted EPS of $9.42.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Importantly, we accomplished all of this while making huge incremental investments in our team's safety and wellbeing and completely reoutfitting our stores to keep our team and guests safe.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Far from being a fluke, this performance is further proof that we built a business model that is working as intended, one that puts Target in a category of its own.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: A few consistent pillars have been and will continue to be at the heart of our playbook.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: The enormous investments we made in the supply chain, store operations, and technology capabilities are already powering exponential growth in digital commerce.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: They've enabled us to use our stores as showrooms and service centers, but also as hubs for digital fulfillment.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Without these investments, we simply wouldn't have been able to satisfy the exploding guest demand for same-day services, represented by more than 600% growth in drive-up.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Likewise, Shipt is an extraordinary capability that grew by more than 300% last year and will continue to grow as more guests recognize the power of having their purchases brought to their doorstep in as little as an hour.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We've consistently invested in our merchandising strength like our differentiated own brand portfolio, our curated national brands, inspired limited-time offerings, and strategic relationships that run the gamut from web-only start-ups looking for omnichannel scale to premier partners like Disney, Apple, Levi's, and Ulta Beauty.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We're continuously improving our physical and digital shopping experience, investing billions in store remodels, specialized store roles, and service training for our teams while continuing to open up new small formats in urban centers, major college campuses, and iconic tourist destinations.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Most importantly, we're continuing to invest in our team.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Even before 2020's outsized incremental expenditures on team health and safety, Target was an employer of choice, an academy company for those looking for rewarding and purposeful careers.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In addition to accelerating our $15 starting wage in 2020, we celebrated our team's exceptional efforts with five separate recognition bonuses, most recently in January when we invested another $200 million to reward each of our frontline team member $500.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: As we develop capabilities like Target Circle or acquire them like shipped, we do so with a clear vision for how they'll work together in service for our guests.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Ultimately the value they create in our core business has to contribute to a retail offering that's greater than the sum of the parts, but when we look at these elements individually, it's strikingly clear how much value we've added in a very short time.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In 2016, our digital transformation was only beginning.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We weren't even a top 10 e-commerce provider, and we were just getting our same-day services off the ground.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Today we have the most complete suite of same-day fulfillment services in the industry.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We're one of the leading e-commerce players, and for click and collect same-day services, we continue to deliver industry-leading growth and dollar volume as well as net promoter scores over 80% despite record demand.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In 2016, we had about 30 small-format stores.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Today, we have 140 and will add another 30 to 40 per year over the next several years.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: If these stores were a stand-alone chain, their revenue would rival that of fast-growing chains with many more locations.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In 2016, we launched Pillowfort and Cat and Jack, touching off our own brand reinvention that has since resulted in more than 30 new brands, with more on the way this year.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: By the time we gathered for this meeting last year, Cat and Jack and five other own brands were generating $1 billion or more apiece in annual sales, and that tally has continued to grow.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We cleared 2020 with 10 of our own brands each generating $1 billion or more and four of those crossed the $2 billion per year threshold.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Any one of these brands alone would be a sizable retailer, and as you know, their contribution to profits is outsized.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Of course, owned and exclusive brands are just one component of our merchandising strategy, which has always drawn on curated national brands across our assortment.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: As we've expanded capabilities in recent years, we've also steadily built our roster of strategic partners.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Levi's is an excellent example of how we can build upon a long-standing collaboration and help strategic partners catapult into new product categories.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We started partnering with Levi's years ago on the Denizen denim brand, and that partnership grew to include Levi's Red Tab apparel and built out the presence in hundreds of stores and on target.com.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Just this last Sunday, we launched the Levi's for Target collection, a limited-time offering of home goods.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: This is the first foray by Levi's into this category and it's a great example of combining their strengths with ours, including our incredible sourcing and product design and development capabilities to forge new potential for both of our brands.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Meanwhile, our team is also gearing up to introduce Ulta Beauty at Target to our stores and target.com, starting with the first 100 stores later this year.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: From this initial batch, we'll test, we'll learn, and we'll expand to hundreds of additional locations over time.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: This partnership combines Ulta Beauty's unparalleled assortment, category expertise, and guest loyalty with our large, high-growth, traffic-driving beauty business and the ease and convenience of our fulfillment services.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Together we'll be able to offer guests access to established, emerging, and prestige beauty brands as well as expert beauty consultation in an industry-leading omnichannel retail experience.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: As a stand-alone or isolated innovation, each of these elements I mentioned has something in common with the other.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Each was advanced based on how it would complement our other assets and capabilities, and we tested each one with an eye toward scale.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In fact, the ability to integrate and scale is a key component of our decision-making, and to emphasize the critical importance of scalability, I simply think back to what we could have done in 2016 but didn't.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: At that time, conventional wisdom held that the only way forward was for retailers to build capacity to send more packages to homes.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Instead, we went our own way, built a fulfillment model with our guest's local store at the center, and took the initiative on same day.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We could just as easily have constructed additional fulfillment centers and driven the shift to digital sales with more ship-to-home capacity, but as you know, the economics were terrible and we wouldn't have been differentiated.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In short, we didn't see the textbook solution as scalable or as likely to do what we've done, namely set the groundwork for years of guest satisfaction and brand loyalty as represented by comments like this: Thank you for providing curbside pick-up, it actually was the determining factor in me buying from Target instead of one of those online retailers; or this, or this, or this note from a guest who simply said, please always continue to do curbside pick-up, it is such a help even outside of COVID.

sentence: So where do we go from here and how do we keep climbing from this strong new baseline?

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Throughout the pandemic, we built deep trust and loyalty with our guests who clearly prefer the ease and everyday inspiration of shopping at Target along with our relentless commitment to the safety and cleanliness of our shopping environment.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: This is a decades-long commitment that was only emphasized by the pandemic, and it will continue to be a differentiator in the months and years ahead.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Our multi-category merchandise portfolio is a huge advantage particularly as shoppers continue to consolidate trips, and we're absolutely committed to delivering value and everyday affordability, which is important in any environment but particularly as the economic consequences of COVID continue to play out.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: At the same time, we'll continue to listen closely to our stakeholders and to build upon our strategy, so in the years ahead you'll see continuous iteration and improvement in the pillars I've mentioned already, but we'll also focus on better localizing our experience, applying learning from our small format expansion, and we'll continue to build skill in personalizing the experience, leveraging capabilities like Target Circle to better understand our guests and find new ways to engage and reward the 90 million members who have joined so far.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: To ensure we're continuously delivering great value and emphasizing everyday affordability, we'll stay laser-focused on being price right daily and on showcasing our value with clear messaging and relevant promotions.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Importantly, we'll also double down on an approach to sustainability that builds on our rich legacy and company purpose.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: This includes decades of community relations, corporate responsibility, and philanthropic leadership grounded in our 75-year track record of giving 5% of our pre-tax profits in support of vibrant and inclusive communities.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Our intent is to further use our size and scale to benefit people and the planet, building on the work we've done already to elevate our offering of sustainable brands, to create equity and opportunity in our communities, and to help protect the environment.

sentence: To do it, we're testing a new type of facility here in Minneapolis called a sortation center.

sentence: The idea is to make our stores as hub model even more efficient while also reducing our load on external carriers.

sentence: Take a look.[Commercial break]This capability frees up time and space in our stores which we can redirect into fulfilling more orders.

sentence: While we're still ramping up production at this first test facility, we're very confident in this concept and plan to open five additional sites in other urban markets later this year.

sentence: With our small format strategy, we'll expand in urban markets like Portland, L.A., and New York City where there are still opportunities to serve new guests, and we'll continue our focus on college stores with the University of Georgia and the University of Michigan planned for later this year.

sentence: We remain extremely bullish on our college sites.

sentence: Even as the pandemic sent students to online classrooms and sales softened at many of those stores, we see them as a long-term play to serve the college guests, many of whom are on the brink of adulthood and building lifelong shopping habits.

sentence: We'll also open a number of midsized stores to serve dense suburban neighborhoods from Denver to Brooklyn.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As hundreds of retail vacancies have left holes in communities across the country, we've committed to sites where we can fill a need for the local guests.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As retail real estate prices have declined this year, we've found these opportunities to serve new communities to be even more affordable.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Along with opening new stores, we'll get back to remodeling our existing fleet.

sentence: After stopping our full store remodels last spring, we'll pick back up later this year and complete about 150 stores in time for holiday and we'll plan to ramp up to more than 200 stores a year in 2022 and beyond.

sentence: Safety and ease have become the heart of Target's shopping experience and we'll incorporate what we learned during 2020 into our future store design.

sentence: That includes implementing more contactless features from our restrooms to our checkouts and adding distance between merchandise and at the check lanes.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As you heard from Christina, we'll also bring brand partnerships to life in our stores throughout 2021.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: A great example is the word we'll do to add Ulta Beauty to our sales floor, creating a specialty environment that's seamlessly integrated into the Target experience.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Similarly, we'll use store design elements to highlight additional brands like Disney and Apple for our guests.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We're investing in a lot of really exciting developments to fuel Target's growth, but what they all have in common, they're giving our team the tools and the backdrop to take better care of our guests and each other.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: That shows up most in our stores where the vast majority of our 350,000 team members bring our brand to life for guests across the country.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: A huge priority for our stores this year is adjusting our staffing strategies to create more predictability for our team.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: That's a challenge in any retail job where hours are based on dynamic factors like consumer shopping patterns and changing team needs.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: But we know having an engaged team with more consistent hours leads to higher productivity, greater efficiency, and lower turnover.

sentence: It creates a place where people join to learn a job and stay to build a career and better serve our guests in the long run, so we'll train team members to take on other roles across the store and offer the option for longer shifts.

sentence: We'll also build on our stores' operating model by introducing a new standard of service to our teams.

sentence: It's not a checklist but a set of principles that define great service, like welcoming a guest and paying attention to what they need, which might be as simple as finding an item or as big as building an outfit.

sentence: It's meant to give our team flexibility and empower them to do what's right for the guests in the moment.

sentence: Without our team, everything else you heard today comes to a standstill.

sentence: The Target team continues to be the most important part of our operation, and I want to say an enormous thank you to all our team members for all they do to serve our guests and our communities.

sentence: You've seen us make a lot of operational investments over the last few years in our team, in our stores, and in our capacity for long-term growth.

sentence: In the most recent quarter, those returns were clear.

sentence: We've created an operation unlike anyone else with our physical assets working together, centered on our stores, and fueled by our team to serve our guests and grow for the long term.

sentence: The capabilities we've built not only allowed us to navigate the most volatile time in retail history but show that they can flex and grow to serve the ever-changing needs of the consumer.

sentence: The work isn't done.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We're constantly refining an operation that is efficient, fast, and supportive of Target's durable and scalable business model.

sentence: From an engineer by training and a finance guy at heart, I can attest that you can't get too efficient or relevant enough.

sentence: There's no finish line for continuous improvement in innovation.

sentence: We have a lot of strength heading into 2021 and a lot of work still in front of us, but with a sound operational foundation and the talent and resilience of the Target team driving us ahead, I look forward to sharing our progress in the quarters and years to come.

sentence: With that, Michael, I'll hand it over to you.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: [Commercial break]All I can say is wow, those news clips paint a vivid picture of the rollercoaster our team and our business experienced throughout 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: All in all, it was a standout year in which everything we've spent years developing and building came together to serve our guests like never before.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Today after a year of record growth, I want to start my remarks by expanding on a point Brian mentioned earlier because investors often want to know, how much of Target's growth is being driven by specific strategies or specific assets?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: For example, they want to know if we can isolate how much of our growth is coming from drive-up, from digital in total, our own brand work, the remodel program, and any other way we can slice and dice the data.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I understand the impulse.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our internal team often wants to do the same thing, and of course, as a self-described data geek, I'm inclined to think the same way.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But then I see data like we first shared with you last year, guests who tried drive-up for the first time spend about 30% more on average compared with before, including an increase in conventional store shopping, and we see a similar change in behavior among guests who try Shipt for the first time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: These findings demonstrate that the benefits of drive-up and shipped go far beyond the value of an individual trip.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: They're both capabilities that drive guests' affinity, creating value that extends well beyond the services themselves.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That same thinking applies to our merchandise categories.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: If you focus only on the amount of sales or growth by category, you can miss how they all work together to drive guest affinity.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I see how this plays out with my own family.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Over the next few months, the cold weather in Minnesota will finally end and my kids will need warm weather clothes.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the next Saturday morning Target run, we'll shop for those clothes and we'll also pick up some food, a few office supplies, laundry detergent, and maybe a prescription from CVS.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We might wander over and purchase some spring decor, and we'll probably need some more earbuds since the kids seem to be inventing new ways to lose or destroy them.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On our way out, we'll probably stop at the Starbucks near the entrance so my wife and I can enjoy a coffee on the way home.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now if you're going to analyze that basket, is there a way to know which category drove the trip, and beyond the basket itself, shouldn't we broaden the analysis even further since that trip depended on a conveniently located store that's clean, safe and fun to shop, featuring low everyday prices and a friendly and engaged team?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Over time, I've come to understand that guest engagement and financial performance are driven by everything we're doing at the same time, not any factor in isolation.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among the critical factors, of course, there are the tangible assets that show up on our balance sheet, including our stores, distribution centers, and technology, but the list goes way beyond the balance sheet and includes our team, our reputation, and the trust we've established with multiple stakeholders, which only deepened in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Then there's the Target brand itself.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our own and exclusive brands, capabilities like marketing, merchandising, product design and development, sourcing and so much more, and of course there's our culture, our mission, and our values which help to unify a diverse and widely dispersed team in support of a common purpose.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So what's the key to our future performance?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It's our continued investments in the assets and capabilities, both tangible and intangible, that we can build and integrate to drive guest engagement and growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: How should we determine what to focus on?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The answer comes from continually listening carefully to our guests.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The better we know them, the more effectively we can invest in what they want and develop new ways to deliver joy and inspiration while making their lives easier.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: If we invest the right way, guests will reward us with more engagement and growth, which in turn will create additional opportunities to invest.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our success in 2020 which was years in the making is a perfect example.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It started many years ago as we engaged in a comprehensive evaluation of our business, our strategy, and took a deep dive into the wants and needs of our guests.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That work led to a new strategic focus followed by years of investment of both capital and expense to roll out new fulfillment capabilities, rejuvenated stores and brands, a modern store operating model, and more.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Through that work, we've built the foundation that allowed our team to deliver unprecedented results in the face of a rapidly changing landscape in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This year, our focus is to lock in last year's gains, build on that foundation, continue to deepen guest engagement and drive long-term growth, and following last year's growth of $15 billion, more than we grew over the prior 11 years combined, we're entering 2021 as a much larger company with a host of opportunities to build on last year's success.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Digital is one of those opportunities.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As John mentioned, in 2020 the penetration of digital sales advanced many years in a single year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With COVID as the catalyst, guests who had never tried our digital services quickly changed their habits and tried them sooner than they would have otherwise.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We've long told you that on average, a multi-channel guest spends nearly four times as much as a store-only guest and nearly 10 times more than a digital-only guest.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now just in case, there are any stats majors listening, that's a statement about correlation, not causation, so I'm not saying that a guest spending immediately changes that much after they move into a new channel.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Even so, these averages help us to understand how deepening engagement translates to a more valuable guest relationship, and last year Target gained an additional 12 million multi-channel guests.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Of course, a portion of those guests were completely new to Target, but the vast majority had previously shopped with us but only in a single channel.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The opportunity this year is to build on our now deeper relationship with these guests as we engage with them more frequently and help them migrate toward the much higher average spend we see from our multi-channel guests over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Today, even though we already have an unmatched suite of digital fulfillment options, there's more we can do for our guests.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: One way is to continue expanding the assortment of fresh, refrigerated, and frozen food items available for pick-up and drive-up.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: When we studied the behavior of guests who first shopped for these items through one of these services last year, we saw an average increase in shopping frequency of about one visit per month compared with a control group.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On average, these guests increased their food and beverage spending between 20% and 30% and, importantly, spent about 20% more in other categories.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you heard from Christina, we also have an opportunity to continue developing and launching new own brands while we become an increasingly attractive partner for leading national brands.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the years ahead, we'll likely have many more partnership opportunities, and given our strong performance and financial position can be very thoughtful in approaching every one of them.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This begins by ensuring the partnership is right for our guests and that the partner and financial arrangement are appropriate long-term choices for our business.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Of course, there's a huge opportunity to create value through Target Circle, which has grown in less than two years to include more than 90 million members.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Circle is easy and free to join, and members enjoy rewards that drive engagement directly, which we can measure by the increase in spending among guests who join.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But the value of Circle only begins there because it also helps us to gain an ongoing, deeper understanding of our guests and their changing preferences, helping us to connect them with the services, brands, and categories that address those wants and needs.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It's clear that we're entering 2021 with a lot of momentum and a really strong foundation, with a lot more room to grow.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you heard from John, we still have a long runway to expand the available assortment for our same-day services while we invest to broaden Shipt's reach by entering new markets while expanding in existing ones.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: When we acquired Shipt in late 2017, we were confident that same-day delivery was a capability every successful retailer would need to have, and we have spent the last three years integrating Shipt into our strategy and operations.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: At the same time, the acquisition has made it easier for Shipt to grow and achieve scale in new markets, given the volume that Target immediately brings to the platform.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As John covered, we're investing to modernize our network and add replenishment capacity to support future growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Obviously, we came into last year with a great deal of capacity, but we used up a lot more of it than expected.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Here's one way to think about it: at our current average sales per store, last year's growth of $15 billion was equivalent to the addition of more than 300 new Target stores.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: If we had actually opened that many new locations, we'd have needed some additional upstream capacity, and that need is the same whether growth is coming from a bigger store footprint or higher productivity in our existing footage.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While I'm on the topic, I want to pause and address the question of whether our stores are going to run out of capacity to grow digital sales.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I'd start with what John mentioned earlier, how our top quartile stores demonstrate the continued potential for our average stores to handle more throughput.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But I want to drill down into a really specific example to provide another view of our untapped capacity and what we can do when an individual location reaches its limit.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: To do that, I'm going to go way back in history and talk about our experience at the Target store in Colma, California, part of the San Francisco market.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Twenty years ago, Colma had grown to be our second-highest volume store in the chain, generating more than $90 million in annual sales, nearly three times our chain average at the time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Given its extreme volume, we suspected the store was running out of capacity, which was limiting its ability to grow, so when the site of a former Montgomery Ward's became available just across the highway in Daly City, we decided to buy it and build a new Target.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This was unheard of in our history, building a new store less than a mile away from an existing one, and it was a calculated risk because the new store would only make sense if it drove incremental volume.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's exactly what happened.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The combined sales of the two stores quickly grew far beyond what the single store was able to generate, and today each of those locations is in the top 5% of our stores based on sales volume.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Let's come back to today.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Last year, our stores fulfilled more than 95% of our total sales, which works out to an average of about $47 million in fulfilled sales per store.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That means our average store today is fulfilling about half of what the Colma store was already supporting 20 years ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This offers another clear window into the growth potential of our average store today.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But will there sometimes be extreme examples of stores that hit their capacity?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I hope so because we know what to do when that happens.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: If we have a viable real estate opportunity nearby, we can invest in another of these modern, multi-channel assets we happen to call a Target store.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: To be clear, based on what we see today, we don't expect a lot of these opportunities over the next few years, but I'd love to be wrong about that since we'd likely generate strong returns on the new stores we could open in those markets.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the meantime, we continue to make productive investments in new small-format stores, and we're eager to begin ramping up our remodel program in 2021 and beyond.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With all these options to generate profitable growth, we're in a position to play offense and lean into the opportunity to build on last year's momentum.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As such, we're planning for annual CAPEX in the $4 billion range in each of the next few years to support remodels, new stores, and supply chain projects that add replenishment capacity and modernize the network, including sortation centers.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Beyond full store remodels, we'll also invest in Ulta Beauty shop-in-shops while optimizing front-end space in our highest volume locations, increasing the efficiency of our pick-up and drive-up services.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now this is the section of my remarks in which you'd typically expect me to cover our P&L expectations for the year, but today given the high level of uncertainty we continue to face, providing a lot of guidance would be an exercise in false precision.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Instead, I'm going to spend a few minutes talking about the most important factors affecting our near-term plans as we maintain our laser focus on investing for the long term.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: First, as I think about implications for Target's top line in the months and years ahead, I think about the drivers as three levels of a funnel.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: At the widest part of the funnel are macro factors, including uncertainty about the path of COVID-19 and the speed and effectiveness of the vaccine campaign; how consumer attitudes and behaviors will evolve as we emerge from the pandemic, for example, there's an emerging consensus that the nature of work will permanently change as employers move to a more flexible model and allow for more work from home.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This will likely have long-lasting implications for consumer spending.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And finally, beyond changes in the consumer mindset, macro considerations include the health of the economy, the near-term impact of the stimulus, and how quickly various industries and communities will recover from the pandemic.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The middle stage of the funnel involves questions around potential industry trends in each of the categories we sell, and every industry has its own story.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In categories consumed mostly at home, including food and beverage, essentials, home, and hard lines, industry trends have accelerated over the last year and could see some softness as we emerge from the crisis; however, the timing and extent is hard to predict and could be offset by permanent changes in consumer habits, including a higher percentage of work time spent at home and an elevated focus on cleanliness and health resulting from the pandemic.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the beauty and apparel industries, which experienced softness in 2020, trends are expected to improve over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Specifically, as people resume working in offices, attending concerts, movies and sporting events, traveling and eating out, they're likely to focus more on their appearance and spend more on these categories than they did in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But let's be clear, these are just quick high-level thoughts on potential industry trends and they're far from ironclad predictions, so as we move to the bottom of the funnel and think about how those trends are likely to play out at Target, we first need to think about market share within those industries.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the topic of share, we have a lot of confidence as we look ahead.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In 2020, Target saw unprecedented share gains across all five of our core merchandise categories.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Importantly, these gains were not limited to the categories in which others were forced to close and they stayed remarkably consistent throughout the year and across the country.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Based on this experience and our investment focus going forward, we're optimistic about our opportunity to lock in recent share gains and deliver long-term growth on top of the foundation we've already established.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now I want to move beyond the top line and illustrate how we're thinking about other lines on the P&L for the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In this discussion, beyond prior-year comparisons, I will often be looking back to 2019, since that year provides a more stable baseline compared with the extreme volatility we encountered in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Let's start with the gross margin line where in 2020, we experienced large but offsetting variances related to specific factors.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The first was supply chain and digital fulfillment costs which drove about 110 basis points of pressure last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While that headwind was notable, it was less than I believe most of us would have expected given that we saw $10 billion of digital sales growth accounting for two-thirds of our total growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we look ahead to this year and beyond, we expect to see a smaller amount of pressure from the supply chain in digital fulfillment given that digital growth is likely to moderate, and we continue to make progress in reducing average unit fulfillment costs.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: A second headwind to last year's gross margin rate was category mix as lower-margin categories grew faster than our higher-margin categories, accounting for about 90 basis points of rate pressure.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: At a minimum this year, we expect category mix to exert less pressure than last year, and notably, it could easily become a tailwind like it was in prior years.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: However, our crystal ball is not nearly clear enough today to predict this year's category mix with any precision.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The third factor in last year's gross margin performance was our merchandising decisions, which include our pricing, mix of owned and national brands, and the magnitude of our promotional and clearance markdowns.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In 2020, the combination of these factors provided a significant tailwind of about 150 basis points, driven primarily by favorability in markdowns.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: A portion of this favorability was related to promotions, but the biggest single factor was a significant decline in clearance markdown rates as demand in seasonal and other clearance-sensitive categories far outpaced our expectations.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In 2021, we expect our markdown rates will increase somewhat from these abnormally low levels, which will create some gross margin pressure compared with 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So how do these expectations come together in 2021?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we consider the range of expectations for the combined impact of these three drivers, we believe that our 2021 gross margin rate will remain somewhat lower than our 2019 gross margin rate of 28.9%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the SG&A expense line this year, we'll be annualizing last year's significant investments in safety measures and team member pay and benefits.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We'll also be annualizing the fixed cost and other scale benefits we realized throughout the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Looking ahead, given that we're focused on locking in last year's gains, we expect to retain significant scale benefits compared with 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In addition, we expect to deliver continued efficiency improvements driven by investments in our supply chain, technology, and operating model, which will help to offset continued investments in our team.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: All together, we expect that our 2021 SG&A expense rate will also be lower than our 2019 rate of 20.8%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the D&A expense line, we expect to see moderate dollar growth in 2021 as we ramp up remodels and accelerate depreciation on the assets we replace.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Of course, rate performance will depend on the total sales we deliver this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So as we consider how all of these rates come together on the operating margin line, we're facing a wide range of possibilities as we enter the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I've already talked about the unpredictability of sales and how category and channel mix alone can impact our margin, but even with that uncertainty, we should continue to benefit from the leverage we gained in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Altogether, our expectation is that this year's operating margin rate will move down from the 7% we recorded in 2020 but remain above our 2019 operating margin rate of 6%, with the most likely outcome in the lower half of that range.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now for those of you hoping we'd provide a more precise view of our expectations today, I want you to know that I feel the same way.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I know that it's difficult to model our business right now.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our team is facing the same challenge.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the face of this uncertainty, we continue to put a huge premium on flexibility and agility which served us extremely well throughout 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: After all, flexibility is a cornerstone of our business model which features a uniquely diverse category mix and a store-based fulfillment model that can quickly adapt to changes in guest shopping patterns.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With the benefit of this model, an outstanding team, and a strong balance sheet, we're perfectly positioned to navigate any near-term uncertainty while we continue to invest in long-term growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While it may sound counterintuitive, our expectations for the next few quarters feel cloudier than our view of the longer term, when we're highly confident in our ability to grow profitably and build on recent share gains.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now before I move beyond the P&L, I want to spend a minute talking about the prior year comparisons we're facing in the first two quarters of this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you'll recall, in the first quarter last year, sales accelerated meaningfully after the onset of COVID, but our gross margin rate for the quarter declined an astounding amount, more than four percentage points in light of the cost to right-size our apparel inventory.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Also in the first quarter, we began making meaningful investments in the health and safety of our team and guests, which we've maintained throughout the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Altogether, our first-quarter earnings per share were down more than 60% compared with 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Contrast that with the second quarter last year, when our comp sales grew more than 24%, our gross margin rate also increased, and we saw a jaw-dropping amount of leverage on the SG&A and D&A expense lines which more than offset investments in team and guest safety.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As a result, last year's second-quarter EPS grew more than 80% compared with 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's a swing of more than 140 percentage points in our EPS growth rates between Q1 and Q2 last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we plan and analyze our performance in the first two quarters of 2021, we're going to lean heavily on comparisons to the much more stable environment we experienced in 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This will help all of us to look through the extreme volatility in year-over-year comparisons we'll be seeing throughout the first half of this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now let's move beyond the P&L and turn to cash and capital deployment.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I want to reiterate that our priorities remain the same as they have been for decades.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: First, we look to invest in the business in all of the projects that meet our strategic and financial criteria.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Second, we look to support the dividend and build on our record of annual increases, which we've maintained every year since 1971.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: One note, if we attain that goal in 2021, it will mark our 50th consecutive year of uninterrupted dividend increases, putting us in a very small group of companies who can make that statement.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Finally, we look to deploy excess cash through share repurchases only after we've fully supported the first two goals within the capacity of our middle-A credit ratings.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you know, last year turned out to be a very strong year for cash flow in light of our sales growth and strong operational performance.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As a result, we ended the year with about $8.5 billion of cash, well beyond the amount we'd maintain in ordinary times; but as strong as our year turned out to be, we can't forget the volatility we just encountered and the environment today remains far from ordinary.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It's in that context that we evaluate our 2021 capital deployment expectations.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Regarding CAPEX, I already outlined our plan to invest about $4 billion this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Regarding the dividend, later this year we expect to recommend that our board approve a robust increase in the per-share dividend, but as always this recommendation will depend on how our business is performing.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Beyond those priorities, we have resumed share repurchases this year and, depending on how the virus, the economy, and our performance progresses, could have ample capacity within the limits of our middle-A credit ratings.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But I will quickly say we'll continue to be cautious and maintain an ample amount of liquidity to carry us through a wide range of near-term scenarios.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As such, it may be a multi-year journey before our credit metrics move fully back to historical levels, depending on the speed with which we see more normal volatility across the economy and our business.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now I want to turn to our after-tax ROIC.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we've long emphasized, we rely on this metric to assess the health of our business and the effectiveness of our capital deployment over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: However, as is often the case, we sometimes need to look past near-term volatility, and 2020 presents a great example.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's because last year, we delivered an astounding after-tax ROIC of 23.5%, up more than seven percentage points from already strong performance in 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While this outcome is remarkable and a testament to our team and operating model, I'm going to quickly say that it's artificially high and likely to come back down over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That might sound like a strange thing to say, but it's based on a number of factors that are clear today.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: First, with unexpectedly strong sales, our inventory turns shot up last year and we saw abnormally high payables leverage.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While that had a positive near-term impact on working capital, we also saw really choppy in-stocks which isn't how we want to operate under normal conditions.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In 2021, we're planning for full shelves and better in-stocks, which will bring inventory turns and payables leverage back down to more sustainable levels.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This will require a net investment of working capital for the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Similarly, as I mentioned earlier, we're leaning in to support a strong set of growth opportunities over the next few years.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we accelerate investment in stores, supply chain modernization, and replenishment capacity in support of those growth prospects, we'll likely see an increase in the invested capital portion of this metric over the next few years.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Bottom line, while I believe this metric will stay very healthy and compare favorably to other retailers, I expect it will move back down into the 20% range over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This would represent very strong absolute and relative performance on a larger asset base than we've maintained in the past.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As I get ready to turn things back over to Brian, I want to take you back to this meeting four years ago when I was listening from our headquarters in Minneapolis.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: During my career at Target, I've been lucky to spend time working with our stores and I've developed a deep appreciation for the value they can deliver, so when Brian and John stood up and said we'd be investing to put our stores at the center of everything we do, including both digital and physical shopping, I had a ton of confidence in that plan.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It was a plan based on carefully listening to our guests, it was differentiated, and we were fortunate to have the necessary resources to get there.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the years following that meeting, our team worked hard and we encountered many doubters, but we continued to invest with a long view, and last year's results showed the value of that focus.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we sit here today, we remain committed to making future investments with that same long view.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Rather than sitting back, taking a break, and waiting for the virus to subside, we are focused on playing offense and investing in continued growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Just like four years ago, my confidence in the future starts with the team, so I want to acknowledge everyone on the Target team from headquarters to our distribution centers, to our stores in all 50 states and our offices around the world for their dedication to our guests and passion for taking care of each other.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Without you, we couldn't have delivered such an amazing amount of value on behalf of our stakeholders in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And with your help, I'm confident we'll continue to deliver long-term value for all of our stakeholders in the years ahead.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I can't say it enough.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now I'll turn it back over to Brian for some closing remarks.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Thanks, Michael.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: As we wind down today's event, I'll leave you with a couple of thoughts.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Five years ago, we envisioned a future for ourselves in which the key to guest preference and breakout growth lay in an unappreciated omnichannel asset called the store.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Many were skeptical, which is why we said from the beginning that we were playing our own game in creating a category of one.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Many thought the inevitable drift was for our store guests to become digital guests and that the current only ran in one direction.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We saw something different.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We saw a future in which even the most committed digital-only guests would find the best and easiest shopping experience at Target because of how we connect that experience to our stores.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We knew that to make our stores function for the future that we envisioned, we'd have to build, acquire and bundle a unique set of capabilities: the technology, the supply chain inventiveness, the physical assets and operations, and the team of trusted neighbors that millions turned to for friendly service and a bit of everyday joy.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We began to put all those pieces together like no one else had, and the experience was taking hold on the timetable we expected, then 2020 accelerated everything, and today Target is as synonymous with same day and safety as it with style and swagger.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: That is a very strong position to be in.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Here's where we intend to go with it.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: First, we'll continue to focus on market share over the long term.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We believe our experience, including our fulfillment options, inspiring assortment, ease, safety, and personal service will convert more and more consumers into guests, and we'll also work tirelessly to engage established guests across more of our channels and offerings.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: With new guests choosing Target and established guests engaging with more of our platform, we'll be able to listen to them even more closely, and capabilities like drive-up, Shipt, and Circle will give us a wider window than ever into their preferences, meaning we can further improve the experience we provide in the near term while continuously anticipating where we should go next.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Staying closely connected to our guests always points us in the right direction.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: That's what helped us see a future five years ago that today is a reality.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: It's why we're stepping up our investments to drive additional profitable growth.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Unlike in recent years when we needed to shore up our foundation or create new capabilities, today's investments will build on an omnichannel Target platform that is already working incredibly well, a platform that has raised expectations not just among Target guests but for consumers across the U.S. retailing.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Few can meet those expectations like we can because what we've created is based on a unique combination of differentiated assets, but this is just the beginning of our story on which we'll continue to iterate, innovate, and continuously improve for our guests.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In closing, I want to express my complete confidence in this company's future.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: I'm confident in our strategy and in our capabilities, and above all I'm confident in our team.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: They know that no platform succeeds without purpose and that our ambitions are always informed by the millions of families we serve.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: The results we're sharing today and what we envision for the future simply wouldn't be possible without the best team in the business.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: I want to thank them once again for all they do for Target, our guests, and communities.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Finally, I want to thank you for joining our financial community meeting.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We appreciate your interest in Target, your engagement in our journey, and your long-term investment in a growth horizon that we believe will remain bright for years to come.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: We look forward to hearing from you in the Q&A portion of our program.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: I'll turn it back to John Hulbert to move us into that discussion.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: John Hulbert Thanks, Brian.

sentence: But again, if you're planning to access the Q&A session in listen-only mode, your best option is to stay on this webcast even if you received an invitation.

speaker: Chris Horvers
sentence: Thanks, good morning.
