sentence: We are tripling the number of Disney stores at Target locations and doubling our Apple shop-in-shop experiences.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: On top of that, of course, this will be our debut holiday season featuring Ulta Beauty at Target.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: And on the subject of Ulta Beauty at Target, our guests are telling us it's clearly hitting the bullseye, with makeup, skincare, bath and body, hair care, and fragrance for more than 50 top brands now available at Ulta Beauty at Target, both in-stores and online.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: There's plenty to love about this new partnership, and we are so excited for all that is yet to come.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: And we'll build on our tradition of joy-making partnerships this December, when we will launch an exclusive lifestyle collection of products with one of the most beloved toy brands ever, Lego.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: Think brick-inspired hooded sweatshirts, colorful Lego-shaped tumblers, and, of course, iconic Lego brick and mini figure sets.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: This collection builds on our long-standing partnership with the Lego Group and reflects our shared values of inclusivity, optimism, and joy.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: With nearly 300 must-haves for the family, pets, and home, and most of the colorful brick-inspired items under $30, our guests are sure to find something everyone would love on any budget.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: Joy, ease, value, inclusivity, the ingredients helping to deliver on our purpose: to help all families discover the joy of everyday life, a recipe that we refine quarter after quarter by listening to our guests, learning from their choices, and working across our talented team.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: And these plans wouldn't come to life without the many talents and contributions of our dedicated team.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: So, with deep gratitude and humility, I want to thank our team for serving the communities, for showing up every day for our guests and each other, and for bringing Target's values to life.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: You inspire me with all that you do.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: And because of you, I know we will win this holiday season.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: With that, I'll turn the call over to John.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Thanks, Christina.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Everyday, across the operations team, we focus on execution.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: On our supply chain team, the focus is on moving the right amount of inventory to the right place at the right time.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In our stores, which fulfill more than 95% of our total sales, the team focuses on delivering a great guest experience across hundreds of millions of guest transactions every quarter.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And on our properties team, the team focuses on optimizing our physical footprint, including the planning and construction of new stores and distribution facilities, along with our investments to maintain and enhance the productivity of our existing buildings.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Of course, all of these aspects of operations matter all year long.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: But in the fourth quarter, when we handle the largest volumes of the year, everything moves faster, making the need for detailed planning and precise execution even greater.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: That's why every year, we construct our plans with the fourth quarter in mind, so we can remove distractions and roadblocks in advance of the holiday peak.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: That means, on the properties team, we plan our remodel and new store projects, so they're completed before the holidays, and our technology team rolls out new systems and tools on the same timeline.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In the supply chain and in our stores, we carefully plan the ramp-up of seasonal hiring and team member training in advance of the holidays so everyone is ready to handle the additional volume.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: That's what happens every year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: But as Brian and Christina have already mentioned, this year, our teams have been facing additional out-of-the-ordinary challenges as they plan for and deliver record-setting volumes while facing unprecedented bottlenecks in the global supply chain.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: So while I'm lucky to work with our amazing team every day, it's at times like these that our team shines brightest.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Beyond their skill and expertise, they face every challenge with good nature and a collaborative mindset.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: I can't describe how proud I am to represent everything they've accomplished this year as they've delivered historically strong growth on top of record increases a year ago.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Within our supply chain, the team has been methodically working around multiple obstacles and challenges throughout the network, prioritizing our holiday-sensitive categories within our import receipts while thoughtfully planning domestic transportation to ensure products reach the shelf at the right time, and while we continue to see some periodic outages across different items and categories, wearing the holidays with a very healthy inventory position overall.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Specifically, at the end of the third quarter, inventory on the balance sheet was more than $2 billion higher than last year, representing growth of about 18% from a year ago.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Looking back to the pre-COVID period, our Q3 ending inventory has grown more than $3.5 billion since the end of Q3 2019, representing 31% growth over a two-year period.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: A sizable amount of this inventory will continue to flow to our stores over the next few weeks, and our team has clear visibility to where the inventory is located and when it will arrive in our stores.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In our overseas operations, we've benefited from a significant reduction in delay times.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And, of course, given that we were already anticipating tight conditions many months ago, the team has been writing this year's holiday purchase orders much earlier than last year to proactively mitigate the risk of both known and unexpected delays.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We're also benefiting from really strong performance across our domestic transportation network.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And we've secured the necessary capacity across both rail and over-the-road trucking to accommodate anticipated shipments throughout the fourth quarter.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: At the intersection of our overseas and domestic supply chains, the team continues to work around significant port delays, diverting shipments to less-congested entry points and relying on air freight in certain cases.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And while Target's port operations have long been considered best in class, our team has been actively collaborating with government and port officials to help find solutions that will allow everyone's containers to move through the ports more quickly.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And we're encouraged with the changes that have recently been put in place.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: I also want to pause and emphasize the ongoing collaboration that's been happening between our supply chain, merchandising, and marketing teams.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These teams have worked together to develop promotional and marketing plans that are much more fluid and nimble than in the past, enabling the incorporation of real-time data on inventory availability and location within our holiday plans in order to maximize their impact to the benefit of both our guests and operations.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In our stores, the team is preparing for fourth quarter all year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And they're energized and ready to serve our guests throughout the season.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: This will be the first holiday season since we launched our new service initiative, which is all about empowering our teams and increasing their confidence to build authentic connections with our guests.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Also, new this year, we've rolled out a new point-of-sale system across more than 90% of our stores, providing more speed, efficiency, and enhanced experience at both the checkout and our service counter.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: To continue building on an industry-leading in-store pickup and Drive Up experiences, we've been rolling out new capabilities all year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These efforts include capital projects to add permanent storage capacity in more than 200 high-volume stores, investing in flexible fixtures to provide temporary storage areas to support seasonal peak, adding thousands of new items to the list available for pickup and Drive Up, doubling the number of Drive Up parking stalls compared with last year, and designating stall numbers to help our teams deliver Drive Up orders more efficiently.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Even as we're adding these new capabilities, we're also supporting our long-standing commitment to providing a safe shopping experience, maintaining the enhanced COVID cleaning and safety routines that we implemented throughout the pandemic.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We've also been investing in team member hours, processes, and training to prepare our team to handle record freight and fulfillment volumes this year, all on enhancing safety messaging and actively monitoring processes to protect the safety of both our guests and our team.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And, of course, as Brian mentioned, our team is focused on being fully staffed across the store and supply chain throughout the holiday season.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Our stores have been hitting our seasonal hiring milestones.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And because of the advancements we've made in scheduling this year, average hours per store team member are running significantly higher this year in comparison to past years.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In fact, unlike what you're hearing from many others, because of the investments we've made in pay and benefits and our focus on team member training and engagement, the hourly turnover rate in our stores is actually running lower this year compared with 2019, particularly for our newly hired team members.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And we're continuing to invest in our team.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Following the recent rollout of the most comprehensive debt-free education program in the industry, we announced that to sustain our momentum through the holidays, we're offering pay premiums during peak periods in our stores and distribution centers over the holiday season.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As we've said many times, our investments in the team are the most productive ones we've made.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Turning to the work of the properties team, we expect to finish about 145 remodels in 2021, having completed more than 40 remodels prior to the end of Q3 with more than 100 additional projects slated to wrap up before the holiday.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: The team also opened another 15 new stores in the third quarter, bringing the year-to-date total up to 30.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Among those projects, we've opened new stores ranging from 11,000 to 160,000 square feet, which demonstrates the flexibility we've developed to design the optimal store size for an individual neighborhood based on their local needs and available real estate in the market.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: To increase the capacity and efficiency of our supply chain, our team has also opened two new distribution centers this year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, we have two new sortation centers set to open in the fourth quarter, with two more on track to open early next year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While our supply chain has had to address a host of unique challenges, I also want to acknowledge the tireless work of our construction team, which enabled them to successfully bring a huge number of store and distribution projects to completion this year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These are highly complex projects across multiple geographies, which require precise coordination across a large number of regional construction providers along with a diverse group of fixture and equipment vendors, all of whom have been facing the same bottlenecks we've been facing in our merchandise supply chain.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Our construction team has handled all of these challenges with good humor and resilience, allowing us to continue reaching guests in new neighborhoods and support the growing supply chain needs of the entire chain.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In support of those growing needs, we recently announced that we're adding more than 30,000 permanent positions across our supply chain network to support the growth we expect to continue delivering in the fourth quarter and beyond.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These team members will support new buildings in our regional DC network, adding replenishment capacity to support an increasingly productive store network.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: They'll also be staffing and supporting our new sortation centers, which deliver efficiency, speed, and additional capacity in support of last mile fulfillment.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And it's amazing to pause and look back at how much our network needs have grown in a short time.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: For the entire fiscal year in 2018, our business generates $74 billion in sales.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Less than three years later, our business had already delivered $74 billion in sales through the third quarter, with the biggest quarter of the year still ahead of us.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Our team and supply chain infrastructure have done an outstanding job in supporting that growth.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And given that we don't expect it to end anytime soon, we are committed to growing our physical footprint and our team, so they can continue to deliver on behalf of all of our stakeholders in Q4 and beyond.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: When I first started working here in 1996, Target delivered just under $18 billion in revenue for what was then called Dayton Hudson Corporation.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While many things have changed since then, both in retail and at this company, we successfully maintain what's made Target's successful and unique for nearly 60 years.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We've maintained our focus on offering affordable design in support of a unique merchandise assortment, providing a differentiated and outstanding shopping experience, investing in the best team in retail, and giving back to the communities that sustain us.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: This is another example of what we call the Power of And.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: The reason Target has stayed relevant for so many decades is our ability to stay true to our values and continually evolve in the way we serve our guests.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Over time, we've emphasized our commitment to making the appropriate investments in our business, ones that will deepen Target's relationship with our guests, driving engagement which ultimately leads them to shop at Target more often.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And while it's our job to focus on driving performance every day, we've committed to making investment decisions with a long-term perspective, not limiting our horizon to a month, a season, a quarter, or even a year, but thinking about how to position Target as a leading retailer for generations.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's how I think about our third quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the face of multiple challenges in the external environment, we maintained our focus on our guests and took specific actions to ensure we have a healthy inventory position going into the holidays, even though those actions involve some incremental cost.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And importantly, as we face those decisions, we had the resources we needed including the best team in retail, a sophisticated global supply chain, and a durable model that could accommodate those guest-focused investments.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And while we're making these decisions with a focus on the long term, we've already seen the benefit of this year's inventory investments, given that they helped to power third quarter traffic and sales growth that exceeded our expectations.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In addition, given strong expense discipline across the organization, we benefited from a compelling amount of leverage on our SG&A and D&A expenses, resulting in solid EPS growth despite the sizable investments we were choosing to make.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As Brian mentioned, our 12.7% comp in the third quarter came on top of a nearly 21% increase a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As expected, within the quarter, we saw a shift in a portion of our back-to-school sales back into August, given that most schools across the country began the school year with in-person learning.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As a result, our August comp was our strongest of the quarter, our September comp dipped down to about 10%, and we accelerated back into the low-teens in October.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among the component drivers of our sales, growth continues to be driven by traffic, even as we retain nearly all of the basket growth that happened a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Specifically, third quarter traffic increased 12.9% on top of a 4.5% increase last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While average ticket declined only slightly, about 20 basis points, after growing more than 15% a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among our sales channels, stores comparable sales grew 9.7% in the quarter on top of 9.9% last year, while digital comp sales grew 29% on top of 155% growth a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Within our digital fulfillment, sales on orders shipped to home increased slightly over last year, while same-day services grew about 60% on top of a more than 200% increase a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among those same-day options, both in-store pickup and Shipt grew more than 30% in the quarter, while Drive Up grew more than 80% on top of more than 500% a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Put another way, since 2019, sales through Drive Up have expanded more than 10 times for about $1.4 billion in the third quarter alone.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Moving down the P&L, our third quarter gross margin rate of 28% was 2.6 percentage points lower than a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among the drivers, core merchandising accounted for 2 percentage points, or more than three quarters of the rate decline, driven primarily by incremental freight and other inventory costs.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among the other gross margin drivers, payroll growth in our supply chain accounted for about 70 basis points of pressure, while category sales mix contributed about 10 basis points of benefit.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Notably, digital fulfillment had an approximately neutral impact on gross margin rate in the quarter as the cost associated with higher digital volume were offset by the benefit of a shift in fulfillment mix toward our same-day options, which have meaningfully lower average unit costs compared with traditional e-commerce.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the SG&A expense line, we saw about 160 basis points of improvement in the third quarter, reflecting disciplined cost management combined with the leverage benefit of unexpectedly strong sales.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the D&A line, we saw about 20 basis points of rate improvement as sales growth more than offset the impact of higher accelerated depreciation, which reflects the continued ramp-up in our remodel program.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Altogether, our third quarter operating margin rate of 7.8% was about 70 basis points lower than a year ago but more than 2 percentage points higher than two years ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On a dollar basis, operating income was 3.9% higher than a year ago and double the number recorded in the third quarter of 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Moving to the bottom of the P&L, our third quarter GAAP EPS of $3.04 was 52% higher than last year when we recorded more than $500 million of interest expense on early debt retirement.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the adjusted EPS line, where we excluded early debt retirement expense, we earned $3.03 in the quarter, representing an 8.7% increase from a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Compared with two years ago, both GAAP and adjusted EPS have increased more than 120%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Turning now to capital deployment, I'm going to start as always with our long-term priorities.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: First, we look to fully invest in our business, and projects that meet our strategic and financial criteria.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Next, we support the dividend and look to build on our long history of annual increases, which we've maintained every year since 1971.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And finally, we return any excess cash within the limits of our middle A credit ratings through share repurchases over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the capex line, we'd invested $2.5 billion through the first three quarters of 2021 and expect to reach about $3.3 billion for the full year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As I mentioned last quarter, this is somewhat lower than our expectation going into the year and reflects a retiming of project spending into next year, given that we've experienced delays on some projects relating to external factors like permitting and inspections in some communities.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: However, as John mentioned earlier, we're eager to invest in a long list of productive growth opportunities over the next few years, adding new stores, remodeling existing stores, building replenishment capacity in our supply chain, and rolling out additional sortation centers.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As of today, we continue to believe these investments will amount to capex in the $4 billion to $5 billion range in 2022, and we'll continue to refine our view in the months ahead.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Turning now to dividends, we paid $440 million in dividends in the third quarter, up $100 million from last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This increase reflects a 32% increase in the per-share dividend, partially offset by a decline in share count.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I want to pause here and take note of the fact that with the payment of our December dividend, we'll officially achieve our 50th consecutive year of annual increases in the per-share dividend, something very few companies have achieved.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And lastly, given our cash position and strong cash generation by our operations, we continue to have ample capacity for share repurchases within the limits of our middle A ratings, even after we've made robust investments in capex and dividends.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the third quarter, we deployed $2.2 billion to repurchase 8.8 million of our shares, bringing our year-to-date total up to $4.9 billion.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As I've mentioned in prior quarters, given our continued strong financial performance, our debt leverage has been lower and cash on the balance sheet has been higher than we'd expect to maintain over the longer term.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As a result, going forward, we expect to increase our leverage and reduce our cash position at a pace that's consistent with our financial expectations, credit rating goals, and assessment of the external environment.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I've mentioned before that the timeline to move those metrics fully back to historical levels will likely be a multi-year journey.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And the rapidly changing conditions we've seen over the last two years demonstrate why it's prudent to maintain a thoughtful pace.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As always, I'll end my review of performance with our after-tax return on invested capital, which measures the quality of our current performance in the context of the investments we've made over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: For the trailing 12 months through the end of Q3, our business generated an after-tax ROIC of 31.3% compared with 19.9% a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This is incredibly robust performance and demonstrates why we are enthusiastically planning to continue investing in our business.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now, let me turn to our expectations for the fourth quarter and full year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Ninety days ago, we said we were planning for high single-digit growth in our comparable sales over the back half of the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While we still believe that's in the range of possible outcomes for the fourth quarter, we just exceeded that expectation in Q3.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As such, we're planning for a Q4 comp in the high single-digit to low double-digit range, consistent with the range we've seen over the last two quarters.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In terms of profitability, we continue to expect that our business will deliver a full year operating margin rate of 8% or higher, up significantly from 7% in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This rate favorability, combined with the full year sales growth we're positioned to deliver, would translate into another incredibly strong year of profit growth, following a record year in 2020.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So now, as I get ready to turn the call back over to Brian, I want to pause and address a question that I'm certain you'll be asking, which is, how much of the current cost pressures will turn out to be temporary and how much will turn out to be structural?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And I'll give you the honest answer, which is that it's almost certainly some of both, and no one knows the precise answer.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That said, there's no doubt that supply chain bottlenecks should ease over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: However, beyond the supply chain, we're also facing product cost increases from some vendors driven by higher costs in their businesses.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And while you heard from John that we're extremely well-positioned given our team investments over the last few years, the labor market remains very tight across the country.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So how do we think about the future.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: From a financial standpoint, we focus first on serving our guests and translating that focus into further growth, an area where we see a lot of runway.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you've seen with the investments we've made and continue to make, we're earning deeper trust and engagement from our guests.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This trust leads to more trips and broader shopping across our merchandise assortment and fulfillment services.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With a skilled and agile team focused on driving guest engagement, further growth, and market share gains, we're confident that our durable model can continue to offer compelling value for our guests, accommodate continued investments in our team, and deliver outstanding financial performance, even in the face of a challenging external environment like we're facing today.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This is one more example of the Power of And.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So now, I want to pause and thank our entire team for delivering a great Q3 which came on top of years of already strong performance.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The financial results I have the privilege of sharing quarter after quarter wouldn't be possible if Target didn't have the best team in retail.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With that, I'll turn the call back over to Brian.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Thanks, Michael.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Before we turn to your questions, I want to pick up on something Michael just mentioned, which is the growing agility of our team.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: This comes in part from a heightened focus on prioritization in which we ask our team to focus on a small list of key enterprisewide priorities with a goal of making much more rapid progress toward the goals that matter most.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: With prioritization, we've also seen more alignment across the organization.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Regardless of where specific team members might work, our enterprise priorities guide their decision-making, allowing them to take action and change course faster when facing rapidly changing external conditions.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Beyond prioritization and alignment, we've also achieved a higher degree of collaboration.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: When tackling business problems, it becomes easier for everyone to communicate and partner cross-functionally to achieve our common goals together.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Prioritization, alignment, collaboration, three important concepts that deliver compelling outcomes in a large organization like ours.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: And in our remarks today, you've heard us highlight some of those benefits which helped drive strong Q3 performance despite challenging macro conditions: a unified focus on serving our guests; collaboration between merchandising, marketing and operations teams as they optimize holiday promotions; joint efforts between our stores, supply chain, merchants, and vendors to address supply chain bottlenecks and find solutions in support of our inventory.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: To say we're feeling the impact of those benefits already this holiday season would be an understatement.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: In fact, I'd place some alongside our multi-category portfolio, our unmatched same-day services, and the skill of our extraordinary team as keys to our holiday readiness.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: So once again, I want to thank our team.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: There's no question that, because of their dedication and connection to our guest, we stand ready for an exceptionally strong holiday season.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Throughout the team, across every function, I've seen the energy and passion as they prepare for the busiest season of the year.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: And I'm confident that same energy and passion will ensure Target's consistent and sustainable growth over the longer term as well.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Now, Christina, John, Michael, and I would be happy to take your questions.

speaker: Michael Lasser
sentence: Thanks a lot for taking my question.

speaker: Michael Lasser
sentence: Michael, you began the question already by suggesting you're not sure how long the gross margin's going to last.

speaker: Michael Lasser
sentence: Can you at least help us understand if the third quarter was the peak gross margin degradation that you expect to realize over the next few quarters?

speaker: Michael Lasser
sentence: And what are you doing to mitigate this gross margin pressure in terms of passing along price increases to the consumer?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Thanks for the question, Michael.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you know, we don't guide margins specifically out into future quarters, but I will say and reiterate what I said in my remarks.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: I think you're seeing in the third quarter the result of some very specific investments we made.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And the biggest of those investments is an investment to make sure we've got a great inventory position heading into the fourth quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And pulling all the levers within the system to ensure we're there for the guests has been our priority.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And some of those levers, you know, think of expediting products come at a cost, and you saw some of that in the third quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But I feel really good about the payoff from an investment decision like that.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We've got inventory of $2 billion north of last year, up almost 20% on a year-over-year basis, and that's fueling the continued topline growth that we see.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, I feel really good about the set of investments that we're making and how they have us positioned for the back part of the year.

speaker: Michael Lasser
sentence: My follow-up question is, even without providing any context on the gross margin for at least the fourth quarter, can you give us a sense for how much you are able to offset or continue to offset this gross margin pressure with further SG&A reductions?

speaker: Michael Lasser
sentence: Should we expect your SG&A dollars in the fourth quarter to grow at a similar rate that they grew in the third quarter?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the SG&A side, I think the thing you see in Q3 is just an example of how powerful productivity improvements that come with growth are for our business.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We generate astounding leverage when the topline is running forcibly in the right direction, and it certainly was in the third quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's one of the reasons.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We want to make sure we're so well-positioned to support continued growth because the P&L works great when we're generating the SG&A leverage, just like you saw in Q3.

speaker: Michael Lasser
sentence: Thank you so much and have a good holiday.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Thanks, Michael.

sentence: Operator Thank you.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These issues continue to make it more difficult and more expensive to move inventory where we need it to be.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Our team has done a great job managing through these challenges.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And as you've seen from our recent gross margin results, our P&L has reflected those higher freight costs.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Coming into this year, we anticipated we'd see continued tight conditions and elevated costs and freight markets, but the actual conditions and costs have been much more challenging than expected.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: More specifically, first quarter freight and transportation costs came in hundreds of millions of dollars higher than our already elevated expectations.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And for the full year, we're now expecting about a billion dollars of incremental freight costs, even compared to our expectations only three months ago.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Among the reasons for this incremental pressure, record high fuel costs are a meaningful driver, as well as the global shipping market, where costs have stayed unusually high and where we sometimes need to rely on the spot market to secure adequate capacity.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Compounding these near-term pressures on our gross margin rate, volatility in both consumer demand and delivery times placed additional stress on our supply chain in Q1, one that was already running lean-on capacity in light of the growth we've seen over the last two years.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As Brian and Christina mentioned, this quarter, we ended up carrying too much inventory in several categories where the slowdown in sales was more pronounced than expected, including home electronics, sporting goods, and apparel.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, capacity pressures were compounded by the fact that in several of these categories, including kitchen appliances, furniture, and outdoor living, items are bulkier than average and require higher-than-average amounts of storage capacity.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As our team collaborated with Christina's team to work through this excess inventory, we made decisions with an eye on preserving the guest experience.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Rather than jamming store sales floors with excess product, which would have made them more difficult to shop, our team secured temporary storage capacity instead.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And as Christina mentioned, rather than carrying items beyond their relevant season, her team made the tougher call and marked items down to clear them and keep our presentations fresh and inspiring.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While these were difficult decisions in the moment, we have no doubt they're the right long-term choices.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: However, they involved higher costs, resulting directly from the actions we chose to take and indirectly in terms of team member hours required to manage the extra volume.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As Michael will discuss in more detail, while we don't expect these conditions to persist over time, they'll continue to impact our Q2 results before conditions begin improving later in the year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: More specifically, as we move beyond the front half of the year, we have had enough time to adjust inventory levels and receipt volumes to match the pace of sales even in longer lead time categories.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, capacity in our supply chain will continue to build throughout the year, as the new buildings we opened last fall continue to ramp up their productivity while we work to open additional buildings in the years ahead.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Beyond this ongoing work to expand the upstream supply chain, we continue to add downstream capacity in our sortation centers, which increased speed and reduced the unit costs of last-mile delivery.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Following our successful test of the concept in the Minneapolis market, we now have six sortation centers open and operating, with plans to open three more by the end of the year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While the newly opened centers are still ramping up their capacity, in total, our six sortation centers handled 4.5 million packages in Q1, a number that's expected to grow significantly throughout the year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Each of these facilities already has volume flowing to our national carrier partners, including the ability to sort USPS packages individually by post office, creating a high-speed, low-cost delivery option in the metro area surrounding each center.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, we've begun rolling out our lowest-cost delivery option, Target last-mile delivery, at our Atlanta sortation center and will soon expand that capability to the other four recently opened facilities.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: For this capability, we collaborate with our partners at Shipt, whose drivers sign up to deliver batches of orders that have been sorted hyper locally down to the neighborhood level.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: This provides a fast, efficient, reliable, and low-cost delivery option for our business, benefiting both our guests and the P&L. While we're excited about the results these centers are already delivering, this initiative is in the very early stages.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And we have plans to continue opening centers and ramping up this new capability for years to come.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Beyond investments in the supply chain, we're also excited about the investments we're making in our stores, allowing them to become more productive, more fun, and more inspiring to shop.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: For the year, we have plans to complete remodel projects in nearly 400 stores.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And through the first quarter, we had already mobilized on just under half of those projects, keeping us on pace for the year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Just under 200 of this year's projects will be traditional full remodels in which we transform every part of the store from wall to wall and floor to ceiling, updating the shopping experience to make it more inspiring for our guests and more efficient for our team to operate.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Beyond those full remodels, we're planning to complete just over 200 fulfillment remodels in 2022 as well.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These projects are focused on the operations of the store and their ability to support our same-day services.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: More specifically, these project make changes within the four walls of the store to add capacity for same day orders and incorporate features to enhance our pickup and drive-up capabilities.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: When warranted, these remodels include the addition of walk-in coolers and freezers near the front of the store, adding reliable capacity for our team to fulfill fresh, refrigerated, and frozen items through our pickup and drive-up services.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, with many of these projects, we add a dedicated door for our team members to use when delivering drive-up orders to the parking lot.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We're also adding canopies, more prominent signing, and more drive-up spaces in our parking lots, making the drive-up process safer and easier for both our team members and our guests.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Beyond these existing store investments, we continue to open new stores around the country.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In the first quarter, we opened seven locations, all smaller formats, in markets ranging from Jackson Hole in Wyoming to Times Square in New York.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We continue to be pleased with the performance of our new stores and their ability to flexibly serve guests in new neighborhoods.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And for our stores and markets that were temporarily affected by COVID, including college locations, tourist destinations, and dense urban areas, we've seen continued rapid recovery in sales volumes as activity ramps up in those markets following periods of lockdown over the last two years.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Similar to the pressures we've been experiencing in our merchandise costs, our construction team has been dealing with volatility in the price of raw materials and labor in our new store and remodel projects.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And like our merchandising partners, they've done a great job working around those costs and constraints, keeping projects on track while maintaining their focus on delivering a great guest experience.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: So as I get ready to hand the call over to Michael, I want to pause and thank the entire operations team from our stores to supply chain and our properties team to our partners at Shipt.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: The growth we've seen in our business and the expansion of our capabilities over the last two years has been both energizing and inspiring.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: But it certainly hasn't been easy for our team.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: They've handled growth well beyond what any of us would have expected two years ago, even as they worked around new challenges and unexpected obstacles.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: One of the joys of the last year has been the ability for me to once again get out in the field, traveling to our stores and distribution facilities around the country, and experiencing firsthand the energy and positive attitude our team brings to work.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: They're united in their support of our guests for our brand and for each other.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Every day, they bring our company purpose to life.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And every day, I am inspired by what they accomplish.

sentence: Even with all of the challenges they've been facing, they refused to get distracted.

sentence: Our team shows up to work every day with a passion for serving all families and for serving each other.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among our fulfillment channels, store sales grew slightly faster than digital in the quarter.

sentence: Within digital, same-day services continued to drive our growth and accounted for well over half of our first quarter digital sales.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In fact, of the $3.3 billion in first quarter digital sales that we've added since 2019, Drive Up accounts for nearly half of that growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the first quarter gross margin line, we saw a rate decline of about 4.3 percentage points compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among the causal factors, merchandising actions drove about three percentage points of the decline, driven by the combined impact of impairments, markdowns, and other actions taken to rightsize our inventory position in categories that were too heavy, along with the impact of higher freight costs.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Among other drivers, higher supply chain costs accounted for a little over one percentage point of this year's rate decline, reflecting the impact of higher headcount and compensation in our distribution centers.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Sales mix accounted for the remainder of the decline, worth about 10 basis points of pressure.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the SG&A expense line, we benefited from fixed cost leverage and strong expense control throughout the quarter, which helped to offset the impact of inflation-driven cost increases in multiple expense lines.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Within compensation, the continued impact of team investments was offset by lower incentive compensation compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the DNA expense line, we saw about 10 basis points of benefit in Q1, reflecting leverage on strong revenue growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Altogether, our first quarter operating margin rate of 5.3% was about 4.5 percentage points lower than last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While we expected this year's rate would be well below last year, our actual performance in the quarter was far lower than we anticipated, driven by the unexpectedly high costs we incurred on the gross margin line.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Turning now to capital deployment, I'll start where I always do, by reiterating our priorities, which have remained consistent for decades.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: First, we fully invest in our business and projects that support our strategic and financial criteria.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Second, we support the dividend and look to build on our 50-year record of annual dividend growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And finally, we return any remaining excess cash within the limits of our middle A credit ratings through share repurchases over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Beginning with the top priority, first quarter capex was just under $1 billion, keeping us on track to spend $4 billion to $5 billion for the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While our teams continue to face multiple challenges, including supply shortages, shipping delays, and permitting and inspection delays in some communities, they're doing a great job of working around these obstacles and keeping projects moving.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In addition, as John mentioned, unexpected inflationary pressures are affecting some of our capital projects, which will impact our total spending for the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As I mentioned at our recent financial community meeting, we're excited to make progress on our capital projects, which continue to move our business forward.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And today, given the team's efforts to advance this year's projects, I believe we'll reach the high end of our $4 billion to $5 billion plan for the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Moving to our second priority, we paid dividends of $424 million in the first quarter, up about 25% from last year, reflecting a 32% increase in the per-share dividend, partially offset by a decline in share count.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We plan to recommend that our board approve a healthy increase in the quarterly dividend in the mid-teens to low-20% range later this year, keeping 2022 on track to be our 51st consecutive year of annual dividend increases.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And finally, regarding share repurchases, given our strong leverage metrics coming into the year, we entered into an accelerated repurchase plan in the first quarter, which will result in the retirement of up to $2.75 billion of our stock by the time the plan settles in June.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In addition to this ASR, we repurchased another $10 million in shares in the first quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While we anticipate having continued ample capacity to return capital through share repurchases this year, given the current supply chain challenges we're facing and their impact on working capital, we now expect our total repurchases this year will be lower than the $7 billion we returned in 2021.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As always, we'll adjust our pace, up or down, based on external conditions, business performance and cash flow with a goal of maintaining our middle A credit ratings.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, now I want to turn to our after-tax return on invested capital, which measures both our profitability and the efficiency of our capex decisions over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the first quarter, we reported a trailing 12-month after-tax ROIC of 25.3%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While this is a very strong number indicative of the underlying health of our business, it was much lower than expected, near the very low end of where we expect to operate over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now, let's turn to our guidance.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In terms of the top line, based on our first quarter results and the trends we've seen so far in May, we continue to expect full year revenue growth in the low- to mid-single-digit range.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In terms of our profitability, given the unexpected cost headwinds that we're currently facing, we now believe our full year operating margin rate will be well below our prior guidance of 8% or higher.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: More specifically, given the elevated level of volatility we're currently facing and multiple sources of uncertainty going forward, we see a range of potential outcomes centered around a 6% operating margin rate for the full year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As John mentioned, in the second quarter, we expect the challenges we faced in the first quarter will continue to impact our near-term profit performance.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And our team is focused on doing everything necessary to ensure we enter the fall season with an appropriate level of inventory by category.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As such, we expect a Q2 operating margin rate in a wide range, centered around our first quarter rate of 5.3%, well below where we would expect to operate under normal conditions.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As we move into the back half of the year, we continue to expect our profit performance will begin to improve.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In particular, as John mentioned, we expect to have worked through the excess inventory positions that hampered our Q1 performance and which we expect to impact our gross margin in Q2.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That said, we don't expect the external environment will be anything close to normal in the back half of the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In particular, we don't expect to see any meaningful reduction in global supply chain pressures until 2023 at the earliest, so the elevated costs we've been facing will continue to affect our profitability for the remainder of the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But let me be clear about a couple of things.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: First, we are not happy with our current profit performance, and our team is laser-focused on helping to quickly restore our business performance to where it should be operating over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That said, nothing that is happening today has changed our long-run expectations regarding the ability of our business to grow, nor has it changed our view of the long-run potential of our business to deliver an operating margin rate of 8% or higher over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And today, as we navigate these near-term challenges, we are fortunate to have an incredibly healthy underlying business, one that can stand up to the significant headwinds we're facing and come out stronger on the other side.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We have ample financial capacity to continue making long-term investments in new stores, remodels, supply chain and, of course, in our team, all with a focus on serving and delighting our guests, driving deeper loyalty, and building on the top-line growth we've seen in recent years and which continues today.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: After all, even after a significant pullback from last year, first quarter earnings per share were more than 40% higher than in the first quarter of 2019, prior to the beginning of the pandemic.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Well, that doesn't mean we're where we want to be operating today.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It shows we have a strong foundation from which we can recover from today's challenging environment and restore our operating margins to 8% or higher over time, consistent with our long-term financial algorithm.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And given the loyalty and momentum we've established with our guests and the power of the investments we continue to make, we expect to continue growing the top-line, even as we regain the level of profitability we expect our business will generate over time.

sentence: Now, I'll turn it back over to Brian for some closing remarks.

speaker: Brian Cornell

sentence: Back in June, we announced that our team would be undertaking a bold effort to right size our inventory position in the categories for which demand patterns have radically changed.

speaker: Brian Cornell

sentence: It would have cluttered our sales force and hampered our ability to present new, fresh, and fashionable items, the ones our guests expect from Target.

sentence: Just as importantly, the extra inventory would have presented an ongoing burden to our supply chain and store teams as they face the distraction of working around it day after day.

speaker: Brian Cornell
sentence: Instead of taking that path of position, our team chose a more decisive path, aggressively reducing the inventory we already owned and cutting back on receipts for the back half of the year.

sentence: And throughout the execution of these action plans, our teams remained steadfast in their guest-first focus, refusing to compromise the shopping experience in our stores or online.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: As you heard from Brian, the short term profit implications of these decisions were meaningful.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: But we're confident they're the right long-term decisions for our business, for our teams, and for our guests.

sentence: As we formed and revisited our plans for the third quarter and beyond, we spent a lot of time listening to the wants, needs, hopes, and concerns of our guests.

sentence: Now, let me turn to some of the category highlights from the second quarter in which overall comparable sales grew 2.6% on top of 8.9% a year ago, reflecting continued strength in food and beverage, beauty, and household essentials.

sentence: Essentials grew in the mid single digits with performance led by pets and healthcare.

sentence: Overall across our discretionary categories, sales were softer than a year ago but remain nearly $3.5 billion or more than 35% higher than the second quarter of 2019.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: Within hardline, softness in electronics was partially offset by strength in entertainment, which grew in the high single digits, along with high-single-digit comp growth in toys, an encouraging sign as we plan for the fourth quarter holiday season.

sentence: Overall, the home category saw a low-single-digit decline compared to last year, despite affinity for our seasonal assortments and encouraging early results in back-to-school and back-to-college.

sentence: As I mentioned earlier, while overall sales growth is one key indicator of the health of our business, market share is an equally important measure that we use to understand how we're performing.

sentence: And notably, during inflationary times like these, we heavily focus on unit share specifically to better understand our relevance as compared to our competitive set, given that growth in both traffic and units is a strong proxy for the guests' overall engagement with Target.

sentence: Time and time again, these metrics have proven to be a better barometer for lasting success as compared to growth solely through average retail prices.

speaker: Christina Hennington
sentence: That's why I'm so encouraged that across all five of our core merchandising categories, we grew unit share in the second quarter.

sentence: So, now let's turn our sights to all that is to come for the balance of the fiscal year.

sentence: Having celebrated holidays in a big way in the second quarter, guests already have their sights set on upcoming holidays and seasonal moments in Q3 and beyond.

sentence: Our guest research indicates that more families plan to participate in Halloween festivities compared with last year, and we're ready with a wide array of gender- and size-inclusive costumes, new owned brand trick or treating candy and accessories, haunted house cookie building sets, and so much more.

sentence: And for those that want to celebrate the broader fall and harvest season in general, rest assured that there will be no shortage of new offerings from Good & Gather to create perfect meal snacking and entertaining solutions, including delicious new flavors of the season like maple, cinnamon, apple, and, of course, all things pumpkin spice.

sentence: So, now, before I pass things over to John, I'd like to take a moment and echo Brian's gratitude for the team.
