speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Thanks, Christina.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In past calls, I described how our operations team is always focused on two things at the same time.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Of course, they're always focused on short-term execution and problem solving to ensure we provide a convenient, consistent, and inspiring experience for our guests.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, our team works every day to deliver on our long-term vision and aspirations, ensuring our operations are ready to support our future plans.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While this dual focus on both near-term and long-term priorities has always been present, it's been especially notable this year, given that we've been operating in a very unique environment.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In terms of the short term, and as Brian and Christina mentioned earlier, our work to quickly rightsize inventory required determination, commitment, and coordination between multiple teams across the company.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And given the need to protect the guest experience, there was no higher priority than delivering against this near-term plan.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: At the same time, our team remains passionately focused on the long-term investments we're making in our future.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These investments include our work to modernize and expand our store footprint, increase upstream capacity in our supply chain, automate distribution center processes to reduce store workload, and enhance our last-mile fulfillment capabilities by opening sortation centers and integrating them into our Shipt network.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And fortunately, as Brian highlighted, the strength of our business allows us to continue funding these long-term investments, even in the face of the challenging external backdrop we're facing today.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: I want to first turn to our work on inventory.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And I'm happy to report that our team has made remarkable progress over the last few months, causing conditions in our supply chain to improve significantly.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: More specifically and to provide some helpful context, over time, we want to keep our DC network operating at or below 85% of its maximum capacity, given that operational difficulties and costs rise significantly when we move beyond that level.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: So, it's important to note that back in June, inventory in our DC network peaked at well over 90% of our capacity.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Also notable, by the end of the second quarter, less than two months later, our team had quickly reduced DC capacity utilization to below 80%.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Put another way, by the end of the second quarter, the physical space occupied by our distribution center inventory was more than 20% lower than the peak we reached in June.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: So, today, while we still have some individual sites where we need to make more progress, the team has accomplished a remarkable improvement in a very short time, which will allow our end-to-end operations to function more efficiently and effectively in the back half of the year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As Christina mentioned, beyond addressing the inventory we already owned, the team also took a hard look at sales trends and determined ideal inventory levels across every category for the remainder of the year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As a result, we've meaningfully reduced our fall season receipt commitments in many discretionary categories.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: With these reductions, we're projecting our DCs will remain at or below 85% capacity through the remainder of the year, even after the seasonal increase in holiday inventory is set to occur over the next two months.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In other words, for the first time I'm aware of, our fall season inventory is projected to peak at a lower level than in spring, providing another vivid illustration of the unique dynamics we've encountered so far this year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While this inventory rightsizing process hasn't been easy and our teams have devoted an amazing amount of effort in a small amount of time, this work has allowed our teams to strengthen ongoing communication mechanisms and build new processes.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Going forward, these improvements will enable our merchandising and supply chain teams to maintain enhanced real-time communication, particularly with respect to categories where we face the highest inventory risk, allowing us to respond to changes with more speed and agility.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While pressure from excess inventory has presented the biggest challenge to our team this year, dealing with high costs and volatility in the external supply chain has run a close second.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And today, while conditions remain far from what we would have considered normal in the years before the pandemic, there are early signs that both costs and volatility may have peaked.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: More specifically, lead times in global shipping have begun to decline.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Spot rates to move shipping containers have fallen somewhat.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And in light of the reduction in petroleum prices we've all seen recently, fuel surcharges have been easing somewhat compared with the peak rates we saw earlier in the second quarter.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: That said, conditions remain highly unfavorable when compared to the years before the pandemic.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And we're mindful of the continued risks in the months ahead, including potential slowdowns at the West Coast ports, a reversal of the recent decline in energy costs, and the possibility of additional COVID lockdowns in China.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, we continue to encounter far too many delays affecting overseas shipping, which require us to pay spot rates to move containers, rates that are well above our pre-negotiated shipping rates.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As such, we're maintaining our practice of moving receipt dates earlier than we would have in the past, which allows us to mitigate the business risk from receiving shipments later than expected.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: You'll recall that at this time a year ago, when the external supply chain began slowing down and shipments were arriving late, we began relying on airfreight much more than usual to ensure we received key seasonal merchandise on time for the holiday season.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Well, that was the right decision at the time, given the circumstances we were facing.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: This year, we expect to meaningfully reduce our reliance on airfreight by moving to early receipt dates for seasonal inventory.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: To accommodate these early receipts without adding further color to our supply chain and stores, we secured temporary capacity to store and stage shipping containers near the ports where we receive them.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: When needed, this allows us to quickly clear the containers from the port area and hold them until the ideal time to begin moving inventory into our supply chain network.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Well, we don't expect to need this additional capacity over the long term, we believe it's clearly the most efficient approach in today's environment, given the volatility we continue to face.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: I also want to highlight the critical role that our stores have played in our work to improve conditions in our supply chain.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: During the second quarter, our store teams engaged in a host of activities to support the effort, including the execution of countless promotions and markdown programs to move the excess merchandise quickly and the development of innovative presentation strategies to highlight the deals we were offering our guests.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: This included repurposing the seasonal presentation space in our stores to highlight deals and create meaningful statements, including key item promotions.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: It also included the early wind down of our outdoor living assortment, which allowed us to bring in our back-to-school set earlier than usual, ensuring we were back in stock and reliable on key items parents needed to fill their back-to-school shopping lists.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: More specifically, at the end of the second quarter, about three quarters of our back-to-school and back-to-college receipts were already downstream in our stores, a number that was closer to 50% at the end of Q2 a year ago.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: So, now, before I turn the call over to Michael, I want to turn my focus to our longer-term priorities and the multiple ways we're investing in our future growth.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As you know, the majority of our capex is going into our store network, both to extend our footprint and invest in existing locations.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These store investments fall into three major buckets.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: The first and largest investment is in our store remodel program, where we completely transform the space in the existing location, modernizing the shopping experience while enhancing the productivity of our team.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: At this point in the year, well over 100 remodels are currently in flight across the country, keeping us on track to complete nearly 200 remodels this year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition to these complete transformations, we're also making smaller investments in hundreds of other locations.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: This includes the hundreds of fulfillment remodels we'll accomplish this year in which we reconfigure portions of the store to enhance the efficiency, safety, and capacity of our drive-up, in-store pickup, and Shipt from store services.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition, this year we're investing in several hundred locations to add an Ulta Beauty at Target, a co-branded Apple shopping space, or a Disney store presentation to the sales floor.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And finally, we're on track at add about 24 new store locations in 2022.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: So far, this year, we've opened 12 new locations across the country in neighborhoods as diverse as SoHo in New York and Jackson Hole in Wyoming.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Beyond this work in stores, we're also making significant investments in our supply chain focused on three main priorities.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: The first is to build additional upstream capacity to our network, given that we continue to grow sales on top of the $27 billion we added in 2020 and 2021.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In support of this goal, we opened two upstream DCs near the end of 2021 and plan to open six new upstream facilities over the next several years, including two on track to open in 2023.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In addition to the space we're adding to the network, we're continuing to modernize how our existing distribution centers serve our stores by developing and automating processes that reduce the amount of store workload in order to receiving inventory and restocking store sales floors.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And finally, we're rapidly expanding the number of sortation centers operating around the country.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: We have six of these facilities operating today, including three that have opened in the last few months.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And we have plans to add five more by early next year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: These small facilities expand Shipt and storage capacity in the locations they serve, while significantly reducing last-mile delivery costs, particularly as we integrate our Shipt drivers into the process.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: Given the package delivery density we've achieved across many markets over the last few years, we see continued opportunities to add more sortation centers over the next few years, which add speed and significantly reduced last-mile costs in markets where they operate.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: As I mentioned last quarter, this year's capital projects are being impacted by the cost increases, material shortages, and supply chain pressures that are affecting other parts of our business.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And I'm really proud of how our construction team is managing through these headwinds.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: More specifically, while cost increases are raising the cost of many of these projects, the team has done an excellent job in keeping the vast majority of projects on track and on time, despite the significant headwinds they are facing.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: So, as I conclude my remarks, I have to pause and add my thanks to the entire team for their resilience and perseverance during a period of incredibly rapid change, which caused this quarter to be as challenging as any I've seen in my career.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: In the face of that challenge, what's been amazing is how our team members have stayed positive, how they've worked to find collaborative solutions across multiple teams and never strayed from their commitment to our guests and our company purpose.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: With the progress they've made, our operations are now in much better shape.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: And the team is energized and ready to play offense in the back half of the year.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: While we are all mindful of the near-term volatility in the environment, it's times like these that often present the biggest opportunity to gain long-term market share, as others face the distraction of trying to stay afloat while we continue to invest and improve our operations.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: That's one of many reasons that I've never been more optimistic about our prospects in the years ahead.

speaker: John Mulligan
sentence: With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As John mentioned, we often ask our team to be mindful of both short-term and long-term considerations when making decisions.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And given the unique circumstances we've been facing, this quarter, we faced a decision with meaningful implications for both.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As Brian outlined earlier, if we had decided not to deal with our excess inventory head on, we could have avoided some short-term pain on the profit line, but that would have hampered our longer-term potential.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Instead, because of the path we took, our quarterly profit took a meaningful step-down.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: But our future path is brighter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our operations are healthy, our store in DC teams have more flexibility to maneuver, and we're ready to feature both the fresh assortment and uncluttered shopping experience our guests expect and deserve.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That passionate commitment to the guest experience is one of the many reasons we've now seen 21 consecutive quarters of comparable sales growth.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While normally our income statement gets the most attention, I want to start my remarks today with the balance sheet and specifically our inventory position.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And as I dig into the detail, I want to acknowledge upfront that this kind of analysis is a relatively complex exercise because of the growth and volatility we've experienced over the last couple of years, because of the broad and diverse assortment that we sell, and the fact that our business is seasonal from quarter to quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: More specifically, given that our inventory position throughout the pandemic was far from optimal, focusing on year-over-year growth numbers isn't very helpful right now.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As a result, we often base our inventory analysis on growth trends compared with 2019, a pre-pandemic year when our inventory and sales trends were much more in sync.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With that as context, I want to zero in on one of the questions I'm sure you have, which is why our inventory on the balance sheet remained roughly constant at around $15 billion between the first and second quarters.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The simple answer is that while that single number didn't change much, we accomplished exactly what we intended to do during the quarter, which helped changed conditions significantly below the surface.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: More specifically, because of the inventory actions we executed, unit growth compared with 2019 in our discretionary categories decelerated by more than 15 percentage points between the first and second quarter, a change we estimate would have reduced our inventory position by more than $1 billion if taken in isolation.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: However, a couple of offsetting changes moved our quarter-end inventory in the other direction.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: First among them, we leaned into our frequency categories during the quarter, accelerating three year unit growth versus Q1 at a double-digit rate, resulting in stronger in-stock metrics compared with 90 days ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Another factor that drove inventory dollars higher is the continued increase in unit costs we've been seeing across all of our categories, which caused the dollar value of our inventory to grow faster than unit growth in the second quarter.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, where do we stand today?

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: At the end of the second quarter, inventory on the balance sheet was about $6 billion higher than we reported three years ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Of that dollar growth, about $3 billion or approximately half of that total growth is the result of higher unit costs across our assortment.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Of the remaining $3 billion, our analysis indicates another $1 billion to $2 billion is related to our decision to move receipt timing earlier, given the volatility we continue to expect in the supply chain.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And also importantly, beyond reshaping the inventory we already have, our Q2 inventory actions also included the removal of more than $1.5 billion of fall receipts in our discretionary categories, reflecting our continued focus on reducing risk in the current environment.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's why we feel good about our inventory position as we head into the back half of the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, now I'll turn to a review of our second quarter financial results.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Total sales increased 3.3% in the quarter, driven by a 2.6% increase in comparable sales combined with the impact of new stores.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Total revenue increased 3.5%, reflecting sales growth along with the benefit of nearly 15% growth on the other revenue line, driven by continued strength in our Roundel ad business.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Just as Christina pointed out that unit share is a key measure of Target's relevance versus competitors, traffic growth is another important indicator of the relevance of our brand.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our continued traffic growth in the second quarter clearly demonstrates the ability of our balanced multi-category assortment to deliver continued relevance in a rapidly changing environment like we're seeing today.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, that even as our guests preference for individual categories has been changing dramatically so far this year, that hasn't affected their preference for Target.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As a result, traffic accounted for 100% of our comparable sales growth in the second quarter, increasing 2.7% on top of 12.7% a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Average ticket remained essentially flat in the quarter as low-single-digit increase in average retail was offset by a similar reduction in the number of items per transaction.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Across our sales channels, store comps grew 1.3% on top of 8.7%, a year ago while digital comps grew 9% on top of 9.9% last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Digital growth continues to be led by our same-day services, which saw double-digit growth overall and mid-teens growth in drive-up.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the gross margin line, we saw a nearly nine percentage point decline compared with last year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Merchandising accounted for more than seven points of this pressure, driven primarily by our inventory reduction efforts along with the impact of higher fuel and transportation costs, product cost increases, and higher shrink, partially offset by the benefit of retail price increases.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In addition, digital fulfillment and supply chain drove about 1.5 points of pressure, reflecting increased compensation and headcount in our distribution centers combined with the cost of managing excess inventory and higher last mile shipping costs.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Consistent with the first quarter, mix accounted for approximately 10 basis points of pressure.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: The softness in higher-margin categories like apparel and home was largely offset by softness in lower-margin discretionary categories, most notably electronics.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the SG&A line, we continue to benefit from fixed cost leverage and efficiency gains across our operations, which helped to offset the impact of cost inflation across multiple expense lines.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Within overall compensation, lower incentive compensation more than offset continued investments in pay and benefits for our hourly team members.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Altogether, our second quarter operating margin rate was 1.2%, down from an unusually high 9.8% a year ago, driven entirely by the decline in our gross margin rate.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This operating margin performance was below the midpoint of our most recent guidance as the cost of our inventory actions was somewhat higher than expected.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: While an operating margin rate of just over 1% is well below anything I've seen in my career and something I never expect to see again, I have no doubt that it was the right outcome given the unusual circumstances we've been facing this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our focus throughout the second quarter was to ensure that we took care of the excess inventory of our network and adjust future receipts to reflect the rapid change in sales trends we've seen so far this year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: We accomplished this goal to the benefit of our operations, our team, and our guests.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Finally, one note on our tax rate.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In a period like this year when our operating profit is unusually low, tax benefits have a larger-than-normal impact on our tax rate, which helps to explain why our year-to-date tax rate has been lower than expected.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Looking forward, given that we anticipate a meaningful improvement in our operating performance in the back half of the year, we continue to expect our full year effective tax rate will be in a range around 21%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now, I'm going to turn to capital deployment and begin where I always do by articulating our priorities which we've supported consistently for decades.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Our first priority is always to invest fully in our business in projects that support our strategic and financial criteria.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Once we've met this first priority, we support our dividend and look to extend our 50-year record of annual increases.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And finally, once we've supported the first two priorities, we return any remaining excess cash by repurchasing our shares over time within the limits of our middle A credit ratings.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Regarding the first priority, second quarter capex was approximately $1.5 billion, bringing our year-to-date total to just over $2.5 billion.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As you'll recall at the beginning of the year, we guided to an expected full year capex range of $4 billion to $5 billion.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, I'm happy that, as John mentioned, the team is doing a great job of keeping projects on track despite facing multiple headwinds, all while inflation in the cost of equipment materials and labor is driving project spending above initial projections.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: As such, we now expect our full year capex will be $5 billion or more for the year, reflecting both the number of projects that remain on track and the expected impact of cost inflation.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Of course, while we prefer not to face the cost pressure on these projects, I'm encouraged that so many value-creating projects remain on track to be completed this year, projects that will benefit our operations and our P&L for years to come.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Turning to our second capital deployment priority, we returned $417 million in dividends to our shareholders in the second quarter, up from $336 million a year ago, driven by a 32% increase in the per share dividend, partially offset by a decline in average share count.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And finally, in June, we reached the final settlement for the accelerated share repurchase agreement we initiated last March.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Under this ASR, we invested $2.6 billion to retire 12.5 million shares of our stock.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Looking forward, just as our inventory commitments reflect continued caution for the remainder of the year, we're taking a similar cautious stance in terms of our share repurchase activity.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And of course, any repurchase activity will be consistent with our long-term goal to maintain our middle A credit ratings.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, now, I want to close my commentary on the quarter by covering our after-tax return on invested capital, which measures both our near-term profitability and the efficiency of our capex decisions over time.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In the second quarter, our trailing 12-month after-tax ROIC was 18.4% compared with 31.7% a year ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And it's notable, while the current number is well below where we expect to operate over time, an after-tax number in the high teens would have been considered aspirational for our business only a few years ago.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, for us, to temporarily move down to this level in an environment as challenging as we're facing is a vivid confirmation of the underlying strength and resilience of our business model and the reason we continue to be incredibly optimistic about our future prospects.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And that confidence starts and ends with our team.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, I want to pause and express my gratitude to the best team in retail.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Without your efforts, we couldn't have achieved the remarkable growth in traffic and sales that we've seen over the last few years and why even in a tough year our business remained strong.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Now, let's turn to our guidance.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And based on the hard work of our team in the second quarter, we feel really good about how we're positioned going into the back half of the year.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: At the same time, given that we've been experiencing volatile economic conditions so far this year and that volatility appears likely to continue in the months ahead, we're maintaining a cautious stance as we plan our business given the potential macro and consumer risks that might emerge.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's why, as you've heard throughout our remarks today, our second quarter inventory actions were specifically designed to reduce our level of risk in discretionary categories.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And in terms of our operations, the team has focused on building flexibility into our plans, placing a premium on staying nimble and adjusting quickly in the face of any potential change in macro trends.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Regarding the top line, our expectations have remained consistent so far this year with guidance for full year total revenue growth in the low- to mid-single-digit range.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With the front half of the year behind us, both our Q1 and Q2 results have put us squarely in the middle of that range.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And today, based on our current performance and plans for the back half of the year, we remain positioned to deliver full year revenue growth in the low- to mid-single-digit range.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: On the operating margin line, our most recent guidance anticipated a fall season operating margin rate and a range centered around 6%.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: This expectation is nearly double our spring result.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And notably, if we hit that rate in the fall, it would exceed the fall season rates we were delivering prior to the pandemic.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And today, similar to my commentary on the top line, based on the success of our Q2 inventory actions and our current performance, we remain positioned to deliver an operating margin rate in a range around 6% in the fall season.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Between the last two quarters of the year, we expect our third quarter rate will be well below our Q3 performance over the last couple of years, while our fourth quarter rate should be much more in line with our recent Q4 experience.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Most notably, in the third quarter, we'll continue to experience some spillover impact from our inventory actions in the range of $200 million.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In contrast, in Q4, we'll be annualizing meaningful cost headwinds that surfaced a year ago, which will make the year-over-year comparison more favorable, despite the current headwinds we're facing.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: All that said, while we typically anticipate something closer to a balance of upside and downside potential when we make any forecast, the macro and consumer risks in the back half of this year feel skewed to the downside.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's why, even in the face of consistent business trends in recent months, we've undertaken the significant cost and effort to remove risk from our inventory commitments.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: It's why we're stubbornly focused on real-time monitoring and communication of evolving conditions and why we've asked our team to build flexibility and agility into their plans.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With that mindset if trends move away from what we're seeing today, we're ready to quickly adjust.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: So, now, before, I turn the call back over to Brian, I want to emphasize why we're so confident in our long-term potential.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: Even as we navigate a very challenging environment in a year of multiple challenges, including rapidly changing consumer preferences inflation at four-year highs, volatile supply chain conditions, and rising fuel and transportation rates that are expected to add well over $1 billion of cost this year, our business continues to generate historically strong traffic increases, low to mid-single digit revenue growth, and unit share gains across all of our core merchandising categories.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And even in the face of unprecedented profit rate pressure driven by the host of factors I just listed, we remain profitable with an after-tax ROIC in the mid-teens.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: In fact, if our performance in the fall is consistent with the revenue growth and operating margin rates I outlined earlier, we remain positioned in 2022 to generate higher operating margin dollars than we did in 2019.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's what we mean when we say we have built a durable model.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: And today, while we expect conditions to remain challenging in the near term, the operating margin rate improvement we're projecting in the back half of the year should serve as an early indicator of the continued rate improvement we should deliver in the years ahead.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: With the potential for additional rate expansion and continued growth in traffic and revenue in the years ahead, we're facing a compelling financial picture as the economy and consumer eventually recover.

speaker: Michael Fiddelke
sentence: That's why I've never been more confident in our long-term prospects than I am today.

sentence: To continue driving affordability in areas of greatest need, we are announcing today an important initiative from UnitedHealthcare supported by Optum Rx.

sentence: While this is an important step for vulnerable people's health, the larger and longer term cost containment of drugs depends upon manufacturers restraining and lowering the list price of their products, which is a fundamental driver of costs.

speaker: Andrew Witty
sentence: We will continue to use our capabilities to do everything we can to lower out-of-pocket costs for consumers, building on past actions, including point-of-sale discounts.
